title: Land the October 10 LNVPS HTTP ordering decision
description: Record the accepted 2026-10-10 decision: stage 1 orders LNVPS machines over HTTP after the operator verifies the same personal email address separately for each per-machine vendor identity. Amend ADR-0042 and the owning requirements STG-21, ARC-30, CNF-104, TRU-E1, OPN-24 and OPN-26; remove the unshipped TRU-E13 and synchronize T39, T43 and T44. Preserve the phase-A finding, separate jump qualification, all remaining invoice cases, and the pending credential-format and recovery work. title: STA-24: cases the disposition decisions leave open
description:
The amendment of 2026-10-13 (ADR-0044) wrote the disposition rule into `STA-24` and `STA-20b` in the decisions' own words. These cases are not answered by those words. Each is recorded here so that it is decided by its owner and not by an implementation; none is a rule until decided.

1. **A harness job the model requests by name.** `STA-24` refuses "the model's box-plane commands to that machine" under a destructive continuation. `ARC-43` says `fetch_artifact` and `ready_to_reset` "run under the box-plane scope like any `exec`", and `place_secret` is box-plane work too. Whether a job the model requests through `request_harness_job` is one of the model's commands is not said. The companion's `exec` stands for box-plane work as a whole.
2. **A further disposition that names only the unresolved rescue activation.** `STA-24`: "One disposition stands per resource, the latest". If the rescue activation of a standing reinstall goes unresolved and the operator disposes of it alone with a continuing choice, that disposition replaces the reinstall one, and the box-plane stop the disposed reset carried is gone. This follows from the words; whether it is wanted is the owner's to confirm.
3. **A call disposed by a disposition since replaced** can never be named again: `STA-24` lets a replacement name only "the calls the standing one disposed".
4. **Where `STG-20`'s installation boundary falls** relative to the disposition and the reset into rescue, and so when the installed pin retires. `STA-24` keeps the pinned SSH attempt permitted while a destructive disposition stands, which needs a pin.
5. **A continuing choice with a pin already recorded.** `STA-20b` makes keeping the current rescue boot and running the install again "continuing as if not done"; `CHN-R7` lets no installed-system pin replace an active one without a reinstall. An install that regenerates host keys then cannot be pinned.
6. **The rescue activation that counts.** The companion reads `STA-24`'s "after that rescue activation is confirmed" as an activation dispatched after the standing disposition was recorded, confirmed, with no reset after it. An activation confirmed before the disposition with no reset since, and one dispatched under a disposition since replaced, do not count, and a new activation is admitted. Narrow by intent; confirm or widen.
7. **Untyped scopes.** A destructive disposition on a scope that is not a vendor's; the hold across a re-approved scope, a rotated token or a grown bound set; and how a reinstall or an abandonment is carried out by hand (already `TASKS.md` T47).
8. **`docs/briefs/01-install.md`** tells a model in rescue to read the Resume section before wiping and to preserve existing host keys. After a reinstall's fresh rescue boot that steers it to continue the install the operator chose to discard.
close_reason: Settled decisions implemented in requirements, formal companion, witness files, controls and conformance records

comments.author: user
comments.text: Decided by the owner 2026-10-13: a harness-owned job the model requests by name is one of the model's box-plane commands under the destructive stop; STA-24 and CNF-110 now say so. The owner also left these as they are: STG-20's installation boundary (a disposition does not move it), and non-vendor scopes with the hold across a re-approved scope or rotated token (T47). The other items here stay open.

comments.author: user
comments.text: Open case from review of the pull request (2026-10-14): a rescue activation spent by a reboot the harness did not request. STA-24 counts a rescue activation dispatched after the standing disposition, confirmed, with no reset intent after it; TauWeb.Dispatch.rescueConfirmed ignores observations. Trace: reinstall disposition, activation confirmed, an unexpected reboot observed (the activation is used by that boot), then a reset: it counts as the reset into rescue and ends the restriction, though with the activation spent it boots the installed system. Contact with that system is still stopped by the pin (the rescue pin does not match), so no command lands; the gap is that the reset is treated as the continuation. To decide: whether an observed reboot (a reset predicate reporting ended or succeeded, not any read of it) spends the activation, in STA-24's sentence and in rescueConfirmed. Dedicated path only; LNVPS has one reinstall call.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
Decided: the spent-activation case. STA-24 now says "the reset into rescue is a reset dispatched after that rescue activation is confirmed and while the newest read of that activation still confirms it". TauWeb.Dispatch.spent_activation_not_counted carries the refusal after a non-confirming newest activation read, the activation call remaining terminal, and the later admitted reset after a fresh activation confirmed. STG-4 owns the immediate re-read and durable journal duty for this disposition's reset.

New open case: the ordinary install ceremony's own reset into rescue, with no disposition, has the same window. A reboot nobody requested spends the activation, and the reset then boots the installed system. Nothing refuses that reset before dispatch. Its harm is bounded by the pin check: if /rescue/last still holds the pre-reset snapshot's keys, the reset-into-rescue predicate never holds, its barrier stands, and the operator disposes. If the unrequested boot publishes fresh disjoint keys after that snapshot but before the harness's reset lands, those keys can satisfy the predicate; the pinned SSH attempt remains the bound. This window is not closed. The ordinary ceremony and its conformance cases are unchanged; this issue stays open with its other undecided cases.

comments.author: Allan Douglas
comments.text: Settled cases implemented 2026-10-16. Case 1: decided 2026-10-13, already in STA-24 / CNF-110; Dispatch exec and stops include requested harness jobs. Case 2: STA-24 and CNF-110 give the replacement display, cancellation and retry-the-activation/keep-the-reinstall offer; standingIn and permits retain the latest-disposition rule. Case 3: STA-24 / CNF-110 list omitted calls, settled unknown and never named again; TauWeb.Dispatch.omitted_call_stays_settled carries it. Case 4: the 2026-10-13 ruling plus dispatch now define STG-20 boundary timing; Dispatch.installationOf and dedicated_reset_retires_prerequisites derive it, Pins.dedicated_reinstall_admitted puts reinstall at the rescue reset; CNF-80 is corrected and CNF-86 checks choice replaced before dispatch. Case 5: STA-20b keeps the matching root and withholds the reset on changed keys or predecessor prerequisites; Dispatch predecessor_reset_offer_refused / predecessor_reset_offer_admitted_without_guard and changed_keys_reset_offer_refused / changed_keys_reset_offer_admitted_without_guard, with CNF-86 and brief 01-install. Case 6: STA-24 counts only activations dispatched under the standing choice; rescueConfirmed and activation_before_disposition_not_counted / activation_under_replaced_disposition_not_counted already carry it; CNF-110 adds the still-armed second-activation refusal. Case 7 stays TASKS T47, unchanged. Case 8: STG-20 / ARC-7 show the journal-derived installation id; brief 01-install probes and labels the root at formatting, resumes only matching roots and stops on duplicate or unreadable labels; CNF-86 exercises it. Pins kept_root_keys_after_reinstall_refused / kept_root_keys_pinned_without_guard and observed_keys_after_reinstall_refused / observed_keys_pinned_without_guard provide the freshness backstop; ADR-0045 records its limit. The 2026-10-14 comment ceremony window: STG-4 now re-reads and journals activation immediately before every rescue reset, including a failed-append refusal in CNF-38; STA-24 corrects the residual after first contact. The single reset kind does not carry that universal duty. ADR-0044 records cases 3 and 6 reasons; no broader replacement exception was introduced.

title: Decide how the new seed's sheet carries retired-seed allocations after Replace
description:
tw-i55's reading of Replace for a destroyed machine's reported record (panel `i55rep`) found a gap
that reaches past the lost-key report. Four of four readers called it older than tw-i55.

**Background.** Replace gives the installation a new seed, and "The old sheet belongs to the retired
seed, so Replace ends with an export of the new seed's sheet" (`STA-17`). The journal keeps
retired-seed entries: it owns "allocated entries, including tombstones for failed or destroyed
allocations", "All this metadata is included in `STA-16` exports", and "old records are retained
until migration is complete" (`STA-22b`). The companion's `TauWeb.Allocation.replace` says "the
entries stay under their old epoch". But the sheet has one `seed_id`, and import "derives each
listed public key and compares it, validates unique indices within each family and next-unused
counters above all listed indices" (`STA-22b`). Replace restarts the counters, and "A retired-seed
index can coincide with a migrated machine's new index" (`STG-20`).

**Gap.** The text does not say how the new seed's sheet names a machine allocated under the retired
seed, or a record that refers to one:

- `artifact_history`: "exactly one entry per non-jump machine, including retained destroyed-machine
  records", keyed by `machine_index` and refused on "missing, duplicate".
- Exposure-ledger entries that name a destroyed machine in a peer's bound set ("including any
  retained destroyed machine that entry names"). `SEC-5` row 6 ends a machine's own record at
  "Machine destroyed", so whether that machine's own entries survive, as distinct from references
  to it, is also unclear.
- A live machine Replace holds unmigrated under `STA-20` or `STA-24`, which "MUST be shown as not yet
  migrated … and MUST keep its old key", while "Every live machine other than a jump host has
  exactly one entry". The new sheet cannot list it under the derivation check, and leaving it out
  loses its placements' waits on a Restore.
- An LNVPS old machine still awaiting deletion evidence when "the new sheet's export" is shown
  finished (`STA-17`). Its `destroyed: true` can first appear on a later new-seed sheet.

Listed under the old index, such a machine fails the derivation check, can exceed the fresh
counters and can duplicate a live index. Left out, every record naming it points at nothing. Either
way a Replace export can fail its own import, against `CNF-84`'s "no export can write a sheet its
own import refuses".

**Question.** How does the new seed's sheet carry, and how does import check, a retired-seed
allocation and every record that names it?

- carry it seed-qualified, with its recorded public key accepted unverified;
- move it to a new-seed index; or
- leave it on the retired seed's last sheet only.

Constraints that hold under any answer:

- "every imported seed may restore listed identities but MUST NOT allocate new ones" (`STA-22b`).
- Installation ids stay "distinct among machines allocated under the current seed" (`CNF-86`).
- A restored sheet is "knowledge as of export" (`STA-16`).
- No raw value, bare digest, scan key or new value-derived reference enters the sheet (`SEC-5`).
- An older sheet restores its own as-of-export state.

tw-i55 asks the same question for a destroyed machine's reported placement record. Its answer
should give one naming rule that this bead can extend to the cases above. This is an owner question
and makes no normative edit until answered.
close_reason: done

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Note — tw-i55's naming rule has landed, 2026-11-05

tw-i55's answer (comment 110000001 there, "Tag with old seed") is now in the text. It gives the
naming rule this bead can extend:

- A version-7 placement record names its machine by `seed_id` and `machine_index`.
- The new seed's sheet carries a destroyed machine that a reported record names in a separate
  `retired_allocations` member, under its retired seed, index, resource identity and recorded
  public key, with `destroyed: true`. Import accepts that key without deriving it (`STA-22b`'s one
  exception). The derive, unique-index and counter checks over `allocations` are unchanged.
- Only a placement record names a retired allocation. The credential format says: "How artifact
  history, host pins, installation groups and exposure-ledger entries name a machine allocated
  under a retired seed is not yet specified, and neither is what the new seed's sheet holds for a
  live machine that Replace leaves unmigrated."

A review on the tw-i55 change raised the same gap for `artifact_history`: its entries are keyed by
`machine_index` alone, and a retired allocation's index can equal a current machine's (`STG-20`),
so an importer cannot tell which machine an entry belongs to. It asked for the same treatment of
the exposure ledger, host-pin installations and the unmigrated live machine. That finding is this
bead's question, not new scope. The bead's own question and options stand unchanged, and this note
makes no normative edit.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Owner decision — after Replace, the new seed's sheet keeps every retired-seed machine under its own seed, 2026-11-05

Accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule: four of four readers agreeing is accepted; three of four, or two of three, is accepted only when the reader the rule names is in the majority.

Comment 110000001 carries a destroyed machine that a reported placement record names, under its retired seed, and the credential format says: "How artifact history, host pins, installation groups and exposure-ledger entries name a machine allocated under a retired seed is not yet specified, and neither is what the new seed's sheet holds for a live machine that Replace leaves unmigrated." Until that is written, a Replace export can fail its own import (`CNF-84`: "no export can write a sheet its own import refuses").

**Part B — a live machine Replace leaves unmigrated, and an LNVPS rebuild's old machine awaiting deletion evidence.** Accepted: the machine stays on the new seed's sheet as a live allocation under the seed it was allocated under, with its machine state and its other records. Import accepts its recorded key without deriving it, but before any contact with the machine, or any vendor read or call under its identity, the harness derives the key from the retired seed the operator supplies and compares it. The machine is marked destroyed when its deletion evidence is durably recorded. Counts: four of four for the live retired allocation. The key check before contact: three of four, two stating it outright and one implying it; the fourth raised the recorded key's weakness only as an objection and did not address the check.

**Part A, naming.** Accepted: every record that names a machine names it by `seed_id` plus `machine_index`, with no default seed. Counts: four of four.

**Part A, retention.** Accepted: every destroyed retired-seed machine the journal retains keeps all its retained records on every later sheet, whether or not a reported placement record names it. Counts: three to one, with the named reader in the majority. The one reader in the minority would keep a destroyed machine only while a reported record names it.

The text forces neither part: four of four.

**What these picks widen or amend, named:**

- 110000001's "This loosens `STA-22b`'s 'derives each listed public key and compares it' for that allocation only" widens to live retired machines (Part B) and to destroyed retired machines no reported record names (retention).
- `STA-22b`'s "The one exception is a sheet's retired-seed allocation" changes: the exception covers every retired allocation the sheet carries, and for a live one the derive-and-compare check is deferred to before contact, not waived.
- `CNF-84` (BLOCKING) changes: its refusals of "`destroyed` absent or other than `true`", of an entry "no placement names" and of "a record without a report naming one" are replaced; a live retired allocation, a destroyed one no placement names and an unreported placement on a live retired machine are accepted.
- The credential format's "Only a placement record names a retired allocation" and "a retired allocation ... has no `machine_states` entry" change: artifact history, machine states, host pins, installation groups and exposure-ledger entries name retired-seed machines too, and a live retired machine keeps its machine state.
- `STA-22b`'s "The journal keeps that destroyed machine's retired-seed entry while a reported placement record names it" widens to every retired-seed entry the journal keeps.

**Not selected:** for Part A, keeping a destroyed machine only while a reported record names it, and a separate per-record encoding whose absent seed means the payload's; for Part B, moving the machine to a reserved new-seed index before the disk moves, keeping it only on the retired seed's last sheet, and leaving it off the new sheet until its migration finishes.

**Version.** This amends payload version 7 rather than adding version 8. Version 7 was added today, its text marks these members not yet specified, and no fixture, tool or prototype in the repository writes a recovery sheet, so no conforming version-7 sheet with these cases exists to stay readable.

**What the text work must write in:**

- A required `seed_id` beside every machine reference in `artifact_history`, `machine_states`, `host_pins`, `host_pin_installations` and the exposure ledger, including each machine of a ledger entry's recorded bound set; the version 3 to 6 conversion supplies the payload's seed.
- `retired_allocations` carrying every allocation the journal keeps under an earlier seed: destroyed machines, consumed tombstones (a Failed allocation and its predecessor link included), live machines Replace has not migrated (a jump host included) and passes whose revocation or manual retirement is outstanding, each with its state and, for a live one, the reason the screen names.
- A machine whose new index is reserved but whose migration is unconfirmed (a failed relabel read): its records stay under the retired seed, and the reserved index is linked, not a second machine.
- Migration and destruction each as one journal act that moves or marks the entry and every record naming it.
- After a Restore, migration of a live retired machine without a reserved index waits for another Replace, since an imported seed allocates nothing; a second Replace keeps earlier retired entries under their own seeds.
- The sheet holds no key, so a Restore from the sheet alone runs no deletion check for an LNVPS old machine (`SEC-4`).
- `STA-16`, `STA-17`, `STA-22b`, `CNF-84` and a new ADR.

This owner decision is settled and must not be re-asked. It makes no normative edit by itself and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Text landed — retired-seed machines keep their own seed on the new sheet, 2026-11-05

The pick in 113000001 is written into payload version 7 of the credential format, `STA-16`, `STA-17`, `STA-22b` and `CNF-84`, and recorded in ADR-0058; ADR-0057's open point on retired-seed naming now points there.

- Every machine reference carries a required `seed_id` beside its index, with no default seed; the version 3 to 6 conversion supplies the payload's seed.
- `retired_allocations` carries destroyed machines, Failed tombstones, unmigrated machines (a jump host and an LNVPS old machine included) and outstanding passes, each with exactly one state member and, for an outstanding one, a closed reason.
- A live retired allocation's key check is deferred to before contact, use of a pass's key, a vendor read or call, or binding, never waived.
- Migration and destruction are each one journal act; a reserved new index is linked as `migration_index`, not a second machine; after a Restore, migration without one waits for another Replace.

One review pass ran; its findings are fixed or, for two points it found the pick does not decide, filed as tw-rds: retired-seed handoffs, and a pending `migration_index` at a later Replace. Both are marked not yet specified in the text.

This comment makes no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: State-machine clarity and composition atlas
description:
## Outcome
A navigable behavioral atlas of the existing specification, plus a separately scoped session-authority assurance track. This is a work plan, not a specification amendment. Checkpoint 0 is recorded below; no atlas implementation was made while filing it.

## Source and baseline
The owner's State-Machine Clarity and Composition Plan, prepared 2026-11-01, checkpoints 0–5 and Recommended first change, is transferred into this epic and its child descriptions so execution does not require a temporary plan file.

Working revision: 9086166b0ee62387da6440da059f5b89f01a0d8d on main, initially clean. It equals the reviewed baseline exactly; there are no intervening committed amendments to reconcile. The actual tree, owners and current witness files were inspected rather than treating the plan's review as current authority.

Baseline command, run unpiped on 2026-11-01: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`. Actual result: exit 0, “All gates passed.” Formal, witnesses, regions, identifiers, fixtures, obligations, citations and coverage all passed. No pre-existing failing gate or missing toolchain. This command does not run the mutation controls; no current controls pass is claimed. Subsequent implementation must run the required gates before and after, and controls for any changed refusal checks.

## Bounded first delivery
Use the Stage applicability and admission table in 07-conformance.md as the source list: stage-1 typed LNVPS, local authority, interruption, delivery, re-entry and maintained-cloud Restore/Replace. Distinguish typed restart confirmation from guest boot, service survival and delivery checking. Dedicated delivery_reboot/rescue, attest, untyped calls, multi-machine tenants and paid relay retain their own applicability. A synthetic witness or documentation pass admits no production capability, procured-inference minting, vendor behavior or browser/device conformance.

## Existing diagram inventory
Locations are at the working revision. Preserve useful figures and route readers to them; do not claim that the repository lacks state diagrams.

| Existing view | Location | Treatment / class |
|---|---|---|
| System context | 00-overview.md, System context (Mermaid near line 143) | Navigation: keep; label conceptual and show stage-1 route separately from attest and larger sets. |
| Two planes | 01-architecture.md, Two planes (near line 126) | Navigation: keep; index approval and binding owners, including inference's separate route. |
| Concurrent sessions | 01-architecture.md, concurrency (near line 645) | Navigation: keep; default singleton illustration, keys remain machine-owned, not new session-owned keys. |
| Recovery ladder state diagram | 01-architecture.md, ARC-16 (near line 742) | Presentation: qualify Retry with STA-5/STA-6/STA-8/STA-24 pointers; third-rung behavior remains the semantic question tw-ae7. |
| Routes to a fingerprint | 02-channel.md (near line 32) | Navigation: keep route/admission and pending evidence distinctions; the admitted LNVPS route is not completed integrated conformance. |
| Attest sequence | 02-channel.md, CHN-4 (near line 360) | Navigation plus missing evidence: retain route-specific label; do not promote it to the stage-1 path or a full durability/first-contact proof. |
| Trust tiers | 05-trust.md (near line 10) | Navigation: keep; outside the behavioral transition core. |
| Dedicated installation sequence | 06-first-stage.md, The sequence (near line 273) | Navigation: keep as construction-test-bed sequence, not stage-1 LNVPS evidence. |
| Recovery by access/vendor | 03-state-and-recovery.md (near line 907) | Presentation: keep and qualify “Zero downtime” as key/pin recovery rather than live session/scan/allocation authority; preserve the existing ARC-22 LNVPS pointer. “Always works” is a design route, not integrated device evidence. |

The archived rust-first-ai-harness-pwa-spec.md has an ASCII component diagram near line 151; retain it as archive, not current authority. Mermaid inventory was searched across repository Markdown. No replacement diagram is needed for every existing figure.

## High-level word audit and classification
The classes below are those of plan checkpoint 0; each proposed change has one primary class. Navigation and presentation changes preserve behavior. Missing evidence remains a named boundary; semantic decisions remain outside the clarity track.

| Word / finding | Owner and observed distinction | Class / destination |
|---|---|---|
| retry | ARC-16 and CONTEXT.md's Recovery ladder compress recovery to “Retry”; STA-5's vendor retry classes and STA-6's box-plane rule are elsewhere. STA-8: “It MUST NOT be retried automatically and no timer may clear it.” | Presentation: route the ladder to these owners; never draw automatic replay of an uncertain effect. |
| resume | ARC-22's Resume-or-abandon opening screen, STG-12, ARC-10's read/converge, STA-7's replay, STA-20's stopped wait and STA-23's processed suspension/end are distinct. STA-7: “**No model turn is silently resumed from an uncertain destructive operation.**” | Navigation: index each continuation boundary. Missing evidence for real device scheduling belongs to existing conformance, not a new arrow. |
| ready | ready_to_reset belongs to ARC-43/STA-20b and current-installation prerequisite evidence. STG-21a: “It does not establish a completed guest boot or service survival.” Running-state readiness, pin eligibility, scan readiness, allocation permission and admission are distinct. 07-conformance.md separates construction from delivery admission. | Navigation: preserve independent predicates; no global Ready enum or universal gate. |
| delivered | ARC-17, ARC-39 and ARC-43 own verdict, findings, declaration and local evidence labels; executive-summary.md already distinguishes findings and report authority. ARC-17: “placement itself clears no finding.” | Navigation: keep the current delivery distinctions, including lifecycle findings permitting placement and the post-placement demonstration. |
| confirmed | STG-21a owns operation-specific LNVPS predicates; STG-4 owns Robot's different predicates; STA-3/STA-24 own durable acceptance. Restart receipt, guest boot, service survival, accepted pin and final verdict are different. | Navigation: map observation to exact authority; do not apply Robot status-read confirmation to LNVPS restart or imply billing ends at stop. |
| Recovery chart's Zero downtime / Always works | STA-17/STA-22b restore known identities with no new allocation authority; STA-23 ends lost runtime authority; ARC-17/SEC-5/ARC-43 retain findings/scan re-check duties. | Presentation: qualify at the figure's owner without inventing the missing restored-command rule (tw-ub7). |
| Session/dispatch composition | Dispatch.lean's opening docstring assumes termination and single-writer convention; pending-check/lifecycle reads, untyped pause/hold, detailed protected encodings/listing selection and inference clocks are omitted. | Missing evidence: explicit prose-only labels; selected assurance child handles only session-authority seam. |
| Relay coverage | Relay.lean's header explicitly retains a historical profile; current /v2/ behavior is outside it. TASKS.md open T30 is the existing port owner. | Missing evidence: point to that owner; no duplicate current-relay task. |
| Delivery reboot trace task drift | tw-itv's no-trace claim is stale: schema-8 file and Dispatch.lean contain command_holds_delivery_reboot / delivery_reboot_without_hold; check-controls.sh has the drop-reboot control. rebootRequest still copies execRequest facts and uses approvalExec. | Missing evidence: retain tw-itv for distinct approval and bounded-description remainder; do not duplicate or claim closed. |
| Witness pair integrity | check_witnesses.py checks emission drift; tw-316 owns reciprocal pair/start/events/changed-assumptions validation. | Missing evidence: link existing bead; local atlas selected-pair checks must not create a competing corpus-wide gate. |

## Semantic decisions already owned elsewhere
These do not block filing or the first atlas change. Label the affected cells “not specified” and link the existing question. Do not settle them in a renderer or completion claim.

| Existing owner | Distinguishing history / conflicting boundary |
|---|---|
| tw-ae7 | ARC-16: “then destroy the machine and restart under a different domain, which costs a server.” ARC-22 offers different LNVPS stop/renewal-off and reinstall stand-ins. A stuck stage-1 machine reaches rung three: same-machine reinstall versus stopped old machine plus new order versus no third rung remains undecided. |
| tw-ub7 | STA-24: “What this rule cannot reach is a journal that is lost with the phone”. STA-20's hold is journal-derived, but on-machine persistent records survive. Restore an older backup after a command send; then request another command: whether to collect old records before sends is unsettled. |
| tw-pgp | STA-24's untyped-vendor destructive hold names “the model's box-plane commands”; ADR-0050's machine destructive rule stops work whoever starts it. Dispose an untyped vendor call destructively, then request a harness-composed job: no silent extension from typed behavior. Stage 2 boundary. |
| tw-pkn | SEC-5 row 23 retires a reference at machine destruction; CNF-95(f) retains A/B withholding until both references are rebuilt, and ADR-0050 rejects output release without scanning copied secrets. Destroy M while A still withholds output possibly containing M's secret: release/continued-scan outcome remains undecided. Stage 2 boundary. |
| tw-z99 | STA-24: “An unresolved activation or key registration touches no running system and blocks nothing on the box.” ADR-0048 admits delivery reboot beside activation. Activate rescue, then delivery reboot: a changed boot can be rescue rather than the installed delivery target. Dedicated-route decision. |
| tw-sfu, tw-hwl, tw-nj8 | Definitive create failure while a session still owns its set: failure evidence and later sends, successor allocation on the same entry, and ordering a different entry are separate undecided boundaries. Do not promote unresolved/disposed/stop to failure or drop old membership. |
| tw-yuo | The phase-B finding establishes a pinned arch login, while STA-20 needs a root-only job directory and delivery reads need privileged access. Login then create a root-only job record: no owner yet defines the privilege route, authorization or refusal. Keep this existing stage-1 question explicit; do not guess a sudo policy. |
| tw-lq8 | Rescue rekeys a dedicated machine under a fresh seed after sheet loss; the shown installation identity changes while its root label can remain stale. The next rescue install can misread its own root as a predecessor. Installation ordinal, relabel ordering and migration remain this later-route owner's question. |
| tw-l1l, tw-yhd | Reinstall target/acceptance history and recovery outside a session retain their existing questions. Sheetless discovery/listing alone must not become cloud-destroy authorization. |

The existing proposed operator-reported key-revocation amendment remains tw-i55, not a new atlas task. No newly discovered behavior decision blocks this transfer. The session-authority child must stop at an actual new ambiguity and capture clauses plus distinguishing history before seeking a decision. OPN-27 remains the tenant architecture owner; empirical recovery/scanning retain OPN-3/OPN-18/OPN-28 and their conformance applicability.

## Constraints inherited by every child

The renderer projects committed per-step outcomes and knowledge; it never evaluates guards or authors expected outcomes. Validate exact supported schema/module/shape and declaration resolution. title: Review and check session authority across asynchronous interruption
description:
## Outcome
Separately review and strengthen the session-authority boundary across asynchronous interruption with a narrow formal-companion extension connected to Dispatch, or record an exact unproved/undecided gap. This assurance track is not a prerequisite for clarity completion.

## Why this exists
Dispatch.lean assumes an ended session sends no further request and does not prove termination. Independent local properties are insufficient to establish that stale asynchronous work cannot revive authority or bypass a journal-derived barrier.

## Scope and contract first
Start from STA-23, SEC-1, SEC-4 and applicable ARC-31a clauses at the execution revision. Inventory represented versus omitted facts and review exact candidate statements against these owners before adding proofs. Use processed events and symbolic authority/session/binding identities; keep durable historical evidence separate from live runtime authority. Naming a new Authority module is optional, not prescribed architecture.

Represent ordinary hide, processed suspension, validated continuation, explicit Lock, pagehide/shutdown, session end, request admission and late actionable publication. Preserve seed-backup hide's full Lock exception. Procured-key clock/expiry checks apply only to that inference path, not global credential expiry. No instantaneous physical app-switch or guaranteed cleanup observation.

Review these plan proof targets, not new requirements by fiat:
- Ended authority cannot admit a new ordinary effect or actionable publication.
- Stale approval/late completion cannot restore it or transfer across sessions/bindings.
- Ordinary visibility-only hide outside backup ceremony preserves eligible sessions.
- Processed suspension requires the specified validation before ordinary sends/publication, with no assumption every freeze was reported.
- Lock/replay/expiry leaves remote uncertainty intact and supplies no permission to repeat it.
- Ending one session leaves other eligible sessions and successor resource barriers intact.

Connect authority decisions through a small explicit interface to existing Dispatch behavior; reuse its barrier rather than copying guards. Separate authorization properties from real implementation pre-send/post-await fences and storage ordering. Already accepted remote work can continue after local authority ends. Keep general statements, finite witnesses and implementation evidence separate.

## Non-goals and decision handling
Inherit tw-237 constraints: no full browser/OS proof, secrets/timing simulation, engine or new runtime in this repository, new procured-inference admission, weakened theorem/gate, or hidden behavior amendment. New formal definitions remain a checking interpretation until the per-clause authority conditions are met.

If owners conflict or omit the needed answer, capture exact clauses and a distinguishing event history, obtain the decision before behavior change, and amend only the affected normative seam with its record afterwards. Do not silently select refusal precedence or use a rejected trace to redefine the rule. Existing restoration/hold/acceptance decisions listed in tw-237 remain separately owned.

## Dependencies / ordering
Blocked by the first atlas slice so the contract review can use its authority/barrier matrix and established presentation conventions. Composition and trace expansion need not wait for this child. No hard dependency on tw-itv, tw-316 or later-route semantic decisions unless an actual new shared obligation is demonstrated.

## Acceptance Criteria
Run the Nix check-all gate unpiped before/after. For each selected exact property require a useful successful path and a guard mutation/removal exposing a concrete bad trace. Add a discriminating test at the authority/Dispatch seam, not only unrelated local properties. Controls require exactly their target finding and valid acceptance where needed; run them under the prescribed memory cap and record actual results. Update any affected formal declarations and Markdown together, preserve existing proofs, inspect axioms/assumptions, schema/version and emitter obligations. State what remains prose-only or assumed and identify real browser fault/fence evidence still owed downstream. A precise gap is acceptable under plan checkpoint 4, but no missing proof may be reported as proved.

## Spec refs
Plan §§2,8,10, tw-237, STA-23, SEC-1/SEC-4, ARC-31a, Dispatch.lean's session-termination assumption and ADR-0032.
close_reason: Completed symbolic session-authority composition with Dispatch. Retained successful paths and isolated guard-removal witnesses for actor/session matching, bound-entry membership, exclusive growth and immutable key limits. Specification gates, 63 offline tests and 274 controls passed; authority schema 2 emitted. No runtime conformance or behavior amendment claimed.

title: Clarify conflicting candidate and allowlist provider pins
description:

ARC-31b in 01-architecture.md says "Existing candidate pins MUST stay attached to their slugs when the order changes." TRU-A1a in 05-trust.md says "A model entering the candidate order from the allowlist MUST inherit that entry's pin."

title: No gate checks that a marked witness pair shares its events and differs only in assumptions
description: Corpus-wide structural validation of marked refused/admitted witness pairs is missing from the emission gate. The 2026-11-02 Agent Brief comment records the current verified gap, complete acceptance criteria and drain-lane handoff. It supersedes the original historical inventory. ADR-0032 and the existing witness schema own the comparison contract; the emitted corpus owns the trace list.
close_reason: Implemented in 592d89c, 4d92ce1 and c29ab22: reciprocal witness occurrence matching with complete typed start and event inputs, unequal assumptions, and stable findings. Emission and atlas safeguards retained. Nix check-all, 82 offline tests and 309 mutation controls passed.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
## Agent Brief — triage outcome, 2026-11-02

**Category:** bug. **State:** ready-for-agent. **Disposition:** hand to the drain lane, after its current ready queue. The independent read was unanimous that this bounded repair needs no behavior decision. The owner authorized proceeding when no such decision remains.

**Summary:** Enforce the existing refused/admitted witness-pair shape across the emitted corpus, even when committed bytes match the emission.

**Current behavior and verification:** Matching emitted and committed scratch copies passed the witness gate despite equal assumptions, different start, different ordered event inputs, a missing partner, nonreciprocal references or same-side metadata. The current corpus satisfies the intended structural matching. The atlas checks only its selected pairs. Repeated theorem declarations name distinct trace occurrences; declaration uniqueness cannot be assumed. The original bead's historical numeric inventory is superseded by the emitted corpus, which is the source of the list.

**Owner and desired behavior:** ADR-0032 says "Each refused-and-admitted pair appears whole, marked" and describes "the bad trace refused with the guard, admitted without it". The existing witness schema remains the format's home. Every marked trace must have exactly one reciprocal opposite-side counterpart in its own witness file, with equal start and ordered event inputs and unequal assumptions. Compare the full event objects, preserving scalar types and array order; object-key order is immaterial. Outcomes and subsequent state projections are not pair inputs.

**Key interfaces:** The existing witness emission gate and pair metadata; declaration references identify candidate trace occurrences, not unique trace keys. Match using reciprocal declarations and the complete start/event structure, with one-to-one accounting. Ignore unmarked uses of the same declaration. Validate malformed metadata and missing or ambiguous partners explicitly. Do not reject a legitimate pair because more than one assumption changes or because its refused side uses a nonproduction assumption; retained Pins cases rely on both distinctions.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Every marked trace is checked corpus-wide; retain the atlas's selected-pair safeguards.
- Refuse malformed metadata, absent/nonreciprocal/wrong-side partners, changed start or ordered inputs, equal assumptions and ambiguous counterparts. Emit a stable WITNESS PAIRS finding naming the file and trace declarations/locations and explaining the mismatch. Attribute a broken pair once rather than counting both endpoints.
- Add a discriminating control for each refusal. Mutate emitted and committed copies identically so drift cannot explain rejection. Assert exactly one finding item under the target label, not merely one nonempty output line. Include a changed repeated-declaration case, and a removed counterpart whose theorem is still present elsewhere.
- Positive controls accept the valid corpus, reordered witness arrays, legitimate repeated declarations, multiple changed assumptions and differing outcome projections.
- Keep missing/orphan emission checks, forbidden-identifier refusal, declaration tagging and emission equality. Update diagnostic descriptions and existing pointers to this now-covered gap without creating another normative home.
- Run the unpiped Nix check-all gate before and after, the full mutation-control gate, and the same offline unit suite CI runs. Record actual exits; toolchain failure is red.

**Out of scope:** Runtime implementation, recomputing protocol outcomes, exactly-one-changed-guard or production-only assumptions, a new requirement for differing output steps, global declaration uniqueness, a new schema, or any claim that serialized traces have a stronger theorem tie than the emitter currently establishes. No requirement, theorem or guard is weakened.

title: Reject duplicate comment identifiers in the tracked issue export
description:
Reject duplicate comment identifiers across the tracked issue export.

Independent tracker databases can allocate the same numeric comment identifier to different issues. A textual merge can preserve both records even though SQLite comment identifiers are global primary keys. Import then renumbers one comment, so a later export unexpectedly changes an unrelated issue. This happened when the parallel root-access and recovery triage records met the atlas work.

Add a read-only specification gate for global uniqueness of every comment identifier in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and wire it into `tools/check-all.sh` and the existing CI path. Its deterministic finding should identify the duplicate value and every owning issue/occurrence, including duplicates within one issue. It must not rewrite identifiers, modify the export or database, or discard a comment.

Acceptance:
- A consistent export with globally distinct identifiers passes, including comments with identical text but distinct identifiers.
- A duplicate across different issues fails with a finding naming both owners.
- A duplicate within one issue also fails and identifies both occurrences.
- Output is deterministic under record ordering; unrelated valid records produce no extra findings.
- Extend `tools/check-controls.sh` with one negative control per refusal, requiring exactly one finding under the targeted label, and a positive control demonstrating acceptance of valid distinct identifiers.
- Run the repository's required gates and controls unpiped. Leave no mutated tracked file or database behind.

This issue is for the detection gate and its controls only. The current metadata repair and local allocation separation are separate work; no harness implementation or automatic repair belongs in this gate.
close_reason: Added a read-only comment-ID collision gate with deterministic issue and occurrence diagnostics, integrated into check-all, with regression coverage and controls. Required nix develop commands passed: check-all exit 0; unittest discovery exit 0 (48 tests); check-controls exit 0 (238 controls). Scratch aggregate runner returned 1 only for the collision gate, with all other gates passing. Export, database and WAL bytes remained unchanged during verification; shared-memory coordination bytes differed.

title: Decide which act records a rotation and what a failed rotation job does to the old reference
description:
tw-8cl's pick (comment 121000001) keys a rotation's boundary to "the journal act that records the rotation", and `SEC-5`'s `reference_ended` mark is set by the same act. Two readers of that panel found the act underdetermined.

**What the text says.** `SEC-5` row 23 ends the old placement's scan key and reference "Until rotation". `ARC-43` says "Rotation goes through the full `place_secret` ceremony". `SEC-5` now says: "Which act of the rotation's `place_secret` records the rotation, and what a rotation whose job fails or stays unresolved (`STA-8`) does to P's reference, are not yet specified."

**The risk.** Suppose the old reference ends at the act recorded before the bytes leave, and the rotation's job then fails or stays unresolved. The old value may still be at the path, and later output is no longer compared against it.

**Question.**
- Which act records a rotation? Candidates: the record made before the bytes leave; the job's terminal record; the new reference's construction.
- What does a failed or unresolved rotation job do to the old placement's reference, its listing and the mark?

Constraints that hold either way:
- "Unscanned bytes MUST be withheld" (`SEC-5`).
- A rotation never counts as a scan (tw-8cl).
- The mark is set by the act that records the rotation (ADR-0060).

Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.

comments.text:
## Owner pick — a rotation is recorded by its zero-exit job record, 2026-11-05

The question: which act of a rotation's `place_secret` records the rotation, and what a rotation
whose job fails or stays unresolved does to the old placement P's reference. `SEC-5` said: "Which
act of the rotation's `place_secret` records the rotation, and what a rotation whose job fails or
stays unresolved (`STA-8`) does to P's reference, are not yet specified."

**Q1, the recording act: the owner's 2026-11-05 pick is B.** "The rotation is recorded only by the
act that admits the rotation job's completed root-only job record with a zero exit (`STA-20`).
Until then P stays live, listed and required, and the new placement's reference is required too
from the pre-send record, since the new bytes may have left. A nonzero exit, an unresolved job or a
disposition records no rotation."

Four independent readers answered; a fifth seat was unavailable. Two recommended B and two
recommended C (the rotation recorded only by a matching cross-check digest after the job). None
recommended A (the record made before the bytes leave). All four said the text forces no option.
The tie went to the owner, who picked B.

**Q2, a failed, unresolved or disposed rotation job: 4 of 4.** All four readers said the same, under
B or C alike, and this is recorded with the pick:
- A nonzero exit, an unresolved job or a disposition records no rotation.
- P's reference stays as it was, armed or unarmed; P stays listed live and required; no
  `reference_ended` mark is set.
- The new placement is listed, and its reference required, from the record made before its bytes
  leave.
- The text is silent on what a failed first placement does to its listing and reference.
- The answer narrows or widens no earlier owner pick (ADR-0060, ADR-0061, ADR-0062), touches no
  theorem and leaves row 23's lifetime column unedited.

**Not settled by the panel, left to the text work:**
- What an exported sheet carries while a rotation is not recorded. The credential format says
  "Reject duplicates and two records without a report at one machine, application name, secret
  name and path", so writing both P and the new placement would produce a sheet the importer
  rejects.
- Whether a zero-exit record collected after a disposition named the rotation's call records the
  rotation. Two readers said it records none; one said the text cannot tell; one did not address
  it.

**Left open, outside the question:** what ends a failed attempt's new placement, and what a failed
first placement does to its listing and reference.

**Not selected:** A, the record made before the bytes leave; C, a matching cross-check.

This pick is settled and must not be re-asked. It makes no normative edit and no capability,
readiness or runtime claim.

comments.text:
## Closed — a rotation is recorded by its zero-exit job record, 2026-11-05

The owner's pick in comment 130000001 is now text:

- **`SEC-5`.** The act that records a rotation is the one that admits the rotation job's completed root-only job record with a zero exit (`STA-20`). The record made before the bytes leave, a nonzero exit, a job that stays unresolved and a disposition record no rotation: P's scan key and reference stay as they were, armed or unarmed; a P without a report stays live and required, a reported P stays in operator-reported history; no `reference_ended` mark is set. The rotation boundary holds from that act on. The "not yet specified" sentence is removed.
- **`ARC-43`.** The new placement is listed, and its reference required, from the record made before its bytes leave, whatever its job then does. Until the rotation is recorded, the old placement stays beside it as it was, and output owes both references.
- **Credential format.** A rotation's new placement enters the export only once `SEC-5` records the rotation, for a reported P too.
- **Conformance.** `CNF-95(j)` names the recording act and adds the window, nonzero-exit, unresolved, disposition, late-record, reported-placement and window-sheet branches.
- **ADR-0063** records the decision, and ADR-0061 notes that both its points are decided there.

**The two details left to the text work.**
- **The sheet.** Writing an unreported P and its new placement together, or the new placements of a failed attempt and its retry, would give two records without a report at one machine, application name, secret name and path, which the importer rejects. The smallest change the text forces is to export a new placement only once its rotation is recorded. It narrows one thing: a sheet exported between the record made before the bytes leave and the recording act holds no record for the new placement, so a Restore from it lists the new placement nowhere and requires no reference for it. A failed attempt's new placement is never exported. This sits within `ARC-43`'s existing limit after store loss. No sheet field, version or importer rule changes.
- **The late record.** A zero-exit job record of a rotation call that a disposition disposed records no rotation, whenever collected; it is journaled and shown. The review pass agreed 4 of 4.

One review pass ran before the merge, four readers with a fifth seat unavailable, and its fixes are in. The decision narrows or widens no earlier owner pick and touches no theorem.

**Left open, as a separate bead.** tw-x7k: what ends a failed attempt's new placement while the local store stays intact, and what a failed first placement does to its listing, its reference and the export.

This closure makes no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Decide whether the trust display says anything about a key revoked while its reference is armed
description:
tw-5qs and tw-e42 (ADR-0062) offer the operator report only while a placement's reference is
unarmed. This bead asks about the other window: the key is already revoked at its service, but the
reference is armed.

**What the text says.**
- `ARC-43`: "The card is not offered for an armed reference, which keeps its scan until a rotation,
  destruction or local-store loss ends it".
- `ARC-43`: "A placement whose key was revoked at its service while its reference is armed is ended
  by a rotation, once `ARC-17`'s placement gates admit that rotation, or by destruction."
- `ARC-43` lists the placed secret in the trust display "until it is rotated or the machine is
  destroyed".

**The gap.** In that window the placement stays listed live and keeps its scan. The scan errs on the
safe side, but nothing on the trust display records that the operator revoked the key. If
`ARC-17`'s gates hold the rotation, the window can last a long time. The display then shows a live
exposure that the operator says is gone, and records no statement from the operator.

**Question.** Should the trust display say anything about a key the operator says is revoked while
its reference is armed? For example, the display could record a non-final note that changes neither
the scan nor the listing. Or should the text record that the display stays silent on purpose, and
why?

This differs from tw-foh, which is about output after a rotation. This bead is about the time before
any rotation, while the reference is armed.

Constraints that hold either way:
- The report stays final, and is offered only while the reference is unarmed (ADR-0062).
- The listing drops nothing on a machine's claim (`ARC-43`).
- No raw value, bare digest or scan key enters history or export.

Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.

title: Decide how a replacement's keyless account-level step reads in a vendor account both entries share
description:
`STA-22b`'s replacement act (PR #86, owner ratification in tw-nj8 comment 106000001) refuses a step that re-sends the old entry's request or "targets the old entry's identity, resource (`STA-24`), key or own account". It admits the replacement's own step "for its own identity, resource, key and account". It also says "where both entries use one vendor account, a step there that names the replacement's own resource and key is its own step."

**Gap.** When both entries use one vendor account, a step that names no per-entry resource or key falls under neither limb. An example is an email submission or another account-level request to that shared account. It does not name "the replacement's own resource and key". "Own account" does not refuse it either, because the account is not the old entry's alone. A byte-identical request is "re-sending its request". Any other such step is unspecified.

**Question.** In a shared vendor account, is a keyless account-level step of the same kind as the old entry's unresolved step:

- the replacement's own step, admitted under `STA-24`'s barriers; or
- a repeat, refused until the old step is resolved or disposed of; or
- refused unless it differs from the old step by something the text names?

No specified path produces this today. LNVPS gives each machine its own account (ADR-0042), Robot has no create or order step (`STG-18`), and an untyped scope's resource is the scope. So the answer pre-decides a future typed adapter at a vendor where every machine shares one account.

Constraints that hold under any answer: `STA-24`'s barriers, holds and pauses still apply; the old step stays unresolved and restricted; nothing relies on the old step's result. This is an owner question, and it makes no normative edit until answered.

title: Settle tw-lq8's open points: SEC-1's flow count, the rescue-call grant, reinstall and no-acceptance ends, and the brief's unchosen points
description:
tw-lq8 landed `STA-17`'s dedicated rescue rekey: a model-free flow that installs the new client key through vendor-authenticated rescue, then relabels the root and removes an identified old key after a login with the new key (`STA-22b` says "Robot recovery installs keys from a fresh seed through vendor-authenticated rescue and re-reads host pins"). tw-lq8's brief (comment 92000001) left some of the points below unchosen, and its reviews found the rest. None is chosen here.

- **`SEC-1`'s flow count.** `SEC-1` says "Two harness flows hold a client key outside any session … the jump-host flow (`CHN-R6`), and Replace's key migration (`STA-17`), which holds one machine's old and new keys". The rescue rekey also holds a client key outside any session, and `ARC-43` lists it apart from "Replace's model-free direct re-entry migration". Whether `SEC-1` names it or folds it into Replace's key migration is open. A panel of four readings split on whether the text forces either answer.
- **The vendor grant for the rekey's rescue calls.** `SEC-5` row 1 authorizes "Replace's flow only for an LNVPS rebuild's old machine's stop, its renewal-off and the read to confirm that renewal-off", and `SEC-4` says of that grant "The grant covers no other vendor call and no other machine". No rule grants the Robot rescue calls the rekey makes outside a session. The gap predates tw-lq8: it is already in `STA-22b`'s Robot recovery.
- **What a reinstall dispatch does to an unfinished rekey.** `STA-17` says "The machine counts as migrated, and `b-7` becomes its confirmed current id, only when a read shows `b-7`", and `STG-20` ends the unconfirmed mark when "a destructive reinstall of the machine is dispatched". After a changed-label stop no write of `b-7` is sent, so a later reinstall may come before any read of `b-7`; what that dispatch does to the unfinished migration, and whether the machine then counts as migrated, is not specified.

- **A rekey that ends with no acceptance.** `STA-17` says the operator "MAY explicitly accept 7"; the operator may decline, or the root's label may not read. With no acceptance, `STG-20`'s `n` is the ordinal "starting at zero per machine", and no shown id is marked unconfirmed. The install brief's exception holds only "while the harness marks the shown id **unconfirmed**", so a root labelled `a-7` reads as "the predecessor", the hazard tw-lq8 was filed for. What the rekey does then is not specified.
- **Showing unknown past exposure.** The brief's desired behavior says "Known exposure is counted, and unknown past exposure is shown as unknown, never zero", and it left open "which text supplies the duty to show unknown past exposure as unknown: decision B with `SEC-1`, or `STA-13`". `STA-17` says only that the session "never relies on" zero exposure, and no `CNF-117` case tests the display.
- **The identified-key branch and `CNF-5`.** With the old key identified, `STA-17` "keeps the new key and unrelated authorizations", so a read of the machine still shows more than its own key. Decision 151000001 put "never shown as holding only its own key" on the unidentified case only. Whether the identified case gets the same display check, and what tells an unrelated authorization apart from "A key those records do not identify", are not specified.
- **The label bound for an accepted ordinal.** `STG-20` bounds `n` at 9 999 999 and says "The harness MUST refuse a destructive reinstall that would make `n` = 10 000 000". No rule says what happens to an acceptance of a label above that bound.
- **The companion.** The brief's acceptance criteria say "Where a touched clause is formalized, change its Lean declaration and its prose together". `STG-20`'s `n` changed for this path while `TauWeb.Dispatch.installationOf` did not; the prose says the companion does not carry the accepted ordinal. Whether that disclosure is enough, or the declaration should change, is open.
- **The brief's other unchosen points**, which no text settles: whether the running installation's own unrecorded status is part of the unknown; how the "no admissible saved history" trigger applies where admissible facts reach only an earlier installation, and which partial shapes are admissible; whether this route needs a pointer to `STA-16`'s unchecked rule; and which of the disclosures `ARC-25a` keeps for an unpinned installation apply beside the unknown history.

Settled, not reopened: the `CNF-5` decision on tw-lq8 (comment 151000001), old-key A and decision B.

The question: `SEC-1` says "Two harness flows hold a client key outside any session", naming the jump-host flow (`CHN-R6`) and Replace's key migration (`STA-17`). The dedicated rescue rekey also holds a client key outside any session, and `ARC-43` lists it apart from Replace's migration. Should `SEC-1` name it or fold it into Replace's key migration?

The pick: `SEC-1` names the rescue rekey as its own flow, one that holds only the machine's new key. The sentence drops its count rather than saying "Three". `SEC-1`'s "no party other than … the harness's model-free Replace flow" sentence names the rescue rekey too, and so do the places that quote it in `01-architecture.md` and ADR-0026.

Four independent readings: 3 favoured naming it separately, 1 favoured folding it into Replace. On whether the text forces an answer, 2 found it forces neither, 1 found it forces naming and 1 found it forces folding.

owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
**Owner pick, 2026-11-05: "Also check disk label"** (open point 3: how a dedicated server with no recovery sheet is tied to the approved machine entry the rescue rekey's grant acts on).

The question: `STG-4` makes key registration's resource "the machine's approved entry (`STA-24`)", and `SEC-4` says "What is dispatched is the approved record". With no recovery sheet, no store backup and no journal, nothing the harness retains ties a Robot server to this harness, and `SEC-4` says what an adapter lists of the account "is displayed and never relied on". The grant picked in comment 153000001 cannot dispatch until something ties its one server to an entry.

The pick:
- The grant's own approval card names one Robot server by its immutable server number, shows the vendor's listed facts for it as the vendor's word at one moment, says no saved record ties that server to this harness, and preselects nothing. Approving the card journals and reserves, before any external effect, the fresh-seed machine entry at index `b` mapping the account reference and that server number to `b`'s expected key. Every call is checked against that approved record, never against a listing.
- In rescue, before the new key is written, a harness-composed read must find a root whose label reads in the harness's form. With none, the flow writes no key, stops unfinished, and only the reset back into the installed system is sent. A label that passes proves nothing: `STA-17`'s "no label component establishes an old seed-derived identity" stands.
- Accepted by name: this adds a stop that the grant pick (comment 153000001) does not list, and with no sheet a server whose root label is missing or damaged gets no rescue rekey from the harness, which narrows `STA-15`'s "On Robot the ceremony always works" for that case.

Four independent readings (a fifth seat was unavailable): 4 found no existing rule already ties the server. On whether the text forces an answer, 4 found it forces neither approval alone nor approval with the label check, and 4 found it rules out requiring a retained record. The recommendation split 2 to 2 between approval alone and approval with the label check; the owner broke the tie. 4 found approval alone, confined to one server and no destructive call, weakens nothing; the narrowing above is accepted by name.

Not selected: approval alone; requiring a retained record, which contradicts `STA-15`'s Robot route, `STA-22b`'s no-sheet route, ADR-0020 and `CNF-117`'s no-sheet case.

Text work: in the `SEC-1` and rescue-call grant change. Nothing is enabled.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
**Queued, 2026-11-05: points the rescue rekey's grant leaves not specified** (raised by the readings behind the "Also check disk label" pick; none is decided by the text work).

1. **An unresolved reset back.** `STG-4` confirms the reset into the installed system only "when sshd answers with the installed pin", and its predicates have no negative form. After a stop before the installed system's host keys are read, including the root-label stop, the reset back cannot be confirmed and stays unresolved until the operator's disposition. Whether host keys may be read from a disk that fails the label check is not specified.
2. **An activation left armed.** A stop after a confirmed rescue activation and before the reset into rescue leaves the server set to boot rescue at its next reset. The grant holds no deactivation call.
3. **An entry made by a wrong pick.** What becomes of the machine entry an approval created for the wrong server is not specified. `STA-22b`'s failed state needs "local proof that this allocation's create was never sent", which does not fit, and the entry must grant no later binding or re-entry.
4. **Matching the credential to the account.** How the operator's Robot credential is compared with the entry's account reference before each call is not specified.

This record makes no normative edit.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
**Queued, 2026-11-05: further points the rescue rekey's text leaves not specified** (raised by the one review pass on the binding text; none is decided by it, and they join comment 155000001's four).

5. **More than one labelled root.** The pick requires "a root whose label reads in the harness's form". Which root receives the key when more than one reads in that form is not specified; the text writes no key there until it is.
6. **A card for a server another entry holds.** Approving the card creates a new entry. Nothing compares the card's server number with the entries the journal already holds, so the session, hold and disposition guards, which act per entry, could miss a server another entry names, such as one whose earlier reset back is unresolved.
7. **The kept reset back across a restart.** A restart revives no authority that has ended and no stopped flow. Whether the reset back kept after the root-label stop survives a restart, and what the journaled approval gives a resumed flow before that stop, are not specified.
8. **The host-key read on the success path.** `STG-4` confirms the reset back "when sshd answers with the installed pin". The rescue rekey's text names no job that reads the installed system's host keys before that reset, so how the grant's first end condition is met is not specified.
9. **A failure or operator stop in rescue.** Only the root-label stop keeps the reset back. After any other failure or an operator stop in rescue the server stays in rescue; this is the picked shape and is not specified further.
10. **The rescue rekey where saved records exist.** The route also serves a machine missing from a stale sheet and a machine whose old seed or index is lost while its records remain. How the grant's entry is tied to the server on those routes is not specified; the approved-server binding covers only the case with no admissible saved history.
11. **CNF-117 cases still missing:** an approval rendered on Replace's or a session's card refused for this flow; a vendor call outside the grant refused at dispatch; the flow refused under a binding, a command hold or a standing destructive disposition; a restart after the root-label stop.

Four independent readings in one pass (a fifth seat was unavailable). This record makes no normative edit.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
**Queued, 2026-11-05: points from the rescue-call grant readings, not yet recorded** (raised by the readings behind comment 153000001; none is decided by the text in #89, and they join comments 155000001 and 156000001).

12. **Key deregistration.** The grant registers the machine's fresh-seed client key in the Robot account's key listing and holds no call that removes a registered key. Whether and when the flow, or anything else, deregisters it is not specified (2 of 4 readers).
13. **The relay pass a fresh seed needs.** `STA-22b` says "Replace's machine-migration and new-relay-pass allocations wait for its fresh seed's record". The rescue rekey also moves to a fresh seed, and its text does not say whether a relay pass under that seed is needed or how it is obtained (1 reader).
14. **CNF-117 refusal cases.** CNF-117 has no case refusing the flow's call on another machine, a call outside the grant, or a call under a standing destructive disposition (1 reader; overlaps point 11).
15. **`STA-24`'s reset-race rationale.** `STA-24` bounds a late reset by "key publication taking about 80 s after the reset (`CHN-R1`) and damage limited to disks already chosen for erasure". The rescue rekey's reset is non-destructive and chooses no disk for erasure, so that rationale does not bound a late rekey reset (1 reader).

This record makes no normative edit.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
**Owner picks, 2026-11-05: "One scoped read", "Still offered" and "Yes, hold the card clause"** (open points 1, 7 and 9 of comments 155000001 and 156000001: the host-key read after the root-label stop, the kept reset back across a restart, and a failure or operator stop in rescue).

**Point 1, "One scoped read".** After the root-label stop, one read-only job reads one root's installed host keys. They serve only this one reset back: its `STA-20b` prerequisite and its `STG-4` confirmation. They are never an installed pin or a machine pin, and are never trusted for later contact. The job writes nothing, follows no symlink and does not replay the file system's journal. It refuses, and no reset is sent, when the keys are missing, when keys are found under more than one root, or when a key matches one of rescue's own. A reset without pins stays excluded (`STA-20b`).
Four independent readings (a fifth seat was unavailable): 4 favoured the scoped read, 0 no read, 0 a reset without pins. On whether the text forces an answer, 0 of 4 found it forced.

**Point 7, "Still offered".** The reset back kept after the root-label stop survives a harness restart. It is shown again and rechecked against its prerequisites, and a reset whose intent is already journaled as sent is never sent again.
Four independent readings: 3 favoured "still offered", 1 that a restart ends it. On whether the text forces an answer, 0 of 4 found it forced.

**Point 9, "Yes, hold the card clause".** After any other failure or an operator stop in rescue, the grant ends, and the screen shows that the server is in rescue, the unfinished flow and every unresolved call; the operator acts at Robot. What a new approval for this server does is not decided here and waits for open point 6.
Four independent readings: 4 favoured this shape. On whether the text forces an answer, 2 found it partly forced and 2 not forced.

Text work: in the rescue rekey's text change. Nothing is enabled.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Points 3 and 6 of 156000001 and 155000001, accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule (four of four agree: accept).

Point 3 (an entry made by a wrong pick): "A wrong-server record". The operator alone MAY record that an entry the rescue rekey's card created names the wrong server; it is refused while a session binds the machine, and a failed append records nothing. It ends any of the flow's grant still standing as an operator stop does and bars the entry for good: no session binding, re-entry, association, retry, job, acceptance, relabel, reinstall, abandonment or vendor call other than the reads that resolve its unresolved calls, and no disposition's continuation revives one. It is neither Failed nor a disposition and proves nothing about what was sent; the entry keeps its index, mapping and history, unresolved calls stay behind STA-24's barrier, and the record survives export and Restore. The screen lists what was not undone on that server. The intended server takes a new card and a new entry at a new index. Counts: 4 for, 0 against; forced 0 of 4. Narrowings named: it is permanent and rests on the operator's word alone, and it can leave a server armed or in rescue, cleaned up at Robot.

Point 6 (a card naming a server another entry holds): "Refuse by the existing comparison". The rescue rekey's card is refused, the conflicting entry shown, when admitting its server number for the new entry meets a refusal of Protected browser evidence v1 §3a's admission checks against any entry the journal holds, whatever that entry's state or account reference; the refused approval journals and reserves nothing. This opens no route for a server an entry already holds: such a server is rekeyed, if at all, against that entry, and how is not decided. Counts: 4 for, 0 against; forced 2 partly, 2 no. Narrowings named: STA-15's "On Robot the ceremony always works" is narrowed further than 154000001 did, since no card is approved for a server another entry holds; the refusal is permanent in that journal, since entries are never removed.

With point 6 settled, point 9's open clause reads: a new card of the flow naming that server is refused.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Batch panel on the unvoted rescue-rekey points (base a5f1853), accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule. Four readers answered; the fifth was a missing seat, so 3 of 4 settles.

Accepted:
- Harm to the wrong server: the card says approving resets that server into rescue and writes the harness's key to a root, and is approved only once the operator enters the server number (4 of 4).
- Activation left armed: the stop screen starts at the rescue activation's intent, shows the activation possibly armed, and the operator deactivates it at Robot; no deactivation call (4 of 4).
- Symbolic link and false confirmation in ready_to_reset: it follows no symbolic link, and the reset into the installed system is not offered when a key it read shares a fingerprint with the rescue boot's pin (3 of 4). This applies to every reset ready_to_reset offers.
- More than one root labelled in the harness's form: the root-label stop (3 of 4). Narrows STA-15's "On Robot the ceremony always works" by that case.
- A root the scoped read cannot read: it refuses (3 of 4).
- Reads after the grant ends: the reads that resolve an unresolved call stay permitted after any end of the grant (3 of 4).
- alias_unavailable: the card is refused, with the risk records shown, when its admission would record quarantined/alias_unavailable (3 of 4). Narrows STA-15's "On Robot the ceremony always works" by that case.
- Sheet member for the wrong-server record: kept open for the format work (4 of 4).
- Routes with saved records: kept open (4 of 4).
- Relay pass: a pass under the fresh seed is needed and its allocation waits for that seed's ceremony record; how the flow obtains it and records the destination stays open (3 of 4).
- Key deregistration: the key stays registered, the screen names it, the operator removes it at Robot; no new call (4 of 4).
- Credential versus account: kept open (3 of 4).
- Only public host keys: ready_to_reset and the scoped read read no private key file and refuse a file holding anything but one public key (3 of 4).
- Missing conformance cases: approval from Replace's or a session's card, a call outside the grant, a call naming another server, and the flow under a binding, a command hold or a standing destructive disposition (4 of 4).

Not settled under the rule, going to the owner: binding after other stops, restart before the root-label stop, the success path's host-key read, the card recheck at dispatch, an older sheet reviving a barred entry, Replace and the sheet's states for a barred entry, the scoped read's disposal and later comparisons, and the reset-race rationale.
