comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Re-panel, 2026-11-05, of two rescue rekey points with facts the earlier panel lacked. Four readers; one seat missing.

1. The alias_unavailable card refusal (160000001), with its scope stated: under protected-evidence-v1 §3a a risk attributed to an entry excludes every different entry in the global VendorMachine literal namespace and no current predicate discharges it, so once the journal holds one unavailable-identity risk record of any entry, every later card of the flow is refused. Accepted 4 of 4: keep the refusal as merged. It narrows STA-15's "On Robot the ceremony always works" for every later card once any such risk record exists, permanently in that journal; 160000001 named the narrowing, and this names its reach. CNF-117 (p) gains a case with only a risk record under another account reference.

2. A ready_to_reset read sharing a fingerprint with the rescue boot's pin. Accepted 4 of 4: the read is refused before its keys are journaled as pins; it is no pin and no prerequisite read, the operator is told before reboot, and a later read may still make the offer under every STA-20b prerequisite. ARC-43 journals no pin of such a read; TauWeb.Pins carries no such refusal, which is Markdown-only. Not decided: whether the refused read's fingerprints are kept as an observation.

The brief attributed "no source replaces an active installed pin" to CNF-86; that sentence is in CNF-109, and its rule holds.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text: Owner pick, 2026-11-05, on a sheet exported before the rescue rekey's wrong-server record was appended (part R, point 1): name the limit. A restored sheet is knowledge as of export, so a Restore from such a sheet alone brings the entry back without the bar; this is stated as a known limit, and the record's screen tells the operator to export a new sheet. Not selected: making the record irreversible across sheets (no reader picked it, and the readers found no source outside the sheet that holds the bar), or leaving it not decided. The panel was tied 2-2 (name the limit; leave it not decided), so the point went to the owner. Drafted in STA-17 and CNF-117 (m).

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text: Owner pick, 2026-11-05, on how a Replace and the sheet's list of machine states treat an entry the rescue rekey's wrong-server record bars (part R, point 3): leave it not decided (R3C). STA-17's "is not decided" sentence stays and no rule is added. The question was put as whether a Replace may report complete while a key under the old seed may still sit on the barred server; the readers who chose a rule agreed on skipping the entry, listing it as barred and carrying the bar, and differed only on completion. Not selected: skip and list as barred (R3A), skip, list as barred, carry the bar and never report complete while a key is possibly written (merged reader option), or refusing to complete while the entry has calls unresolved (R3B). Panel count: 2 for leaving it not decided, 1 for R3A, 1 for the merged option; no majority, so the point went to the owner.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text: Owner pick, 2026-11-05, on the rescue rekey's scoped host-key read after its reset back (part R, point 4): keep it and read it only to withhold (a reader's merged option). The scoped read is kept in the journal with the entry for the entry's lifetime, as a record as of that read. It is never a pin and never exported. A later comparison reads it only to withhold, as one of STA-20b's earlier installations' records, and a key matching it is not accepted or trusted for that match. Since SEC-5 row 5 says it is not exported, a Restore loses it as an input that withholds, and the text names that. Not selected: keeping it and letting no later comparison read it (R4A), letting a later comparison read it to refuse on a mismatch (R4B), or leaving both not decided (R4C). Panel count: 2 for R4A, 1 for the merged option, 1 for R4C; the reader backing the merged option was in the minority, so the point went to the owner, who chose the merged option. Drafted in STA-17 (the heading now reads "never trusted later to accept a key or make a connection", with no rule weakened), SEC-5 row 5's disposal cell and CNF-117.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text: Owner pick, 2026-11-05, on a late reset of the rescue rekey (part R, point 9): name the flow's bound and both writes it can interrupt (a readers' merged option). STA-24's reset-race rationale now says the rescue rekey (STA-17) chooses no disk for erasure, and a late reset of that flow reboots its one server into rescue or its installed system and erases nothing; key publication still takes about 80 s after the reset (CHN-R1). It names the two writes such a reset can interrupt, rescue_install_key's line in one root's authorized_keys and replace_root_label's label write, each covered by its own rules in STA-17: the relabel waits for a login with the new client key, and the label is confirmed only by a harness-composed read. For the key write, "erases nothing" holds only if an interrupted write keeps the file's other lines; STA-17 says the job adds the key "keeping every other line", and whether that holds under interruption is stated as not decided. No new MUST. Panel count: 2 for the merged option, 1 for R9B, 1 for R9C; no majority, so the point went to the owner, who was shown both writes and the caveat on the key write and chose the merged option. Drafted in STA-24.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text: Review pass on the R batch (PR 100), 2026-11-05: fixes applied, no new pick. R9's text named two writes a late reset of the rescue rekey can interrupt; STA-17 also gives the flow an old-key removal from the same authorized_keys after the confirmed readback. The text now says the writes "include" all three, gives the removal the same not-decided condition as the key write (STA-17 says it "keeps the new key and unrelated authorizations"; whether that holds under interruption is not decided), and quotes ADR-0056's open point that relabelling the mounted root safely "still needs implementation evidence". This widens the owner's R9 pick by one named write and one cited open point; it settles nothing and adds no MUST, and is flagged for the owner. Also from the pass: the R9 paragraph moved after the reset-race rationale; the ~80 s publication bound is stated for a reset into rescue only; STA-17's label confirmation is quoted; STA-20b's withholding duty now names STA-17's scoped host-key read, with that comparison listed as Markdown-only in STA-20b and the offersReset docstring (implements the R4 pick; no theorem changes); CNF-117's later-reinstall case states its setup.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Panel on six unvoted rescue rekey findings, part G (base e28bea5), accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule. Four readers answered; the fifth was a missing seat, so 3 of 4 settles.

- G2, SEC-5 row 3's disposal cell: point to STA-17 without listing (3 of 4). The cell now reads "Removed from the machine by Replace's migration (STA-17), which is a new seed; STA-17 names the cases where it stays", keeping the jump host clause. The brief's "except where STA-17 says otherwise" was reworded because it would read as an unquoted citation. Narrowing: none.
- G3, STA-22b's retired-seed list and a barred entry: recorded as part of 167000001's open point (3 of 4). STA-17's "is not decided" sentence now also covers whether the journal and the new seed's sheet keep the entry and its record through a Replace. No rule. Narrowing: none.
- G4, host-key bytes or fingerprints: fingerprints only (3 of 4). SEC-5 row 5 now says each key is kept as its {family, fingerprint} with no key bytes, in the journal and in the job records of ready_to_reset and the scoped read; ARC-43 and STA-17 point at it, and CNF-117 checks it. The brief's option said "in the journal and the sheet"; the accepted form keeps the scoped read journal-only, as 168000001 and SEC-5 row 5 require. Owner picks narrowed: none.
- G6, the fingerprints of a refused ready_to_reset read: left not decided, no text (3 of 4).

Not settled: G1 (what counts as one root on RAID, LVM or encryption; 2 for naming it not decided, 1 for failing closed, 1 for a stricter fail-closed variant) and G5 (the relay pass's server destination; tied 2-2 between "already covered" and widening the not-decided sentence). Both go to the owner.

For the owner, not text: a Replace that dropped a barred entry would lose the alias_unavailable card refusal for that server and the screen's not-undone list, a second known limit beside 166000001's.

Raised by readers, not voted:
1. "The host-pin fingerprint format" (credential-format-v1) is defined nowhere normative.
2. rescue_install_key has no outcome for a label probe it cannot resolve: with one root labelled and another device's probe failing, it writes the key.
3. The relay pass's Robot destination is as unstated as the server's, and the server address's source is unstated on the ordinary STG-4 path too.
4. "Observation" is used in two senses: STA-20b's copies of job records and CHN-R7's publication observations.
5. The rescue boot may already have assembled volumes; what counts as a root also decides what the label read enumerates.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Review pass on the part G batch (PR 103), 2026-11-05: fixes applied, no new pick.

- G4: the first draft said the journal's copies of the two jobs' records hold no key bytes, but no rule made the jobs' output carry none. ready_to_reset (ARC-43) and rescue_host_key_read (STA-17) now each say their captured output carries each key they read as its {family, fingerprint} and no key bytes, which is the option's "the two jobs journal the fingerprints of the public keys they read and no key bytes" and matches the install brief's "derives the fingerprints and journals them as pins". SEC-5 row 5 now names "the journal's copies" of those job records, not the records on the machine, and points at ARC-43 and STA-17 for the duty. - G2: the cell reads "Removed from the machine by Replace's migration (Replace is a new seed), except where it stays under STA-17", which fixes the "which is a new seed" antecedent and makes no attribution to STA-17 without a quote.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Review of the G1B sentence (comment 173000001), one pass, two readers.

- Placement: both readers said the sentence, ending the root-label stop paragraph, reads as a note on rescue_install_key alone. It now names both jobs: "For this job and for rescue_host_key_read below, ...", which is the decision's own scope, the rescue rekey's jobs. Nothing narrowed.
- Wording: one reader found that "a layout other than one file system on one disk" read literally covers the whole server, so the harness's own install (an EFI partition beside the root) and the conformance cases that count roots would fall under "not decided". comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Follow-up to comment 175000001, on its "for the owner, not text" point: settled by the owner's 2026-11-05 G1 answer, whose question named mirrored, LVM or encrypted.

- The G1 question read "When a server's disk is mirrored, LVM or encrypted, what does the rescue key job do?" and the owner answered "Leave it open". So a root under LVM or encryption on one disk is open as well, and the widening is not an owner question.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Part H panel (the five unvoted findings of 171000001 and its known-limit flag), read at 912da40. Four readers answered; the fifth was a missing seat, so 3 of 4 settles. H2, H3, H5 and H6 are accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule. H1's home and H4 go to the owner.

Accepted:
- H2, an unresolved label probe in rescue_install_key (4 of 4): it is the root-label stop. STA-17 now reads "If it finds none, or more than one, or a label probe it makes of a device it reads as a possible root does not resolve, which is the root-label stop, the job writes no key ...". The reset back stays, under the stop's existing words and the reset's own prerequisites; the scoped read still refuses "when it cannot read a root". Which devices are read as a possible root is left to G1B's open point, so the harness's own BIOS-boot partition, which has no file system, is not made a stop by this pick. The "So with no sheet" sentence in STA-17 and STA-15's sheet exception add "a possible root whose label the ... cannot read", and CNF-117 (l) gains the case. Narrowing, named: STA-15's "On Robot the ceremony always works" is narrowed by the unresolved-probe case, as 154000001 and 160000001 narrowed it. G1B is not narrowed.
- H3, the relay pass's Robot destination (4 of 4): no text. STA-17's "How the flow obtains that pass and records its destinations is not decided" already covers it under G5B (174000001), since "its destinations" is the pass's and plural. The ordinary dedicated path's missing source for the server address becomes its own item, tw-kx8, which names STA-17's sentence as depending on it and decides nothing for the rescue rekey.
- H5, volumes the rescue boot already assembled (3 of 4): the G1B paragraph adds "What either job reads where the rescue boot has already assembled or activated a volume is not decided either." No rule; it chooses neither the assembled volume nor its member devices. Widening, named: G1B (173000001, 175000001, 176000001) is widened by the assembled-volume case. Nothing is narrowed.
- H6, a Replace that drops a barred entry (4 of 4): no text; this note joins 167000001's open point. If a Replace drops the barred entry, what it may lose is the §3a conflict refusal (checked "against any entry the journal holds"), the screen's not-undone list (each item shown "only when the journal holds the intent"), and the scoped read's withholding, which is "kept in the journal with the entry for the entry's lifetime". The alias_unavailable refusal is not shown to be lost: a risk record is attributed through the risk ledger, and "A risk attributed to an entry excludes every different entry", so whether a dropped entry takes such a record with it cannot be told from the text. This decides neither retention nor how a Replace completes.

To the owner:
- H1, the host-pin fingerprint format: 3 of 4 define it once (SHA-256 over the SSH public-key blob, standard base64 unpadded, no `SHA256:` prefix); 1 of 4 names the encoding as not decided. The readers who define it split on its home: 2 put it in the credential format document, with CHN-R1 pointing there, and 1 puts it in CHN-R1, with the format document pointing there. The home is not settled, so no text yet.
- H4, two senses of "observation": 3 of 4 add a CONTEXT.md entry that changes no comparison; 1 of 4 says the uses are already consistent and need nothing. The required reader is in the minority, so it is not settled.

Unvoted findings from this panel, for a later batch:
- rescue_host_key_read "writes nothing to any disk" and CNF-117 (l) checks every disk's bytes before and after, but the rescue boot's own RAID assembly or resync may write to the disks while the job runs.
- rescue_install_key's label read is not said to be journaled with the ordinal it saw, while ADR-0056's acceptance relies on "the label"; whether the acceptance reads the job's captured output or a second read is not stated.
- rescue_install_key adds the key to "that root's authorized_keys", but "follows no symbolic link" is said only of the scoped read; whether the key-writing job refuses a link that leaves the root is not stated.
- How the operator's Robot credential is matched to the approved entry's account reference before calls stays open (already in an earlier record of this bead).

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Follow-up to 177000001: the owner's 2026-11-05 picks for H1's home and H4.

- H1, the host-pin fingerprint format: the owner's 2026-11-05 pick puts its home in `CHN-R1`. The definition was 3 of 4 with the required reader in the majority (1 of 4 named the encoding as not decided); the home split 2 for the credential format document against 1 for `CHN-R1`, and the owner chose `CHN-R1`. `CHN-R1` now reads "Every host-key fingerprint the harness records or compares, on every route and in the journal, a job's output and the sheet, is the SHA-256 of the key's SSH public-key blob, written in standard base64 without padding and without the `SHA256:` prefix: the host-pin fingerprint format." The MD5 colon fingerprints Robot's `authorized_key[]` takes are kept apart: they "name client keys, not host keys, and are not in the host-pin fingerprint format". The credential format document's line now reads "`fingerprint` uses the host-pin fingerprint format, which `CHN-R1` defines". It grants no new source, contact or capability, and narrows no earlier pick; as the owner asked, it is worded for every route, the journal, job output and the sheet, not only Robot's publication.
- H4, two senses of "observation": the owner's 2026-11-05 pick is H4C (3 of 4; 1 of 4 said the uses were already consistent). `CONTEXT.md`'s flagged ambiguities gain an "Observation" entry naming a machine's word over the notify channel, a copied job record (`STA-20b`'s "advisory observations") and a publication reading. It changes no requirement and no comparison's scope: `CHN-R7`'s "any observation or installed-system pin from any source in any earlier installation of that machine" keeps its breadth, the entry does not say whether `STA-20b`'s copies are among those observations, and `STA-20b`'s "earlier installations' records are read only to withhold it" stands.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Follow-up to 177000001 and 178000001: one review pass on the part H branch, fixes applied.

- The restatements of the unresolved-probe case now use the rule's own words. STA-15's sheet exception and STA-17's "So with no sheet" sentence read "a possible root whose label probe does not resolve" in place of "a possible root whose label the ... cannot read".
- STA-17's open points add "nor is what makes a label probe resolve". The operator's install brief says when a probe resolves for the install; STA-17 adopts no definition for the harness's job, so this stays open and adds no rule.
- The recovery figure's note no longer restates one condition; with no sheet, "that route has the root-label limits `STA-15` names".
- `CHN-R1`'s sentence reads "on every route and in the journal, in a job's output and in the sheet" (a grammar fix; the meaning is unchanged).
- The `CONTEXT.md` entry reads "is used in several senses, among them these", because the word has other uses (box-plane output, `STA-24`'s evidence, a label's as-of reading) that the entry does not list.
- Correction: the case the earlier records place in CNF-117 (l) is in its sub-item (p).

For a later batch, not text: `tools/check_fixtures.py` accepts an optional `SHA256:` prefix on a JSON `fingerprint` field, so a host-key example that breaks `CHN-R1`'s format would pass. No example in the repository has such a field today.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Part I panel (the five unvoted findings of 177000001 and 179000001), read at 4f3b8d9. Four readers answered; the fifth was a missing seat, so 3 of 4 settles only with the required reader in the majority. I2's core, I3 and I5 are accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule. I1, I2's journaling clause and I4's home go to the owner.

Accepted:
- I2B, which read the ordinal acceptance relies on (4 of 4): `STA-17`'s acceptance paragraph names as not decided which admissible captured observation of the root's label the proposed ordinal is read from, `rescue_install_key`'s own read or a later harness-composed read, and points at `ARC-43` ("These reads take their values from the job record's captured output"). No rule. Narrowing of the option, named: its second clause, "and how it is journaled", is not written. 3 of 4 picked the option's full wording; the required reader picked it without that clause, saying the journaling is already covered, so that clause is not settled and goes to the owner. Nothing in ADR-0056, G1B, H5 or G5B is narrowed or widened.
- I3A, symbolic links in `rescue_install_key`'s write (3 of 4, the required reader in the majority; 1 of 4 picked I3B, naming it as not decided): `STA-17` now says that writing the key the job follows no symbolic link and writes no file outside that root; it refuses a path to `authorized_keys` that is a symbolic link or passes through one, and then writes no key. All three readers in the majority make that refusal a failure of the flow, so the grant ends on it (`SEC-4`'s "on a failure other than `STA-17`'s root-label stop"), not the root-label stop: the reset back is not kept. `SEC-4` is unchanged. `CNF-117` (l) gains the case. Narrowing, named: `STA-15`'s "On Robot the ceremony always works" and `STA-17`'s "So with no sheet" sentence are narrowed by a root whose `authorized_keys` path is or passes through a symbolic link, as 154000001, 160000001 and 177000001 narrowed them for their cases; the no-sheet route loses that server too. No pick of G1B, H5 or G5B is touched, and the root-label stop is not widened.
- I5A, the fixture gate's `SHA256:` prefix (4 of 4): `tools/check_fixtures.py` drops `(?:SHA256:)?`, its docstring and finding name Robot's MD5 colon-hex client-key fingerprint and the host-pin fingerprint format (`CHN-R1`), and its limits say the check keys on the member name, so it would also refuse a prefixed SHA-256 fingerprint of a key that is not a host key, and it does not tell a host field holding MD5 colon-hex from a client one. `tools/check-controls.sh` updates the existing control's expected finding and adds a negative control with a prefixed value and a stays-green control with the same value unprefixed. No field the gate scans has a fingerprint member today, so it refuses nothing now. It implements 178000001's H1 pick and narrows no requirement.

To the owner:
- I1, the rescue boot's own writes during `rescue_host_key_read`: 2 of 4 picked I1C (name what the rescue boot itself writes while either job runs as not decided, a widening of H5), 1 of 4 picked I1A (already covered), and the required reader picked part of I1B (state in `CNF-117` (l) that its roots are one file system on one disk with no volume layer and no assembled volume, with no change to the job sentence). No option has a majority.
- I2's journaling clause: whether the I2B sentence also names as not decided how the read the acceptance relies on is journaled (3 of 4 yes; the required reader no, as already covered).
- I4, the credential and the entry's account reference: 4 of 4 picked I4A (name as not decided how the flow ties the credential it calls under to the entry's account reference; no rule), but the home splits 2 for `STA-17` (beside "Every call of the flow is checked against that entry") and 2 for `SEC-4` (beside "it is checked at dispatch"). The tie goes to the owner; no text yet.

Unvoted findings from this panel, for a later batch:
- `STG-20` says "the harness reads the label only for `STA-17`'s root-label stop in the rescue rekey", while `STA-17` also reads the label for the readbacks and the acceptance's observed `a-7`.
- `rescue_install_key` has no bound on what else it writes, and its write needs a read-write mount, which on a journaling file system replays the journal; only the read job's mount is specified, and only it has a byte-equality case.
- The write's target is not named beyond "that root's `authorized_keys`": which account's file, what the job does when the file or its directory is missing, and the mode and owner of anything it creates.
- The fixture gate accepts Robot's MD5 colon-hex in a host-key fingerprint member, though `CHN-R1` says those fingerprints "name client keys, not host keys".

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Review of the part I text (180000001), one pass, two readers. One found nothing; the other found one should-fix and three nits. None was blocking.

Applied:
- The recovery figure's caption said that with no sheet the rescue route "has the root-label limits `STA-15` names". `STA-15` now also names a labelled root whose `authorized_keys` path is or passes through a symbolic link, which is not a root-label limit, so the caption now reads "has the limits `STA-15` names". comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
Owner picks on the three open tw-4mz part I points (180000001). Counts only.

I1 (the volume-layer boundary for the rescue jobs): the owner picked I1C together with the
I1X part of I1B. The panel had split 2 of 4 for I1C, 1 for I1A and 1 for I1B's I1X part, so it
went to the owner. Applied:
- STA-17's not-decided sentence now also leaves open what the rescue boot itself writes to a
  disk while `rescue_install_key` or `rescue_host_key_read` runs. This widens the open set of

title: Decide whether the lost-key revocation report is offered while the placement's reference is already armed
description:
tw-i55's owner decision (comment 47000001, kept by the need review 81000001) selects a per-placement operator report that a lost application key was revoked at its service. The act ends that placement's required-reference wait and live listing and moves it to operator-reported history. The decision is for the bead's lost-key case and leaves this open: "offering it while a reference is already armed, report correction/withdrawal and rotation's older-output treatment remain separate questions."

**Question.** Is the report offered for a placement whose reference is already armed (by `digest_secret` or the local paste), where no `ARC-43` wait stands?

- If yes: what does it end for an armed reference? Ending the reference also ends the scan for that value, so later output loses that placement's coverage while the key may still sit on the machine.
- If no: the card offers the act only while that placement's required reference is unarmed, and an armed reference keeps its scan until rotation or destruction ends it.

Constraints that hold either way (comment 47000001): the report is per placement instance and clears no other placement, including one holding the same bytes; it lifts no `STA-20` or `STA-24` restriction and authorizes no retry; previously withheld output stays withheld; no raw value, digest or scan key enters history or export.

Depends on tw-i55's text landing first. Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.
close_reason: Decided and specified; see the closing comments and ADR-0062

The owner's 2026-11-05 tracker pick keeps this bead and tw-e42 and closes tw-c85 as their
duplicate. tw-c85's extra background and constraints are carried here and on tw-e42.

**Where the open point sits in the text now.** `ARC-43` (01-architecture.md, "An operator report

comments.text:
## Panel pick — the report is offered only while the placement's reference is unarmed, 2026-11-05

The question: is the operator's lost-key report (`ARC-43`) offered for a placement whose reference is already armed, by `digest_secret` or the local paste, where no `ARC-43` wait stands? `ARC-43` said: "Whether the report is offered while the placement's reference is armed, and whether a report can be corrected or withdrawn, are not yet specified."

The pick is "only while unarmed":

- **When it is offered.** The card offers the report only while that placement's required reference is unarmed, so the `ARC-43` `exec` wait stands for it. The condition is "unarmed", not "lost-key": the harness tests whether the reference is armed.
- **When the state is read.** The state is read at the report's journal act. A re-arm journaled first refuses the report. A paste or digest record after the report arms nothing, as `ARC-43` already says.
- **An armed reference keeps its scan.** It keeps it until rotation, destruction or local-store loss ends it. If the reference later becomes unarmed, for example after a store loss, the report is offered again.
- **What an operator does about a key revoked while its reference is armed.** No report. The routes are rotation through `ARC-17`'s placement gates, or destruction. Model `exec` does not wait on an armed reference, so those routes can be reached.
- **Unchanged.**
  - The report's effect, its scan boundary in `SEC-5`, and the version-7 sheet.
  - The tw-huu `reference_ended` mark, `CNF-84` and ADR-0061's "A placement whose report already ended its reference loses nothing more at its rotation".

**The counts.** Four independent readers answered; a fifth seat was unavailable. Three recommended this option and one recommended offering the report while armed, as the same act. The majority includes the reader the rule requires. All four said the text forces neither option. All four said the mark stays as written. Accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule, 3 of 4.

**Narrowing.** This pick narrows `ARC-43`'s unconditioned sentence "After revoking a placement's key at its service, the operator may report that one placement revoked" to placements whose reference is unarmed. It narrows no owner pick: comment 47000001 decided the report "for the bead's lost-key case" and left the armed case open. It widens nothing.

**The minority's strongest argument.** A service revocation is the same fact whatever the local arming state. A rotation ends the old scan too, so keeping the scan holds only until the operator's next act, and a dead key stays listed live if the operator takes none. Bead tw-foh, whether output after a rotation is still compared against the old value, touches that last point.

**Not selected:**
- Offering the report while armed, as the same act.
- Offering it while armed with a different warning.

This pick is settled and must not be re-asked. It makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Remove ARC-25a's signature-lowering command filter
description:
Owner direction, 2026-11-04: "Remove the whole filter feature. This is too brittle."

The owner chose this after being told that the filter is a text tripwire that other forms evade and that also refuses harmless text. It knowingly amends an existing requirement.

## Scope

- the `SigLevel` / `LocalFileSigLevel` / `RemoteFileSigLevel` text match and its two forms, `signature_level_never` and `untrusted_repository`;

- `CNF-67`'s fixtures for the filter's outcomes;
- the sentences in ADR-0002's 2026-10-27 amendment that describe the filter.

- Beside **unpinned**, the display states that unsigned local package files are permitted and that free shell can lower checking or install unsigned code without refusal.
- Neither persistent signature enforcement nor universal unsigned-package refusal is guaranteed.
- `CNF-67` stays BLOCKING: both pinned distributions, the build-time key check and the native-policy run are unchanged.

## Reach

- On `tw-l1l`, the filter effects named in comments 18000001, 38000001, 44000001 and 59000001 and in the ready brief 70000001 have nothing left to apply (comment 74000001). That includes the ambiguous-legacy-history decision's "Apply the existing ARC-25a command filter to every machine that could be the origin of the unpinned history". Nothing else in those records changes: the per-machine history, the explicit unknown naming every possible origin, and its disclosure and restatement.
- No Lean theorem, witness, control script or gated capability names the filter.
- The open question in `TASKS.md`, whether `ARC-25` governs a later session's package fetches on an unpinned machine, stays open.

title: CI runs specification gates twice per PR push: limit push to main
description:
## Problem
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (workflow `gates`) triggers on `push:` for every branch and on `pull_request:`. Every push to a PR branch therefore runs "specification gates" twice on the same commit: once as `push`, once as `pull_request`. Example: PR #55's tip `fb07ac2` ran as 41775539514 (push) and 41775543723 (pull_request). Each run takes about half an hour of runner time and doubles the checks a reviewer has to read.

## Change
Limit `push` to `main`; keep `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` unchanged:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
```

No job, step or gate changes. `.github/workflows/candidate-order.yml` is not touched.

## Paths that must keep their gates
- A PR from a branch in this repository: one `pull_request` run per pushed tip.
- `main` after a merge: one `push` run.
- The `proposals/candidate-order` branch: `propose_candidates.py` pushes it with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which starts no `push` run, so its gates come only from the `pull_request` event on its PR (runs show `action_required` until the publisher approves them, as the workflow comment describes). Limiting `push` leaves that path as it is.
- Any other branch without a PR: `workflow_dispatch` by hand.

## Acceptance
- The PR for this change gets exactly one "specification gates" run on its tip (event `pull_request`), and it succeeds.
- After merge, the `main` push gets exactly one run (event `push`).
- The proposal branch's past runs are all `pull_request`; nothing in the change alters that trigger.
close_reason: push limited to main in .github/workflows/ci.yml (a8ad109); pull_request and workflow_dispatch kept; ADR-0032 amended 2026-11-04, with the conflicted pull request case noted (9487bd7)

title: ARC-16's third rung at LNVPS has no form: a reinstall of the same machine, or a stop plus a new order
description:
`ARC-16` says "Recovery is a ladder." It continues: "Retry; then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy; then destroy the machine and restart under a different domain, which costs a server." Its diagram's note on the destroy reads "Never handed to another session." and "Costs a server." Stage 1 offers that rung: `STG-17` says "`ARC-16` says "then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy", and the harness **MUST NOT** use the candidate order as that rung: the first stage offers rungs one and three only, and says so."

LNVPS has no destroy route, and `ARC-22` gives destroy and recreate two different stand-ins there, which the third rung needs at once. `ARC-22` says "Where the harness would destroy a machine — an abandonment, or the old machine of a Replace rebuild — it stops that machine, turns automatic renewal off, and shows it as still existing and billed, with the vendor's stated deletion date, until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract." It also says "**Where the harness would recreate a machine** to re-run its first contact, a vendor-API reinstall of the same machine stands in and is a **new first contact**: the old pin does not authorize contact with the reinstalled system; `CHN-R7` governs the publication route and installed-pin retirement, while a different eligible source follows its own admission rule." The specification leaves undecided whether the successor reuses that machine through reinstall or receives a new order after the old machine is stopped.

What the choice touches:

- **Exposure.** `SEC-1` says "A model that has touched a machine counts as touching it until that machine is destroyed, because ending a session does not remove whatever the model may already have left behind." At LNVPS, destruction is the vendor's confirmed deletion: `SEC-5` row 12's "How it dies" cell reads "Machine destroyed (at LNVPS, the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop that stands in for a destroy, `ARC-22`), or operator rotates". `SEC-1` also says "Where a profile declares an independence bound, the recovery ladder's middle rung and re-entry stay inside this rule only while the configured model's **footprint** — every machine it has touched, and every machine co-bound with those — stays within that bound for the life of those machines; past that rung the machine is destroyed rather than handed on." and "Where no bound is declared, the footprint is counted and shown (`OVR-6`), and neither the rung nor a re-entry is refused for it." Stage 1's ad-hoc profile declares none: its "Independence bound" section reads "None declared."
- **A precedent.** On the dedicated path, where the server is rented rather than created, the bottom rung is already a reinstall: `STG-20` says "So the harness's response is `ARC-16`'s bottom rung applied to this path: if the installed system does not answer on the channel within `installed.wait_max` (`bundle/timing.toml`) of the reset that should have booted it, the session declares the install failed, tells the operator, and **offers a return to rescue and reinstallation from the brief** — the same ceremony, and cheap (about five minutes when it works)."
- **A new order's price.** Each LNVPS machine has its own account: `STG-21` says "Before the first order under each machine's identity, the typed LNVPS adapter MUST submit the operator's own email address to that account at the vendor." It continues: "LNVPS sends a single-use verification link valid for about a day; the operator opens it." A new order therefore needs a new per-machine identity (ADR-0042), a new verification and a new invoice, while the stopped machine stays shown as billed until its deletion date. `STG-18` says "Stage 1 buys one LNVPS machine by one invoice through the per-machine identity decided in ADR-0042."
- **Coverage.** No conformance item exercises `ARC-16`'s third rung at any vendor.

Options:

- **A — a reinstall of the same machine** under the successor session, as `ARC-22`'s recreate form: a new installation and a new first contact; the stuck model's footprint keeps the machine, counted and shown where no bound is declared; `ARC-16`'s "Never handed to another session" gains a qualifier; where a profile declares a bound, `SEC-1` already requires the destroy form (B).
- **B — a stop plus a new order**: `ARC-22`'s destroy form for the old machine, which stays shown as existing and billed until its deletion date and in the stuck model's footprint until the vendor's confirmed deletion, and a new order under a new identity for the successor session, with its own verification and invoice.
- **C — no third rung at LNVPS in stage 1**: amend `STG-17` to offer only rung one there; the operator abandons (`ARC-22`) and starts a new setup with the goal entered again.

Decide which form the third rung takes at LNVPS; whether it differs by declared bound; and whether a conformance item exercises it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] If A or B is chosen, `ARC-16` or `ARC-22` (or both) states the third rung's form at LNVPS, and whether it differs where a profile declares an independence bound. If C is chosen, `STG-17` is amended to offer only rung one at LNVPS in stage 1. `ARC-16` says "Retry; then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy; then destroy the machine and restart under a different domain, which costs a server."
- [ ] `STG-17` says what stage 1 offers at LNVPS. Today it says "`ARC-16` says "then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy", and the harness **MUST NOT** use the candidate order as that rung: the first stage offers rungs one and three only, and says so."
- [ ] Every sentence the decision makes false is amended in the same change: `ARC-16`'s diagram notes "Never handed to another session." and "Costs a server.", and `SEC-1`'s "Where no bound is declared, the footprint is counted and shown (`OVR-6`), and neither the rung nor a re-entry is refused for it."
- [ ] If A or B is chosen, a `CNF` item exercises the third rung at LNVPS, or the stage applicability table says why none is owed. If C is chosen, the stage applicability table records why no third-rung exercise is owed at LNVPS in stage 1.
- [ ] Once on main, twr-qso in tau-web-rust can close.
close_reason: Specified the LNVPS in-setup replacement rung (B+E) at ARC-16/ARC-22: stop the old machine and turn its renewal off, finish its terminal reconciliation, then order a distinct approved entry; the setup finishes when the replacement is delivered, and the opening screen keeps each outstanding stopped machine of a finished setup shown as existing and billed until deletion is confirmed. Added one operator-started, model-free deletion check to SEC-4 (STG-21a deletion reads only, under the stopped machine's own key, gated by T44) and to SEC-5 row 1, named at ARC-21 and ARC-22. STA-17 keeps Replace incomplete until the old machine's deletion is recorded, and SEC-4 grants Replace's flow the old machine's stop and renewal-off in STA-17's order; whether the read confirming that renewal-off is inside the grant is named open. CNF-20 gains Replace's cases, and the in-setup order's row replaces completion B and the dedicated reader with completion on arrival and the check. ADR-0053 records it. Specified, not enabled; runtime remains outstanding.

## Owner decision — stage-1 LNVPS recovery rung, 2026-11-02

Selected C: when a stage-1 LNVPS machine stays stuck after retry, stage 1 offers no in-setup third rung. The operator may abandon. Starting a new setup is a separate start with its own goal and approvals, not a successor action in the old setup. Stage 1 keeps one machine on one invoice.

Do not offer same-machine reinstall under a successor as this rung, stop-and-order within the setup, or an in-setup replacement order after waiting for deletion. The existing independent reinstall and recovery operations are not generally withdrawn by this choice; the amendment is scoped to stage 1's in-setup third rung at LNVPS. It does not decide the LNVPS rung's form for later stages or change the dedicated path's existing recovery ceremony.

Abandonment keeps its existing authorization, uncertainty and vendor-operation rules. At LNVPS a stop and renewal-off do not establish deletion or billing cessation. The old machine stays shown as existing and billed until the admitted deletion evidence is durably recorded. A new setup does not erase the old setup, consumed identities, model exposure, unresolved outcomes, retained restrictions or identity exclusions, and supplies no authority to contact or act on the old machine.

The bounded stage-1 amendment belongs in STG-17's offered-rung statement and its related stage-scope/conformance presentation. Keep ARC-16/ARC-22's owners and the stage-1 one-invoice scope coordinated through pointers and checked quotations; update affected attributions, including ADR-0033's existing quotation, when the rule changes. Do not remove or redefine the general ladder or its later-stage question by implication. The decision does not create a new acceptance act or decide tw-l1l's remaining timing, outside-session acceptor or history questions.

Required distinguishing cases: a stuck stage-1 machine after retry offers no in-setup third-rung successor, reinstall or second order; the authorized abandonment flow remains useful and keeps honest billing/deletion/uncertainty displays; a separately started setup uses its own goal and approvals and confers no renewed authority on the predecessor. Record why no stage-1 LNVPS third-rung exercise is owed in the conformance applicability owner without claiming later-stage admission or withdrawing unrelated reinstall cases.

This owner choice is settled. The LNVPS rung form for later stages remains queued. This record claims neither implementation nor closure of that remaining question.

## Technical settlement — later-stage LNVPS recovery mechanics, 2026-11-03

The independent readings agree on the following existing technical boundaries and none calls these an amendment. They do not select a later-stage recovery form or a new sequencing restriction. Stage-1 C remains settled: no stage-1 in-setup third rung, with abandonment and a separately approved new setup remaining distinct.

A stop and automatic-renewal-off are not confirmed deletion or billing cessation. The old machine remains shown as existing and billed, and its exposure and destruction-bound secret duties remain, until the admitted deletion evidence is durably recorded. A scheduled deletion date and operator disposition establish no deletion. The admitted evidence boundary carries its existing vendor-risk qualification; it is not proof of irreversible physical destruction or a new post-confirmation reappearance guarantee.

A same-machine reinstall opens a new installation at dispatch, retires its old installed pin and requires the new first-contact/pin rules. It does not create a new machine allocation or vendor identity and does not erase the machine's earlier model exposure, installation observations, unpinned history or resource restrictions. Approval and acceptance alone open no installation. Each newly approved unpinned reinstall follows the separately selected fresh-acceptance A decision; mandatory pins and package checks retain their existing duties and failed checks never fall back to unpinned.

A genuinely new machine/order requires its own approved entry and original structured facts, distinct durably reserved allocation and admitted per-machine identity, with the existing verification/invoice and first-contact admissions. A second attempt at the same entry cannot bypass its barrier by reserving another index. A distinct entry remains subject to its own approval, unavailable-identity exclusion and all other applicable checks. Restored/imported-seed allocation limits remain; possession of retained credentials alone does not establish permission to allocate. Coordinated identity-format and capability evidence remain owed where not yet admitted.

A new order or successor binding to the new machine grants no authority over the old one. An operation naming the old machine still needs its existing authorized caller or the expressly applicable deterministic flow; no generic sessionless third-rung cleanup privilege is inferred. Rebinding the same machine requires confirmed predecessor end, stopped workers and closed channels. All bindings remain operator acts before channel access. Existing holds, unresolved outcomes, dispositions and no-automatic-retry rules remain independent of a recovery preference; disposition records unknown outcome, not success or non-execution.

The general separate-entry permission does not itself select a third-rung product policy. Nor does it impose a universal deletion-before-new-order gate. Selecting either a different-machine rung or an extra sequencing prerequisite remains outside this technical settlement. Whether a surviving authorized old-machine reconciliation reader exists after a predecessor ends is separately queued, not declared impossible here.

Where a profile declares an independence bound, the existing footprint test still refuses a violating binding, re-entry or escalation. It is not automatically a prohibition on every new order while the old machine exists. Ordering and binding are distinct acts subject to their own admissions; this creates no unbound-order exception. Other profile, vendor-diversity and sealed-access duties remain. The owner-selected bound-profile no-pin B waives none of them. The offered recovery form under such profiles remains a separate queued policy branch.

A different inference trust domain is not supplied merely by a new machine, DNS name, vendor account or allocation. The glossary counts configured weights, proxy and requested provider separately. The exact generic third-rung selection predicate and evidence remain queued; the federation discussion's different-weights language is not silently generalized into a new all-route predicate here.

CNF-80 covers the dedicated path's separately approved destructive reinstall and STG-20 describes that path as a bottom rung. This establishes no LNVPS later-stage successor coverage and makes no claim that the dedicated case exercises a different-domain successor. A later-stage LNVPS form still needs its own useful positive/refusal evidence and stage applicability. No source read supplies runtime conformance, vendor observations or formal authority for an unmodeled clause.

## Checked source quotations

ARC-22 says "A stop is neither confirmed destruction nor confirmed billing cessation."

SEC-1 says "A model that has touched a machine counts as touching it until that machine is destroyed".

SEC-4 says "What is dispatched is the approved record."

SEC-4 says "A typed operation that names an existing machine MUST be authorized against the calling session's binding".

SEC-1 says "Binding is an operator act in the browser, made before any channel access to that machine."

STA-24 says "a second attempt at the same entry sits behind the same barrier even if it would reserve another index."

STA-24 says "A different approved entry is independent, and creating it while a sibling is unresolved is permitted under its own approval, whose card shows the unresolved sibling and that it may be billing, unless the unavailable-identity exclusion below bars its order."

SEC-5 says "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."

STG-21a says "This is accepted vendor risk, not proof of host destruction in every source-permitted execution."

The owner separately selected later-stage no-bound B+E, recorded in the section “Owner decision — later-stage LNVPS third rung without an independence bound, 2026-11-03” on this bead: old stop/renewal-off terminal reconciliation before the new order, with no deletion wait. Its bound-profile branch, exact different-domain predicate, required replacement-entry mechanics and post-session old-machine read authority remain queued. The selected sequencing is not a policy chosen by this technical-common record itself. The ordinary half-finished binding-route source check stays queued; it does not block the live-caller/new-machine example. Token/scope succession is recorded on tw-pgp.

It neither adopts the recommended policy nor claims a normative edit, bead readiness, closure or capability admission.

## Owner decision — later-stage LNVPS third rung without an independence bound, 2026-11-03

Selected B+E: plain B plus the separately proposed reconciliation-first sequencing E, with its gate at the new order: stop the old machine and turn its automatic renewal off, finish the old machine's terminal reconciliation, then order the new machine. The new order is permitted only after that reconciliation, without waiting for confirmed deletion. It is a distinct approved entry, allocation and per-machine identity with its own existing verification, invoice and first-contact admissions, not a re-order of the old entry or a new label for the old machine.

Two independent readings selected plain B, called it simplest and treated it as an explicit policy resolution. The other selected B with its own reconciliation-first sequencing, called that simplest and treated B itself as a clarification. The owner selected B+E rather than silently describing these as three identical votes for plain B. Same-machine reinstall A, universal deletion-before-order D and no later-stage in-setup rung C were not chosen.

The selected ordering boundary is the new order: finish terminal reconciliation of the old stop/renewal-off work before ordering the replacement. Preserve existing operation prerequisites, evidence and terminal-record rules. A disposition remains an unknown outcome, not successful stop, renewal-off, deletion or non-execution, and cannot substitute for a confirmation where the existing flow requires confirmation. The choice supplies no new status-read confirmation predicate, automatic retry, erasure of an unresolved effect or broader sessionless cleanup authority. Any finer session-creation or interrupted-caller mechanics must preserve this selected order and existing authority rather than infer an extra general ban or permission.

The old machine stays recorded as existing, billed and exposed until the existing admitted deletion evidence is durably recorded. Its approved entry, uncertainty, retained restrictions, historical exposure and applicable placed-secret duties remain. A stop, renewal-off, an announced deletion date and the new order clear none of them. The new machine's successor has no authority over the old machine merely because it provisions the replacement. Domain selection and post-session old-machine reconciliation remain queued; neither is implicitly supplied by B+E. No claim is made that deletion reads become universally impossible after the old session ends.

Stage-1 C remains settled: no stage-1 in-setup third rung and no expansion of stage 1's one-machine/one-invoice acquisition. This decision concerns later-stage LNVPS recovery without an independence bound. It does not select a future bound-profile rung or waive footprint, vendor-diversity or sealed-access duties. The previously selected ordinary named no-pin allowance under a bound is no waiver of those duties either.

## Coverage correction and owning text work

CNF-80 covers the dedicated path's separately approved destructive reinstall. It does not exercise this later-stage LNVPS new-machine successor path, and no different-domain successor coverage is inferred from that dedicated case. Retain that narrow correction rather than repeat either a no-coverage-at-any-vendor assertion or a claim that a reinstall fixture proves this path.

ARC-22 says "A stop is neither confirmed destruction nor confirmed billing cessation."

STA-24 says "A different approved entry is independent, and creating it while a sibling is unresolved is permitted under its own approval, whose card shows the unresolved sibling and that it may be billing, unless the unavailable-identity exclusion below bars its order."

SEC-4 says "A typed operation that names an existing machine MUST be authorized against the calling session's binding".

SEC-1 says "A model that has touched a machine counts as touching it until that machine is destroyed".

SEC-5 says "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."

State the selected later-stage flow and sequencing at ARC-16/ARC-22 with coordinated approved-entry references where needed at ARC-15 and an STA-24 pointer at its sibling-entry permission. Keep authorization, allocation, uncertainty, operation predicates and exposure in their existing owners. Reconcile any diagram implication that exposure ends at the LNVPS stop. Coordinate the separate stage-1 C amendment and checked attributions without changing its chosen scope. Add distinguishing later-stage conformance and applicability: useful replacement while deletion is pending, refusal of a replacement order before required old-machine terminal reconciliation, original approved-fact/identity/hold refusals, retained old-machine display and duties, and no new authority over the old machine. Preserve declaration/Markdown agreement for any affected formalized clause, with no weakening theorem, gate, assumption or pin/package requirement.

This is an explicit owner decision and staged record, not a normative edit, capability admission or implementation completion. The differing classification of plain B is preserved; the selected additional sequencing is not represented as unanimous technical clarification. Keep domain selection, post-session reconciliation, required replacement-entry mechanics and the future bound branch visible before declaring readiness.

## Owner decision — the setup finishes only after the old machine's deletion is recorded, 2026-11-03

Scope: the selected later-stage restart rung (B+E) at LNVPS. The old machine M was stopped with automatic renewal off and its terminal reconciliation finished, but its deletion is not yet confirmed. The new approved entry N has been ordered and delivered.

Selected completion B: the setup stays unfinished until M's deletion evidence is durably recorded. N's delivery alone does not finish it. M stays in the setup's cost figures and on its opening screen, and the abandonment flow can still reach M. The accepted cost is that a working N can sit behind the unfinished-setup screen for as long as M's deletion evidence stays unrecorded. Not selected: completion A, which would finish the setup on N's delivery and keep M only as an outstanding liability outside the setup.

The independent readings split two to two on this point, and two of them each claimed that the source forces the opposite answer. Of the other two, one chose completion B and called early completion new policy; the other recommended completion A, called completion B simplest and called the point new policy. This record does not claim the source forces completion B. The owner resolved the split. `ARC-22` should state the rule when the normative text is next edited. Completion B adds no new authority. It does not shorten the existing duties, which hold until confirmation under `SEC-5`: "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."

## Technical common facts

All four independent readings agree on these facts, and none calls them a new policy:

- N is a new approved entry of the original setup, not a new setup. Its prose belongs to the already-selected B+E text work at `ARC-15` and the `STA-24` pointer. No tw-nj8 grant extends to M.
- If nobody collects M's deletion evidence, M stays recorded and shown, in `ARC-22`'s words, "as still existing and billed, with the vendor's stated deletion date, until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract." Its exposure stands and its placed-secret duties remain. That is conformant but costly, and it breaks no duty. Under completion B it also leaves the setup unfinished.
- A model-free deletion reader acting outside sessions would be new authority, even though it only reads. `SEC-1` names "the jump-host flow (`CHN-R6`), and Replace's key migration (`STA-17`)", `SEC-4` says "The abandonment flow is authorized outside any session", and `STA-18`'s listing runs "before any session exists"; none names such a reader.
- None of these can collect M's deletion evidence: a session bound only to N, the `STA-18` listing, Restore, Replace or the jump-host flow.
- The abandonment flow can reach M, because completion B keeps M among `SEC-4`'s "machines of the unfinished setup", subject to `SEC-4`'s id-provenance condition. It is setup-wide, though: `ARC-22` says "Abandonment destroys every machine of the setup", so using it also stops the working N. Whether its authorization covers the deletion reads is the split recorded below.
- T44's derived vendor identity gates every route.

Under completion B, no route ends M's display without deletion evidence. The setup finishes only once M's deletion evidence is recorded. Abandoning the setup instead stays incomplete, with M and N still shown, until each deletion is confirmed: `ARC-22` says "The screen retains unresolved-machine and incomplete-abandonment truth until deletion is confirmed".

Three of the four readings hold that the abandonment flow's existing authorization covers its own deletion reads. On that view, naming those reads at `ARC-21` and `ARC-22` is a technical omission to fix in the text, not new authority. The fourth reading says the source names no such reader.

## Not chosen — the collector for M's deletion evidence

Completion B makes collecting M's deletion evidence a precondition of finishing, so it leaves one choice open: who collects that evidence? The candidates differ in authority:

- a dedicated model-free deletion reader, scoped to the unfinished setup, which would be new authority;
- only the existing callers. These include a session still bound to M, since `SEC-4` says "A session's vendor operations reach the machines of its own set"; a later re-entry session bound to M alone, if a stopped, never-delivered machine is eligible for re-entry; and abandonment of the whole setup.

The readings dispute whether that M-only session is eligible. Clarifying wording at the `ARC-16` note or in `SEC-1` would follow whichever choice is made. The old machine of a Replace rebuild has the same reader gap and stays queued with this question. This record chooses no collector and keeps the bead in triage.

## Queued — different-domain selection

All four readings treat the generic different-domain selector as a capability and evidence dependency, not something to choose now. Queue it under `OPN-27`. One caveat for that entry: `OPN-27` describes its gap as one that "sits under any declared independence bound", so the selector for a setup with no declared bound currently has no owning entry, and the queue entry must say so.

With no declared bound, two readings disagree on the procured path. One says the rung stays gated because it cannot honestly be offered as a different-domain restart. The other says the restart proceeds as a shown collision. That question stays queued; later-stage paths are gated in either case.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a dedicated reader collects the old machine's deletion evidence, 2026-11-03

This follows the completion-B record on this bead and settles the question that record left open: who collects the old machine M's deletion evidence.

Selected collector A, as an amendment: a dedicated, model-free reader that only collects deletion evidence, scoped to the outstanding machines of the unfinished setup. It runs outside any session and drives no model. It may perform only the reads that the LNVPS operation contract needs to confirm deletion; it issues no stop, destroy, reinstall or other mutating call, binds no session and holds no SSH client key. It uses only the machine's recorded vendor key, because `STG-21a` confirms deletion only "under the machine's recorded key". It is new authority: `SEC-4` owns it, `SEC-5` row 1 applies, and `ARC-21` and `ARC-22` must name it as the reader behind "until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract". The accepted cost is a new read-only authority outside any session.

"Read-only" describes the harness authority, not necessarily the vendor side effects. Any vendor-side effect of the reads is disclosed where the reader is specified. T44's derived vendor identity still gates the reader, as it gates every route. The reader supplies evidence and ends no duty by itself; `SEC-5` says "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."

Not selected:
- Collector B, existing routes only. These include a session still bound to M, since `SEC-4` says "A session's vendor operations reach the machines of its own set"; a later re-entry session bound to M alone where that is eligible; and abandonment of the whole setup, which also stops the working replacement.
- Collector T, no collector: M stays recorded and shown as existing and billed, its placed-secret duties stay open, and the setup stays unfinished until it is abandoned.

## Queued — the old machine of a Replace rebuild

The old machine of an LNVPS Replace rebuild takes the same unavailable-destroy treatment and has the same reader gap. It does not follow from this decision: this reader's scope, the outstanding machines of the unfinished setup, does not reach it, and widening that scope would be a further amendment. It stays queued for a later review.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim. The bead stays in triage.

## Technical common fact — with no declared independence bound, the third rung stays gated, 2026-11-03

Scope: the selected later-stage restart rung (B+E) at LNVPS, for a setup that declares no independence bound. This answers the question the completion-B record on this bead queued.

Three independent readings agree on these facts, and none calls keeping the gate an amendment:

- The rung stays unavailable until a selection criterion for a setup with no declared bound, and the capability to meet it, exist. Until then it cannot be offered as `ARC-16`'s "restart under a different domain".
- As already recorded on this bead, a new machine, DNS name, vendor account or allocation does not by itself supply a different domain. A shown collision is not evidence of a different domain either. A collision on a shared layer is still not, by itself, a refusal.
- `OPN-27` describes its gap as one that "sits under any declared independence bound", so its queue entry must also own the selector for a setup with no declared bound.

One reading classifies the choice between gating and proceeding as new policy that the source does not force. All three pick the gate, which is the current state, so this record changes no requirement. A restart in the same domain, shown as a collision, would amend `ARC-16`. None of these three readings recommends it; the completion-B record's earlier reading that the restart proceeds as a shown collision stays on record, and it stays an unselected owner option.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim. Later-stage paths stay gated.

## Owner decision — the dedicated reader also covers the old machine of a Replace rebuild, 2026-11-03

This settles the case the dedicated-reader record on this bead left queued. `ARC-22` gives the same destroy treatment to "an abandonment, or the old machine of a Replace rebuild", and that treatment lasts "until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract". No source clause gives Replace's own flow a deletion read for the old machine M, and that flow ends; only an existing route, such as a session still bound to M (`SEC-4`: "A session's vendor operations reach the machines of its own set") or a later one bound to M where that is eligible, could collect that evidence.

Selected: extend the dedicated reader, as an amendment.
- Scope: besides the outstanding machines of an unfinished setup, the reader covers each outstanding old machine left by a Replace rebuild. Its reads, limits and disclosures are unchanged. It is model-free and runs outside any session. It performs only the reads the LNVPS operation contract needs to confirm deletion, issues no mutating call, binds no session and holds no SSH client key.
- Key: each read uses M's own per-machine vendor key, the one `STG-21a` means by "under the machine's recorded key". It never uses the replacement machine's key or an SSH client key. ADR-0042 already records how Replace keeps that key: "alone, encrypted in the new local store, never the retired seed".
- Gate: T44 still gates the key. `STA-17` says the carry-forward "remains T44's, not an available Replace behavior", and the credential inventory lists the derived vendor identity as "not derivable today". Until T44 lands, the reader has no key for M, and `STG-21a` says "Without the key, no read confirms deletion, and the placed-secret duties continue."
- Evidence only: the reader supplies evidence and ends no duty by itself. `SEC-5` says "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."
- Owners: this is new authority. `SEC-4` owns it, `SEC-5` row 1 applies, and `ARC-21` and `ARC-22` must name the reader for this case.

Accepted cost: the read-only authority outside any session now also reaches machines outside any unfinished setup, after the Replace flow has ended.

Not selected:
- Existing routes only, such as a session still bound to M or a later one bound to M where that is eligible; otherwise M stays shown as existing and billed, with its duties open.
- No collector: no rule edits, and M stays recorded and shown as existing and billed, with its placed-secret duties open.

No clause names the caller that stops M and turns its automatic renewal off, though `ARC-22` requires both: "it stops that machine, turns automatic renewal off". That stays a follow-up for the text work; this decision does not depend on it.

This decision does not decide whether Replace may report complete before M's deletion is recorded. That stays queued.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim. The bead stays in triage.

## Owner decision — Replace stays incomplete until the old machine's deletion is recorded, 2026-11-03

This settles the question the Replace-reader record on this bead left queued: whether an LNVPS Replace may report complete before the deletion of the rebuilt old machine M is recorded. `STA-17` says the old machine "takes its unavailable-destroy treatment", and `ARC-22` keeps M shown "as still existing and billed, with the vendor's stated deletion date, until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract." Neither ties that state to Replace's completion report. `STA-17`'s screen "names unrecovered machines" and reports no complete Replace while one remains outstanding, and no clause says whether M is one.

Selected: stay incomplete, as an amendment.
- Replace is reported incomplete until M's deletion evidence is durably recorded. M is added to `STA-17`'s rule that the screen "never reports a complete Replace or complete revocation while either remains outstanding".
- No other Replace step waits on M. The new machine, sessions and allocation proceed, and Replace's finished steps, such as the export of the new seed's sheet, may be shown finished. Replace's allocations still "wait for its fresh seed's record" (`STA-22b`), not for M.
- The retired seed's backup: the operator may drop it once the last step that needs the retired seed is done. The wait for M's deletion evidence does not by itself keep the backup needed. Where M's vendor key can come only from the retired seed, a read under that key is such a step; the carry-forward that would keep the key apart from the seed "remains T44's, not an available Replace behavior." This clarifies `STA-17`'s "the operator needs its backup *during* Replace and abandons it after."
- Conformance: one `CNF-20` case covers the interval after Replace's other steps finish and before M's deletion evidence is durably recorded. No complete Replace is reported in that interval, including after a restart, after the vendor's stated deletion date passes, and after a failed append of the evidence.
- Owners: `STA-17` states the rule and the backup clarification, `SEC-5`'s operator-seed row follows it, `CNF-20` gains the case, and `ARC-22` gets at most a pointer.

The decision adds no authority and shortens no duty. `SEC-5` still says "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."

Accepted cost: Replace stays incomplete for as long as M's deletion evidence stays unrecorded. If no read can ever confirm the deletion, it never clears, and a status that never clears can teach operators to ignore it.

Not selected:
- Complete with M listed apart: Replace reports complete once its other steps finish, with M shown as outstanding beside it.
- Complete only if M's old public key was removed before the stop, following `CNF-20`'s "removal of the old public key on every maintained machine".

All three independent readings picked staying incomplete and called it the simplest. Two read it as a new policy. The third read it, on its best reading, as a technical omission owned by `STA-17`, but as an amendment in form either way. The owner records it as an amendment.

## Follow-up — re-entry before the stop

No text says how `STA-17`'s re-entry of "each maintained machine" applies to a machine being rebuilt, including whether M is re-entered and its old public key removed before it is stopped. That stays a follow-up for the text work; this decision does not depend on it.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim. The bead stays in triage.

## Owner decision — the setup finishes when the new machine arrives, and one deletion check covers any stopped machine, 2026-11-04

Scope: three decisions on this bead, judged again by a need review on 2026-11-04 that asked whether the system needs each one:

- completion B, in "Owner decision — the setup finishes only after the old machine's deletion is recorded, 2026-11-03" (comment 58000001);
- collector A, in "Owner decision — a dedicated reader collects the old machine's deletion evidence, 2026-11-03" (comment 60000001);
- its extension, in "Owner decision — the dedicated reader also covers the old machine of a Replace rebuild, 2026-11-03" (comment 60000001).

The owner selected "On arrival, one button", as recommended. The owner knew it reverses completion B, which was picked on 2026-11-03 over a two-to-two split.

**Selected — completion on arrival, as an amendment.**

- In the B+E rung, the setup finishes when the new approved entry N is delivered. It no longer waits for the old machine M's deletion evidence.
- M stays on the opening screen as still existing and billed, with its cost and the vendor's stated deletion date, until `STG-21a`'s deletion evidence is durably recorded. Its exposure and placed-secret duties stay open; `SEC-5` says "Until confirmation, retain outstanding-machine truth and placed-secret duties; stop, a deletion date and operator disposition end none of them."
- This is an `ARC-22` amendment and a display rule, not an authority. Today `ARC-22` keys the opening screen to "An unfinished setup MUST own the first screen". The amendment adds that the screen also shows each such outstanding machine after its setup has finished. It must not make a finished setup own the first screen.
- Once the setup finishes, M is no longer one of `SEC-4`'s "machines of the unfinished setup", so the abandonment flow no longer reaches it. Before N's delivery the setup is unfinished and the existing rules hold.

**Selected — one operator-started deletion check, as an amendment and new authority.** It replaces collector A and its Replace extension, both in comment 60000001.

- It is one check, started by the operator from the screen that shows M. It is model-free, runs outside any session and drives no model. Nothing starts it automatically; `ARC-22` says "Nothing runs while the app is closed".
- It performs only `STG-21a`'s deletion reads, under M's own recorded vendor key, because `STG-21a` confirms deletion only "under the machine's recorded key". It issues no stop, destroy, reinstall or other mutating call. It binds no session, holds no SSH client key, and never uses another machine's key.
- Scope: any machine stopped under `ARC-22`'s unavailable-destroy treatment whose deletion is not yet confirmed. The scope is keyed on that machine's state, not on the flow that stopped it: the in-setup rung, Replace's own flow, or an abandonment. It applies whatever state the machine's setup is in, including a finished or an abandoned setup. This answers the question comment 71000001 left open, whether "unfinished setup" covers an abandoned setup still waiting on M's deletion: the check covers that machine.
- Evidence only: the check supplies deletion evidence and ends no duty by itself. "Read-only" describes the harness authority, not necessarily the vendor side effects; any vendor-side effect of the reads is disclosed where the check is specified.
- Gate: T44's derived vendor identity gates M's key, as it gates every route. Without the key, `STG-21a` says "no read confirms deletion, and the placed-secret duties continue."
- Owners: `SEC-4` owns the grant, `SEC-5` row 1 adds it to its list of flows, and `ARC-21` and `ARC-22` name it as the reader behind "until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract". Conformance cases follow.

**The counts.** Five independent readings judged these points.

- Completion: four chose completion on arrival and one chose completion B. The one held that completion on arrival needs a new display home for M and a rule that M leaves the setup; the amendment above names both.
- The check: all five chose an operator-started check under M's own key. Three chose one grant keyed on the machine's state; two chose a narrow grant for each stopping flow.
- All five found that the amendment touches conformance rows that cite these records. Three checked the theorems and found none touched.

**Not selected:**

- completion B, which kept the setup unfinished until M's deletion evidence is recorded;
- collector A as recorded, with one scope for the outstanding machines of an unfinished setup and a second for Replace's old machine;
- a separate check grant for each stopping flow;
- the earlier unselected collectors, existing routes only and no collector.

**What stands.**

- Comment 45000001: B+E, its sequencing and its technical settlement.
- Comment 60000001: the technical fact that with no declared bound the rung stays gated, and the decision that Replace stays incomplete until M's deletion evidence is durably recorded. That decision covers Replace's old machine only; this one does not change it.
- Comment 68000001: Replace's own flow stops M and turns its renewal off, under M's key, in the recorded order. The check gives that flow no further call.
- Comment 71000001: C governs every LNVPS setup until the in-setup replacement order is admitted.
- Comment 58000001's technical common facts and its queued different-domain selector under `OPN-27`, except where they rest on completion B.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim. Nothing is enabled.

title: Settle the reach of SEC-5's withheld-before-destruction rule for peer-held ranges and new reads of old files
description:
tw-pkn landed `SEC-5`'s rule that a machine's destruction retires its row 23 references while what was withheld stays withheld. `SEC-5` says "Destruction never counts as a scan: bytes withheld before it stay withheld, and no old range becomes scanned, safe or releasable because a reference retired", and "re-collecting, replaying, re-requesting or displaying a pre-destruction range after the destruction, or giving it a later retrieval time, does not make it new output". tw-pkn's closing comment (97000001) leaves two points open for the owner, not chosen there:

"- Scope of "bytes withheld before it stay withheld": whether it covers a range held only for another machine's unarmed reference and already scanned against the destroyed machine's references, once that other reference is re-armed.
- Whether a new command that reads a pre-destruction output file on a peer is new output, or a re-request of the old range."

1. **Withheld only for another machine.** A range on peer A is held only because machine B's reference is unarmed, and it has already been scanned against destroyed machine M's references. When B's reference is re-armed and the range scans clean against it, is it still "withheld before" M's destruction and so withheld for good, or does the rule reach only bytes that M's own references held?
2. **A new command reading an old file.** After M's destruction, a new command on a peer reads a file the peer wrote before it. Is that command's output new output, scanned and released under the current references, or a re-request of the pre-destruction range that stays withheld?
