## Owner decision — sessions survive every local event until End, 2026-11-04

Scope: which events end a session, and what a session keeps across the events that no longer end it. This record supersedes the owner decision on this bead titled "Owner decision — a fresh session resuming a no-brief install stopped by app Lock, 2026-11-03". The owner first kept that decision ("the session should just resume"), then gave a new direction, "Do not kill sessions". The owner was later told in one line that the earlier decision is dropped, and did not object. Under this record an explicit Lock ends no session, so the case that decision covered no longer arises. Its carry-over is never written, and no rule it would have qualified carries any of its exceptions.

Selected by the owner, in order, in the words of the options the owner saw:
- **"Every local event".** "Also survive reload and page loss. Needs model context and credentials saved to disk, which the spec forbids." It was chosen over the recommended "Lock only" and over "Lock, plus the page being hidden or cached while it is still alive". The model-context part was later declined (below).
- **"Keep all until End".** "Approvals, machines and the paid key (saved encrypted under the data key) carry on after a reload or kill until an explicit End." The owner chose it knowingly, with these costs shown:
  - "an approved wipe can run with no new tap";
  - "Lock and reload are no longer a kill switch, End is";
  - "a live paid key sits encrypted on the phone";
  - "a paused session keeps its machines".
- **"Held until End".** "When a paid key is lost before it's saved, the session is held: nothing runs, and approvals and machines stay. The operator presses End and starts a new paid session. Otherwise the session ends at the key's expiry." It was chosen over "the session ends on its own" and "a second key for the same session".
- **"Pauses".** "Viewing the backup words again pauses running sessions the way Lock now does, and they come back afterwards with their approvals intact." It was chosen over the recommended "Ends".
- **"Ended history".** "A restored backup brings back the history of its sessions, never a live session. You start a new session and approve again. The old phone, if any, keeps its own session."
- **Told in one line, without objection:** the earlier decision is dropped; ADR-0045 changes; the mechanical weakenings follow; "no model-context checkpoint"; "Replace still ends sessions".
- **"Accept, End stops it".** "A bring-your-own or local session that is never reopened keeps its approvals and machines with no time limit. It ends only on End, Replace or loss of the phone's data. No idle timer. Paid sessions still end at their key's expiry." It was chosen over adding a timer.
- **"Existing notes only".** A session counts as started from the journal's existing admission records, and "the only new record is the End record". It was chosen over the recommended "Text review, with guards", over "Always a new note" and over "Panel it first". The guards of the option not chosen are not assumed to come with this pick. Each was checked against it on its own and holds without a new rule, as set out under the direction below.
- **"Abandon ends them".** "One Abandon approval journal-ends every session holding any of the setup's machines, and every End is durable before the first destroy. The paid-key revocation is attempted and journaled at End. It then destroys what it can and shows what may still bill. The Abandon card says plainly that it ends those sessions." It was chosen over "End first" and "Keep them paused". The owner accepted these costs knowingly:
  - pick 8's "only End stops it" gains Abandon, but only with the card saying so (pick 8 is the "Accept, End stops it" pick above);
  - other machines in a holding session lose their session but aren't destroyed.

**The direction.** A session survives explicit app Lock, pagehide (including entry to the back-forward cache), reload, worker shutdown, and the browser freezing or discarding the page. Approvals, bound machines and the procured paid session key, sealed under the data key, carry on across those events until an explicit End. A paid key lost before its seal is durable leaves the session held until End or the key's original expiry: nothing runs, and approvals and machines stay. There is no second mint and no same-key recovery. Entering the seed-backup ceremony pauses running sessions as Lock does, and they resume afterwards with their approvals. A restored backup brings back its sessions as ended history only. A session counts as started from the journal's existing admission records, each committed before the session gains authority. The only new record is the journaled End, and a journal written before End records existed replays its sessions as ended. Abandoning an unfinished setup is one approval, made outside any session, whose card says plainly that it ends every session holding any of the setup's machines.

**What ends a session:**
- an explicit, journaled End;
- an Abandon whose card says it ends that session. Each such session gets a journaled End with its paid-key revocation attempted and journaled, and every End is durable before the first destroy. Sessions holding none of the setup's machines are untouched;
- Replace;
- for a paid session, its key's expiry or cap exhaustion. The existing `STA-23` rule is unchanged: "At expiry or cap exhaustion, that session MUST end at the next execution opportunity before further ordinary dispatch or actionable continuation". `ARC-31a`'s "Hidden, frozen and suspended time after the lifetime origin counts toward the lifetime exactly as visible time does" is unchanged, as is `STA-23`'s "Ordinary hiding, suspension and return MUST NOT extend a procured session key's original absolute expiry". A reload, kill or Lock does not extend it either;
- loss of the phone's data. Such a session ends by absence, not by a journaled transition, so no proof or conformance case may claim it as one.

`STA-23`'s "Ending one session does not by itself lock the whole store or end another eligible session" is unchanged.

**What no longer ends a session:** explicit app Lock, pagehide, reload, worker shutdown, freezing and discarding, and replay, which now resumes. Entering the ceremony pauses sessions. A lost paid key holds its session. An import brings back ended history only. A journal of the format before End records replays its sessions as ended through the store's format versioning.

Whether Replace and a paid key's expiry or cap exhaustion write a journaled End record is left to the text work. Either way, replay must never resume a session they ended.

**Accepted weakenings, by the pick that accepted each:**
- "Every local event" and "Keep all until End":
  - `STA-23`: "Explicit app Lock, pagehide including entry to the back-forward cache, reload, or worker shutdown MUST stop dispatch, end session workers and close channels; the worker clears its keys and credential buffers and returns locked." These events no longer end a session or its authority.
  - The paid key at rest. `SEC-5`'s "Browser memory only" for the session key, `STA-23`'s "No new credential persistence or off-device executor is authorized by continuity" and `STA-14`'s "re-supplied or re-minted per session, deliberately not persisted" no longer hold for the procured paid key, which is sealed under the data key. They still hold for every other credential.
  - `ARC-31a`: "Replay of intent/terminal evidence restores history, never the session key or authority to re-mint." Replay restores the paid key from its own sealed record. It still restores no authority to re-mint.
  - `STG-20`: "The rendering session's end is not journaled; after a restart, every earlier session's approval is no longer usable", and "A replay ends the session". `CNF-86`: "Contrast explicit app Lock and worker restart, which end the rendering session". A journaled approval, including a destructive one, can dispatch after a reload or kill with no new tap.
  - `CNF-82`: "Explicit app Lock still ends it", and "Reload/full end require unlock again, session workers lose access". Lock and reload no longer prove that a session ended.
  - `CNF-69`: "Worker loss never restores memory-only authority". Worker loss can return the sealed key's authority.
  - `SEC-1`: a binding is freed by "the act STA-23 already performs on lock". A dormant session keeps its machines, and no other session can bind them until it ends.
  - The executive summary's "App Lock remains the operator's way to end local sessions" is withdrawn. End is that way now.
- The mechanical follow-ons, told in one line:
  - `STA-23`: "A killed or discarded worker restarts locked with journal replay and fresh session admission, never durable resurrection of memory-only credentials or an unjournaled continuation." A session that has not ended resumes without fresh admission. The ban on durable resurrection is withdrawn for the sealed paid key only. The ban on an unjournaled continuation stays.
  - `ARC-31a`'s and `CNF-69`'s "revoked when the session ends" no longer brings revocation at Lock or close, since neither ends a session. Revocation comes at End.
  - The theorem `global_end_paths_and_replay_fence`: its lock, pagehide, reload, shutdown and replay cases stop being end cases. It is split, not weakened in place, as the text work below says.
  - The `Dispatch.lean` assumption boundary's replay parts, "Replay ends the rendering session; the end is not journaled or modelled." and "after replay only successor sessions act", are withdrawn. Its convention that "an ended session sends no request" stays an assumption, and the companion still does not prove session termination. The theorems stay, with `ended_session_approval_refused`'s trace and docstring moved from `.replay` to the End.
  - `CNF-7`: "after confirmed predecessor loss, locked recovery and a separately admitted successor are required". Worker loss no longer requires a successor admission.
  - ADR-0045: "Session end is not journaled; the journal alone therefore cannot say whether an approval stands". Its premise no longer holds once End is journaled.
- "Held until End": a held session keeps its approvals and machines while its key is lost. Exposure is then bounded only conditionally, by the accepted cap where issuer acceptance was evidenced, with issuer enforcement and automatic top-up off (`CNF-70`). Where acceptance was unseen, the hard bound is the account balance. Spend stays unaccounted, never zero: "any spend remains unaccounted, not zero or refunded". The owner saw this described as no new rule change beyond the earlier picks.
- "Pauses": `STA-23`'s ceremony sentences, including "The ceremony starts by stopping dispatch, ending session workers and closing their channels, as lock below does."; `CNF-82`'s ceremony line, which "requires the passphrase again, ends sessions and uses the same ceremony"; and the Lean `enterCeremony` step, which ends every session today.
- "Accept, End stops it": `STA-23`'s "There is no new idle or hidden-time lock deadline" stays and no longer bounds a session. A bring-your-own or local session that is never reopened has no time bound.
- "Abandon ends them": the dormant session's end list gains Abandon, only where the card says so; a paused session's hold on its machines gives way to Abandon; a holding session's machines outside the setup lose their session but are not destroyed.

**Not selected:**
- a model-context checkpoint: model context is not saved to disk;
- a second mint, or any recovery of the same key, after a lost key;
- an automatic end on a lost key;
- abandonment that leaves the holding sessions paused, and "End first";
- shrinking a live bound set;
- a destroy sent by a session;
- ending every session at Abandon, rather than the sessions holding the setup's machines;
- ending sessions at the ceremony;
- live sessions from an import;
- an idle or hidden-time timer;
- a new admission record, and the guarded admission option;
- "Lock only", and Lock plus a hidden or cached page;
- keeping progress but asking again for approvals without saving the paid key.

**What stays intact:**
- `ARC-22`'s "Nothing runs while the app is closed". No hosted or off-device executor is added.
- `OVR-3`'s "No credential is written to storage in cleartext". Only the procured paid key is sealed; every other credential is re-supplied or re-derived as today.
- "Prompt bodies are not journaled" (`ARC-31a`). No unjournaled continuation is resumed.
- `STA-3`: "A canonical event MUST be durably appended before it is applied to in-memory state", and "If the append fails, the transition does not occur". This is how a session's existing admission records are committed before it gains authority.
- `STA-23`'s fence, now carried by the journaled End: "Individual session end destroys that session's runtime authority and pending approvals; it does not revive on return.", and "The actual end fence is irreversible and MUST NOT be reset to implement continuation."
- `STA-23`'s "No unload callback is relied on for journaling", which `STG-20` restates.
- A crash during a dispatch leaves the intent unresolved for reconciliation, with no automatic retry, and validation comes before any send.
- `ARC-31a`'s one mint: "No second mint is admitted", and "A durable mint intent consumes the session's one attempt even when a response is lost". The key's cap and original expiry are unchanged.
- `SEC-1`'s "A machine MUST be in at most one live session's set at a time", and no shrink of a live bound set.
- `ARC-21`'s abandonment "never through a session", and `STA-24`.
- `ARC-22`'s "An unfinished setup is device-bound".
- Replace still ends sessions.
- The fresh acceptance for each newly approved reinstall, and the T47 settlements on this bead, are unchanged.

**Strengthened:** a session's end is a journaled, irreversible record that replay can see. The dispatch check (`SEC-4`, `CNF-26`) reads it. Old page or worker incarnations are refused after a reload, replay or shutdown.

**Effect on the other records on this bead:**
- The superseded decision is never written into the text. `SEC-14`, `STG-21`, `ARC-11a`, `CNF-93` and `CNF-102` carry none of that decision's exceptions.
- In the source-pruned queue notes, the example "Take a stage-1 machine with no tenant whose install is interrupted by an explicit Lock. The old session's authority ends for good." no longer holds, because Lock ends no session and the same session resumes. The note's reasoning still covers a setup whose session has actually ended. Its `SEC-1` wording clarification stays queued, framed for that case. Its question, "Whether the fresh session that resumes an ended session's setup owes its own goal and its own acceptance", stays queued and is not answered here.
- `SEC-14`'s "a session resumed after an interruption" that "accepts nothing again" now covers every local event. This is a rewording.

**Left to the text work, for the next normative edit.** Each item below stops and is reported if it needs a new owner choice, a weakening not listed above, a new authority, or a new record kind other than the End record.
- Name which existing admission record or records start a session.
- Give the journal format that adds End records a new version, so an older journal replays its sessions as ended. `credential-format-v1.md` already rejects "unknown algorithms or versions".
- Settle whether Replace and a paid key's expiry or cap exhaustion write a journaled End, keeping replay from resuming a session they ended.
- The lost key: the order of sealing and validation; what a resume with a seal but no terminal does; when a known key id is revoked before End; and whether the hold covers SSH. `STA-23` says "An inference expiry does not expire SSH", and `ARC-31a` holds "every ordinary dispatch or actionable continuation". An unknown revocation stays unknown: "Unknown revocation stays unknown through replay; expiry is not evidence of revocation success".
- Model context on resume: how a resumed session regains its model context, and what becomes of a model turn unfinished at a kill. No model-context checkpoint is saved to disk, and prompt bodies stay unjournaled.
- Import: state that an import resumes nothing, as `STA-16`'s "the restored conduct modes were the exporting session's, which ended" needs. An export never makes the sealed key usable from an import, and an import never revokes it.
- The ceremony: reword its `STA-23` sentences and the `CNF-82` line to pause, and change `enterCeremony` to a pause.
- Abandon: the card's wording, including the sessions it ends and what ending loses; the order of the Ends, the revocation and the destroys; what happens after a page death between the Ends and the first destroy; what carries the flow between openings and who supplies the vendor credential for its reads; whether one bound set can hold machines of more than one setup; and the `ARC-21`, `ARC-22`, `SEC-4`, `STA-18`, `STA-23` and `STA-24` places. `ARC-21`'s "never through a session" stays word for word.
- Proofs: split `global_end_paths_and_replay_fence` into an incarnation-fence theorem and a session-End theorem; change `EndReason`, the global-end and replay steps, and add a resume step; add a witness that a resume with no sealed terminal keeps the key withheld until End. Withdraw the `Dispatch.lean` boundary's replay parts only, keeping its convention that an ended session sends no request as an assumption, and move `ended_session_approval_refused`'s trace and docstring from `.replay` to the End. The abandonment theorems stay.
- Conformance: revise the affected items, add a blocking resume item with its stage row, and add Abandon cases for a failed End append, death before the first destroy, death midway, several holders and an unaffected session.
- ADRs: a new ADR for this direction, and amendments to ADR-0003, ADR-0009, ADR-0022, ADR-0023, ADR-0028 and ADR-0045. ADR-0047 is checked and amended only if it conflicts.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Agent Brief — bounded specification amendment, installation acceptance and session-lifetime decisions

**Category:** bug. **Outcome:** land, in their normative homes, the owner decisions and technical settlements already recorded on this bead. No further owner choice is needed for the scope below. Points the owner left unchosen stay unchosen: where the text work would have to choose one, stop and report it instead of choosing. Move to ready-for-agent when the label flip is confirmed; hand implementation to the drain lane after its current queue.

**Records this brief implements (sections on this bead, by title).** Each section's own text, limits and "Not selected" list govern. This brief summarizes them and widens none.

- "Owner decision — P1-C1, 2026-11-02" (C, keep today's rules).
- "Owner decision — no-pin acceptance after dedicated rescue inspection, 2026-11-02" (timing A), with "Settled technical boundaries under C".

It supersedes "Owner decision — a fresh session resuming a no-brief install stopped by app Lock, 2026-11-03", which this brief does not implement: its carry-over is never written.

**Current gap:** none of these records makes a normative edit, so the source still reads as it did before them. Each is an amendment the owner selected, the owner's keep-today's-rules decision (C), a boundary the readers settled, or a queued wording clarification, and each names its owning text.

**Desired behavior and owners:**

- **C adds no rule.** Keep its "Add no universal operator-approved exact installation-target association, and add no new artifact-evidence prerequisite for offering a reset." Landing the other decisions must not introduce either one, a new per-call approval for `fetch_artifact` or `ready_to_reset`, or a new universal target-association refusal for a pinned installation with no no-pin acceptance record.

Host-key pinning of the rescue connection is not verification of the rescue operating-system artifact. The dedicated path stays gated at its existing milestone.

Under the session-resume record, an actual session end is one of that record's end paths, and a session that survives any local event it lists has survived an interruption. As the decision says, "Withdrawing a typed reinstall approval does not by itself establish the expiry of a separate acceptance"; it selects neither retention nor expiry at withdrawal. Field names and layout are engineering choices. Old-version validation is unchanged, and no fake earlier groups, observations or pins stand in for unavailable history. Cover the five recovery and export cases the decision lists, from identical legacy payloads with different possible origins to refusal of a matching command on every possible origin. `CNF-84` is not weakened.

Record the accepted shared-source risk as the decision states it, without a new warning ceremony, build gate or profile permission slot.

Cover the five cases the decision lists, from refusal or unavailability of a successor selection that omits the escalated stuck machine to preserved predecessor exposure and resource holds. - **The T47 technical settlement and the recovery acceptor settlement** are boundaries of the existing text, not amendments. Where the text work restates them, keep them as stated. In T47, update only the two items these decisions answer, "The recovery ladder's middle rung under a bound set of more than one" (successor-set A) and "An unpinned installation under an independence bound" (B). Leave every other T47 item open as written. If it is unclear whether a record answers a T47 item, stop and report.

  - `STG-10`, `STG-12` and `STG-20`.
  - The conformance items it affects, including `CNF-7`, `CNF-26`, `CNF-40`, `CNF-69`, `CNF-70`, `CNF-82` with its ceremony line, `CNF-86`, `CNF-102` and `CNF-110`; a new blocking resume item with its stage row; and the Abandon cases the record lists.

  - Everything the record lists under "What stays intact" stays intact, including `ARC-22`'s "Nothing runs while the app is closed" and `OVR-3`'s "No credential is written to storage in cleartext". Loss of the phone's data is not modelled as a journaled end. The direction adds no hosted or off-device executor and enables no capability.

**Stop and report — unchosen points; choose none of them, and settle text-work points only inside their bounds:**

If one needs a new owner choice, a weakening the record does not list as accepted, a new authority, or a new record kind other than the End record, stop and report. They are every item in that record's "Left to the text work, for the next normative edit" list, each as the record words it.

The queue note says "The behavior is the same under either reading" and leaves the reading open. Do not choose either reading. If the clarification cannot be worded without fixing one, or the two readings differ in behavior, stop and report.

The T47 settlement states "The successor accepts its own applicable conduct modes, including a larger bound set if it binds one" as an existing boundary, and says of itself "They do not select either remaining owner policy". These records do not say they close that sub-question, or the same item's package-fetch and attest-reinstall sub-questions. Do not edit that item; stop and report it.

  - reuse of an acceptance for unchanged pending work, explicit retention at withdrawal, and expiry on cancellation or a refused send;

**Acceptance criteria:**

Its decisions also touch `STA-16`, the credential format, `ARC-25a`'s trigger and `SEC-14`'s restatement. Land tw-lq8's package after this one, or run the two as one implementer task. ## Owner decision — ambiguous legacy history becomes one conversion line, 2026-11-04

Scope: the legacy-history decision in the record on this bead titled "Owner decision — ambiguous legacy installation history, 2026-11-02" (comment 38000001), as the owner direction on this bead (comment 74000001) left it after removing the command filter. Five independent readings judged whether the system needs that decision. Three called it essential and two called for keeping it simplified. All three essential readings rested on the command filter, which no longer exists. The owner selected the simplification: "One line: all 'unknown'".

The rule, for the later text work: one line in the version-3 compatibility conversion of `docs/design/credential-format-v1.md`. A version-3 machine state lists "the labels of the acceptable weaker modes standing on the machine's bound set", so an unpinned-installation label there belongs to the set, not to a machine. When that label stands on a bound set of more than one machine, each machine of the set restores as history unknown. The unknown history is shown and restated at binding as `SEC-14` requires of installation history ("every later set that includes the machine is shown them at binding and restates them"). It never becomes unpinned history or clean history for any of them. When the set has one machine, the history belongs to that machine. This line converts only the set-level label: a machine's own recorded `installation` value keeps its existing meaning, and the existing rule stands that "absent required data never becomes empty history" (`CNF-84`).

Conformance: one or two `CNF-84` cases. A version-3 payload whose two-machine set carries the label, with both machines now recorded as pinned, restores both machines as history unknown, shows and restates it at the next binding of a set that includes either machine, and records neither as unpinned nor as clean history. The same label on a one-machine set restores as that machine's unpinned history.

Not added: no `STA-16` procedure for working out which machine the history came from, and no inference over old data beyond the line above. The brief's stop-and-report item on that procedure (comment 70000001) has nothing left to apply. The filter-only cases are dropped, as comment 74000001 already records. The queued, unselected proposal to resolve an unknown origin from a matching journal backup stays queued as it was.

Unchanged: the unanimously settled point that new exports keep each machine's actual unpinned-installation history separately from its current artifact status, standing modes and unused acceptance, under explicit versioning and compatibility rules, with its distinguishing cases for current pinned status after actual unpinned history and unused acceptance with no dispatched installation. Unchanged too: existing malformed-input and unsupported-version validation. This record does not touch the timing, independence-bound or successor-set decisions; their need review is recorded separately.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — successor-set membership becomes one line on the subset rule, 2026-11-04

Scope: "Owner decision — successor-set membership for the middle recovery rung, 2026-11-02" (comment 44000001). Five independent readings judged whether the system needs it. Three recommended keeping the operator's choice of peers: two as recorded, one simplified onto the existing subset rule. Two recommended a successor holding the stuck machine alone. The owner selected the choice, written short: "You pick, one line".

The rule, for the later text work: one line in `SEC-1`, at the escalation clause that "re-binds a half-provisioning machine to the successor session under `ARC-16`'s condition", tied to the existing subset rule "Once a predecessor has ended, a later session MAY re-enter any subset of its maintained machines; the machines it leaves out stay unbound until some session is bound to them." On escalation to a successor, the operator chooses which other eligible machines of the predecessor set join it, and the escalated stuck machine is always included. `ARC-16` points to that line. `CNF-7`'s existing subset case ("After a predecessor ends, a later session re-enters any subset of its maintained machines") names the stuck machine's inclusion. ADR-0037 and T47's "The recovery ladder's middle rung under a bound set of more than one" record the answer.

Not added: the five cases listed in comment 44000001 and the brief (comment 70000001) are not written out as their own rules or conformance cases. Their content stays with the rules that already own it, unrestated: the predecessor must have ended with its workers stopped and its channels closed before any new binding; excluded machines stay unbound; exposure is permanent for the life of the machine; resource holds and unresolved effects stay with each resource; the singleton rules for a declared independence bound and for a multi-tenant machine stand; and untyped-vendor exclusivity is unchanged.

Unchanged: the T47 technical settlement and the recovery acceptor settlement as existing boundaries, and the records in comments 77000001 and 78000001.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — the later acceptance window and the independence-bound permission are dropped, 2026-11-04

Scope: two decisions on this bead. The first is timing A in "Owner decision — no-pin acceptance after dedicated rescue inspection, 2026-11-02" (comment 38000001). The second is B in "Owner decision — unpinned installation under an independence bound, 2026-11-02" (comment 44000001). Five independent readings judged whether the system needs each of them, and three of the five recommended cutting each one. The owner selected "Drop both", as voted.

Timing A is withdrawn. The later text work adds no dedicated-path window for accepting an artifact-unpinned operating system after host-key-pinned rescue inspection. The current text stands: `ARC-25`'s "the operator chooses it up front, from what the bundle lacks" and `SEC-14`'s "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it". `ARC-25`'s "A machine that began under a pin and failed it MUST NOT continue unpinned, whoever asks." stands as well. An operator who decides on an unpinned operating system only after inspecting the rescue machine accepts it in a session that accepts it up front. The `SEC-14`, `ARC-25` and `CNF-93` edits that timing A asked for are not made. Other decisions that timing A restated, including prior C and fresh-reinstall A, stay as recorded in their own records. Where comment 44000001 says "Preserve timing A: acceptance can follow host-key-pinned dedicated rescue inspection" and "the selected dedicated rescue-inspection window remains", that window no longer exists; the rest of those lines stands.

Independence-bound B is withdrawn. The later text work makes no `ARC-25`, `SEC-14` or ADR-0035 edit for it. Withdrawing B by itself leaves the item "An unpinned installation under an independence bound" in `TASKS.md` T47 and ADR-0035's "whether an unpinned installation is admissible under a declared independence bound, which nothing here settles" as written, and adds no prohibition and no permission. Whether to forbid new unpinned installations under a declared bound is queued as its own owner question; comment 80000001 records the answer, and that record, not this one, closes the T47 item and the ADR-0035 sentence. The three readings that recommended the cut favored that refusal and said it needs its own decision. The two that recommended keeping a closure note held that the current text already allows the combination. The shared-source risk recorded with B stays recorded as a known risk; this record does not accept it.

For the brief (comment 70000001): its "Timing A" and "Independence bound B" items have nothing left to apply. In T47, the text work updates only the items that comments 79000001 and 80000001 answer.

Unchanged: the legacy-history decision as comment 77000001 records it, and the T47 technical settlement and the recovery acceptor settlement as existing boundaries.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — unpinned installation under an independence bound is allowed, 2026-11-04

Scope: the question that comment 78000001 queued after withdrawing B: whether a new unpinned installation is allowed on a machine under a declared independence bound. The owner selected "Allow, as on 11-02". The panel had voted on cutting B, not on a refusal. Three of its readings favored forbidding the combination, as all three readings had on 11-02. The other two held that the current text already allows it, partly because a set spread across vendors may need a distribution the bundle does not pin.

The decision: under a declared independence bound, a new unpinned installation is allowed with the ordinary up-front acceptance, under `ARC-25`'s "the operator chooses it up front, from what the bundle lacks" and `SEC-14`'s "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it". The bound alone adds no prohibition and no further acceptance. There is no later acceptance window (comment 78000001), and a failed pinned check still never falls back: "A machine that began under a pin and failed it MUST NOT continue unpinned, whoever asks."

Known risk, accepted by the owner: an unpinned artifact source can substitute bootstrap content and an unchecked package-signer set across several members together, despite distinct configured models, singleton sessions and compliant footprint counts. Separate ordinary acceptances do not constrain that shared source. Pinned paths still share publisher and package-signer dependencies, so this is an additional unchecked path, not a claim that pinning proves independence.

For the later text work: the decision closes the item "An unpinned installation under an independence bound" in `TASKS.md` T47, and the ADR-0035 sentence "whether an unpinned installation is admissible under a declared independence bound, which nothing here settles", with a dated amendment there that states the decision and the accepted risk. It adds no new mechanism: no rule edit, no warning ceremony, no extra accepting act, no build gate, no profile permission slot and no conformance case. If the text work finds a normative rule that refuses this combination, it stops and reports rather than editing that rule.

Not selected: a refusal of new unpinned installations under a bound, a per-profile permit or forbid policy, refusal unless a tenant opts in, and a bundle-build rejection.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Robot rescue rekey moves the installation id but leaves the root's label stale; its ordinal may be unknown
description:
## The gap

`STA-17` says "If the old seed or an index is missing, direct re-entry and pass revocation
cannot finish. Robot machines can still be rekeyed through vendor-authenticated rescue
(`STA-15`)". `STA-22b` says "With no sheet, or for machines missing from a stale sheet, Robot
recovery installs keys from a fresh seed through vendor-authenticated rescue and re-reads host
pins; it does not guess old indices".

On that path the machine takes an index under the fresh seed, so the shown installation id's
machine component moves (`STG-20`). Replace's relabel job covers a dedicated machine reached by
direct re-entry. It does not cover this path. A root rekeyed this way keeps a label that no
longer equals the shown id. The install brief recognises only a label equal to the shown id as
its own installation, so the next return to rescue on that machine reads the machine's own root
as a predecessor and can steer toward erasing it.

## What is open

- **The ordinal.** The label is `<machine>-<n>`. With no sheet, or a stale one, the journal may
  hold no installation for the machine: `CHN-R7` says a non-destructive recovery "does not open
  an installation", and the credential format says Replace's migration "does not restart at
  zero". Nothing defines `n` here. Either a rule supplies it (for example from a readable,
  well-formed old root label), or nothing is written and the machine stays unmigrated until it
  is known.
- **The order.** No connection authenticated by the old key exists on this path, but the rescue
  ceremony ends in the installed system, so a connection authenticated by the new key can still
  be confirmed before a relabel. Whether the relabel then runs in the installed system or from
  rescue, and when the machine counts as migrated, is open.
- **The job.** `ARC-43`'s job list has no rescue rekey job yet.

## When it must be settled

Dedicated path only (cloud machines are destroyed and recreated). It must be settled before a
dedicated-server path is offered to an operator, which no stage before the third does; it sits
beside `CNF-84`'s Robot rescue case in `07-conformance.md`'s dedicated row.
close_reason: Landed: the dedicated rescue rekey keeps a proposed installation ordinal, relabels after the new-key login and removes only an identified old key; a machine left with an unidentified key fails CNF-5 until a read shows it clean (STA-17, STA-16, STG-20, ARC-43, credential format v6, install brief, CNF-117, ADR-0056, ADR-0045 note). Open points filed as tw-4mz.

comments.text:
## Owner decision — rescue ordinal accepted as a proposal, 2026-11-02

Selected B: during authorized rescue recovery of the same physical maintained machine, with no admissible saved history and a unique disk label such as `a-7`, the operator may explicitly accept 7 as a proposed current installation ordinal after checks against surviving facts. Migration to the new machine index b then uses `b-7`. A disk label is never adopted automatically.

The accepted number is a proposal, never historical proof. Earlier installation history remains explicitly unknown. Every retained identity, ordinal, installation observation and pin fact must be preserved; acceptance cannot override a contradiction or convert a missing comparison into a passed comparison. Known history still carries forward. Reading or accepting a label does not itself open a destructive installation, establish prior pin provenance, authenticate root contents, identify an old client key, revoke access or complete Replace.

This is an amendment requiring a new authority record and a versioned partial-history representation. Keep old-version validation unchanged: do not fabricate earlier groups, observations, pins or empty-history placeholders to encode the proposed ordinal. The credential format states: "Missing or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history." The new representation must round-trip the proposal's basis and the missing past without silently converting either into ordinary recovered history. It does not authorize future operations whose required facts or comparisons remain unavailable.

Follow-up A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02: the durable ordinal acceptance survives a worker restart when the operator resumes the unchanged recorded migration, for the same machine, root and destination allocation. Restart alone does not require accepting the ordinal again. Existing operational checks and retry restrictions still apply. This does not revive a worker's runtime authority, authorize a different target or changed proposal, permit an automatic retry, or establish that any possibly sent write completed. Sheet-import authority and changed-state conflicts are not selected by this restart decision.

Keep the captured observation, the target-bound operator act, genuine retained facts and relabel confirmation distinct. A failed acceptance append supplies no acceptance. The compact export must carry its own interpretable basis and unknown-history meaning, preserving all genuine facts and old-version validation. A pointer to missing journal evidence is insufficient. The retained acceptance basis and export meaning below carry these clarifications.

Job-order A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02, is an amendment: write the root label and read it back only after the installed system accepts a login authenticated with the new client key. The bounded harness job runs in the installed system. In the stated first-write case, a failed new-key login leaves the original `a-7` untouched. Reading a pinned host answer or authenticating to rescue is not installed-system acceptance of the client key. Keep the relabel's captured readback distinct from installed access, old-key revocation and whole Replace completion.

All three independent readings recommended this order. The alternative of writing in rescue but confirming from the installed system after login was offered separately and was not selected. Safe relabelling and readback of the supported mounted root still need implementation evidence. Prior source/rehearsal descriptions do not establish that capability. If the selected placement cannot be implemented safely, report the obstacle rather than silently falling back to rescue or adding another reboot cycle.

Display timing is technically settled as a presentation clarification within the selected model-free recovery: show `b-7` as the proposed or pending destination after acceptance, and distinguish allocation `b`, observed disk text `a-7`, installed access and label confirmation. Confirmed label/current-ID status needs the captured installed-system readback following the selected new-key login. Once a write has been sent, the earlier observed `a-7` is only an as-of observation, not an assertion about the disk's current label. Computing an internal destination immediately supplies no additional authority. This introduces no new session-binding or dispatch condition. Label confirmation, terminal job evidence, hold release and revocation remain separate facts.

Changed-label A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02, is an amendment: if an admissible captured observation of the same recorded root reports a changed label, such as `a-9` after acceptance of proposed `7` from `a-7`, before the relabel write, stop this bounded migration unfinished and preserve the discrepancy. Issue no relabel intent or label write in response to that conflict. Retain the acceptance, both observations, allocation and all existing history/pin associations under `7`; adopt no `9` and invent no installation boundary. The earlier new-key installation is not silently undone. This refusal creates no command hold without a sent command, grants no erasure, and implies no cleanup or revocation success. It adds no mandatory pre-write probe.

Two independent readings recommended stopping; the other recommended keeping `7` and writing `b-7`, and also offered a separate new confirmation of the same `7`. The owner selected stopping. Neither continuation nor that extra-confirmation alternative is selected. Existing unchanged-restart acceptance and no-auto-retry rules remain; preserving the captured discrepancy through restart must not silently normalize it into success.

Old-key A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02, is an amendment: authorize the model-free rescue recovery flow to remove only the exact old client public key x independently identified by checked retained machine records for the same authorized machine. Removal follows successful installed-system login with the new key and the confirmed `b-7` readback. Preserve the new key and unrelated authorizations. Missing old private material is distinct from missing admissible old public identity; no impossible old-private-key login test is reported passed.

Unknown keys stay untouched and revocation is reported incomplete. Unknown public identity supplies no deletion target, no whole-file replacement and no new command hold. A removal from one named authorization source supports only that scoped effect, never whole-machine cleanup, termination of already accepted sessions, removal of persistence or application-secret rotation. Actual command/resource/destructive holds, durable intent, captured evidence and no-auto-retry rules remain. The stopped changed-label branch does not proceed to old-key removal.

All three independent readings selected exact identified-key removal; two explicitly classified rescue-path authorization as an amendment. Alternatives of replacing the whole key file, operator-selected deletion of an otherwise unidentified key, and admitting a seedless sheet for identification remain separately queued and unchosen.

Later old-sheet conflicts and any actual ordinary-session handoff during partial sheetless recovery remain queued. Installation acceptance and history decisions are recorded separately on tw-l1l; distinct T47 edges remain queued. Exact partial-history comparison/admission cases and formal coverage must be resolved without assuming lost history is empty or weakening a property. This record does not select those remaining policies. Keep the bead needing triage until the actual frontier is resolved and a bounded brief is ready.

Preserve the other settled boundaries: no universal installation-target approval or new reset gate; sheetless recovery grants no new destructive authority; current holds, pin checks, journal-before-send, no automatic retry, capability admission and completion truth remain. No theorem, requirement, assumption boundary, import refusal or control may be weakened to accommodate the amendment. Relevant normative owners are STA-17, STG-20, STA-16 and the credential format; the decision rationale belongs with ADR-0045. A later implementation changes the single normative owners together, then records the amendment.

The accepted observation and root provenance, target-bound operator act, genuine retained facts, relabel intent/result and captured confirmation remain separate linked facts. The compact versioned export carries an interpretable acceptance basis itself; a pointer to unavailable journal evidence is insufficient. No label component establishes an old seed-derived identity. A proposed base ordinal of 7 does not increment during non-destructive recovery; a later separately approved and otherwise admissible destructive reinstall derives 8 at its existing dispatch boundary while retaining the unknown past. This arithmetic waives no admission, pin, hold, retry, completion, capability or label-size guard.

## Source quotations — current text to preserve or amend

These are quotations of the current source, not claims that the selected amendments have already landed. The selected changes and the queued limits remain as recorded above.

`STA-17` (03-state-and-recovery.md:1143):

> Replace's machine-migration MUST move the machine component to the machine's new index and
> carry its installation ordinal `n` with it (`STG-20`).

`STG-20` (06-first-stage.md:643):

> `n` is the journal's installation ordinal in decimal without leading zeros, starting at zero
> per machine. It is derived from the journal with no new journal field, unchanged across restart
> and Restore.

`STG-20` (06-first-stage.md:553):

> That separately approved destructive reinstall
> opens a new installation when it is **dispatched**: the reset into rescue on a dedicated server,
> or the vendor's reinstall call at LNVPS. Choosing it or recording its disposition does not move
> that boundary. At dispatch the old installed-system pin retires and the new `ready_to_reset` job
> read can establish its pin before the reset into the installed system. Any other rescue reset,
> reboot, restart, Restore or non-destructive key recovery does not open that boundary.

`credential format v1` (docs/design/credential-format-v1.md:225):

> Missing
> or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history. `STA-16` owns what Restore does with
> these facts. These fields remain required in the version-4 payload and in the version-3
> compatibility input; the envelope and derivation are unchanged.

`ARC-43` (01-architecture.md:306):

> - `replace_root_label` — a harness-initiated rewrite of a dedicated machine's root label
>   during Replace's model-free direct re-entry migration, outside any session. The model
>   MUST NOT request it through `request_harness_job` or supply its command. Its rules are
>   `STA-17`'s.

comments.text:
## Owner decision — later reinstall admission over an accepted-but-incomplete history, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route with no admissible saved history, whose installation number was accepted as a proposal under the recorded decision B (for example, 7, with installations 0 to 6 unknown). Later, a separately authorized destructive reinstall opens the next installation, and its `ready_to_reset` pin comes up for admission.

Selected admission A, as an amendment: the admission compares the pin against every fact the harness retains, from the accepted installation onward. Any known overlap refuses, as now. The earlier history is shown plainly as unknown, and that comparison is never reported, displayed or exported as passed. The guard does not refuse merely because the earlier facts are unavailable.

This amends the scope of `STG-20`'s "MUST share no fingerprint with any observation or installed-system pin of that machine in any earlier installation" for this case only. For installations below the accepted base, the check covers what is retained rather than what happened. It is a relaxation, and the owner accepts it: the cost is that a stale key from the unknown installations would go undetected. `STG-20`'s backstop is already "vacuous for a predecessor that never reached `ready_to_reset` and left no matching observation", but losing a record does not prove that case, so this decision is needed.

This later owner choice sets aside two limits of the recorded decision B on this bead, for this one `STG-20` earlier-installation check on the dedicated Robot recovery path only. Decision B says "Exact partial-history comparison/admission cases and formal coverage must be resolved without assuming lost history is empty or weakening a property." and "No theorem, requirement, assumption boundary, import refusal or control may be weakened to accommodate the amendment." Everything else in decision B stands, and lost history is still never assumed empty.

Decision B also says "It does not authorize future operations whose required facts or comparisons remain unavailable." That sentence is not set aside, and it does not bar this admission. In decision B's paragraph, "It" is the versioned partial-history representation, which "must round-trip the proposal's basis and the missing past". The sentence says that this representation supplies no authority: it withholds authority rather than forbidding an operation. The authority for this admission is this owner decision. Under this decision's amended `STG-20` scope, the comparison this admission requires is the one over the retained facts, so no required comparison is unavailable.

Limits:
- Only the dedicated Robot recovery path that decision B covers. No generalized admission route follows.
- At LNVPS, `STG-21a`'s publication-based reinstall confirmation still "requires a complete nonempty publication durably recorded for the immediately preceding installation before dispatch", and `CHN-R7` admission is unchanged.
- Unknown history never becomes empty history, and every retained check, hold and no-retry rule stays.

Not selected:
- Admission B, refusing the admission whenever the required comparison includes unavailable history. That would leave the machine with no reset into the installed system after any later destructive reinstall, so its only exits would be abandonment or staying in rescue.
- Reading admission A as no relaxation, on the view that `STG-20` already covers only the history that was kept.

The independent readings split two to one. Two favored admission A; the third favored admission B and reads admission A as a relaxation of `STG-20`, which the owner accepted.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Technical common fact — genuine history below the accepted base is kept, 2026-11-03

Scope: the recorded decision B on this bead. A machine is recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route with no admissible saved history, and the operator accepts a proposed installation number, for example 7. Some genuine facts below 7 survive and are admissible under the existing rules, such as an observation known to belong to installation 4 or a retired installed pin from installation 5.

Three independent readings agree on these facts, and none calls them a new policy or an amendment:

- Each such fact is preserved in decision B's versioned partial-history representation, and the gaps around it are shown explicitly as unknown. Dropping the facts is not open: decision B says "Every retained identity, ordinal, installation observation and pin fact must be preserved". Filling the gaps is not open either: the credential format says "Missing or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history".
- `STA-16`'s Restore rule points the same way for recorded facts: it "MUST retain every recorded installation boundary, its publication observations, and each installed pin's active or retired status".
- The later-admission decision on this bead compares a later `ready_to_reset` pin against every fact the harness retains. Its phrase "from the accepted installation onward" is not a lower bound: retained facts below the accepted base join that comparison too. That makes the check stricter, never weaker, and any known overlap still refuses.
- The credential format's validation of its older versions is unchanged, including its refusal of a "duplicate or skipped installation ordinal". How the partial-history form encodes its gaps is left to the text work under decision B, and no field names are chosen here. One reading calls that encoding a technical omission owned by the credential format, coordinated with its recovery semantics.

This adds nothing beyond decision B and the later-admission decision. How decision B's "no admissible saved history" trigger applies where admissible facts reach only an earlier installation stays queued for the text work. So does whether the only partial shape admissible today is known history from the first installation onward, then a gap, then the accepted base. A single reading raised each point, and neither changes these facts.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Technical common fact — the ordinary session after a partial sheetless recovery, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered under decision B on this bead, with an accepted installation number and earlier history explicitly unknown, is handed to an ordinary session.

Three independent readings agree on these facts, and none calls them a new policy or an amendment:

- The route is `SEC-1`'s re-entry, which binds "on a maintained machine only". `SEC-1` says "Binding is an operator act in the browser, made before any channel access to that machine."
- `STA-13`'s conservative binding, under which "re-entry then binds only a configured model not currently assigned to any other machine", restricts no current tenant. `STA-11` says the ledger's staleness rules "bind only a tenant that is both maintained and threshold-bearing, and none currently is".
- Known exposure is counted. Unknown past exposure is shown as unknown, never as zero.
- The session may rely on an independently admitted active pin, and on the accepted installation number as a proposal with its recorded basis.
- The session may not rely on prior provenance, retired pins, the unknown history, zero exposure, complete revocation or a passed comparison over the unknown installations. Every ordinary check still applies. Whether `ARC-25a`'s command filter is one of them for this machine is an open owner question, below.

Single readings raised further points. Each stays queued and unchosen, and none changes these facts.

Two open owner questions, neither answered here:
- Whether `ARC-25a`'s command filter applies to a machine whose earlier history is unknown under decision B. The filter applies "For every box-plane command targeting a machine with durable unpinned-installation history", and this record does not decide whether unknown history counts as such history.
- Which machine id a bound session sees before the operator confirms the machine's label, and whether an ordinary session may bind before that confirmation.

Four points for the text work:
- Which text supplies the duty to show unknown past exposure as unknown on this route: decision B on this bead with `SEC-1`, or `STA-13`.
- Whether the rescue flow must be named in `SEC-1`, which says "Two harness flows hold a client key outside any session", and in `SEC-5` row 1, or folded into Replace.
- Whether the credential format's per-machine `installation` field, which takes `"pinned"`, `"unpinned"` or `"not_installed"`, needs an explicit unknown value.
- Whether this route needs a pointer to `STA-16`'s unchecked rule, which is worded for a sheet: "The sheet carries no check result and no finding".

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a valid late sheet enriches the live partial history, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route under the recorded decision B, whose proposed installation number was accepted (for example, 7, with earlier history unknown). Later, the operator supplies an old recovery sheet for this machine that is admissible under the existing import rules. Today no act joins a sheet's history to a store that already holds the machine.

Selected: checked, evidence-only enrichment, as an amendment. The sheet's compatible facts join the live partial history; any contradiction refuses the enrichment.

Checked means:
- The sheet passes the existing import validation under its own seed: `STA-22b`'s "Import checks the seed identifier, derives each listed public key and compares it", and the credential format's checks, are unchanged. A sheet that fails them stays outside the store, even if it would fill a gap.
- The physical machine is established by seed identifier, vendor machine id and vendor reconciliation, never by label text. Decision B already says "No label component establishes an old seed-derived identity". A different seed lineage is validated under its own seed, and its link to this machine is established separately.
- Every sheet fact is compared with every fact the harness retains before any of it joins.

Evidence-only means:
- The joined facts keep their own provenance and stay "knowledge as of export", as `STA-16` says of a restored sheet. A sheet whose last group is 5 is not a claim that the machine is at 5 today: nothing rolls back, installation 6 stays unknown, and the accepted 7 stays a proposal.
- They join every later admission comparison, as the later-admission decision on this bead and the common fact on genuine history below the accepted base already require for retained facts. A later pin that repeats a fingerprint recovered from the sheet refuses.
- They grant no binding, pin activation, contact, allocation, key removal or relabel authority. The credential format's "imported data never creates a binding without vendor reconciliation and an operator act" stands, and so does `CHN-R7`'s "Without a reinstall, no installed-system pin from any source replaces an active pin".
- The enriched history never becomes proof that it is complete or current. Gaps the sheet does not cover stay unknown, and the credential format's "Never merge two counters and call the result proof that a backup is current" applies.

Any contradiction refuses: if a sheet fact conflicts with the retained history (for example, an installation above the accepted 7 recorded before that acceptance, a second installed pin in one group, or a fingerprint that the retained history places in a different installation), the enrichment is refused. The owner selected that compatible facts join and that any contradiction refuses. This record reads the refusal as covering the whole sheet, so none of its facts join, not only the conflicting ones. The later decisions on a refused sheet were put to the owner on that reading, and the owner did not challenge it, but the owner has not confirmed it explicitly. Nothing in the live history is overwritten, renumbered or reported as passed, and decision B's "acceptance cannot override a contradiction" holds. What the conflict then means for the recovery, and for a pin admitted before it surfaced, is a separate question that stays open.

This amends `STA-16`, which gains a late-evidence act next to Restore; the credential format owns its representation. No field names are chosen here.

Not selected: no new act, which is simplest. The sheet would stay outside this store, and later comparisons could not use facts the harness had a way to know: a reinstall presenting a fingerprint the sheet records in installation 5 would be admitted with that history shown as unknown.

All three independent readings favored enrichment. Two read it as a new policy needing an amendment, and the third as a technical omission owned by `STA-16`. The owner records it as an amendment.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a late sheet that contradicts the accepted installation number, 2026-11-03

Scope: the late-sheet case on this bead. The installation number was accepted as a proposal under the recorded decision B (for example, 7), and later the operator supplies an old recovery sheet that passes the existing import checks but contradicts that number: for example, it proves installation 9 existed before 7 was accepted. Under the late-sheet enrichment record's reading of its refusal, the whole sheet is refused, so none of its facts join the live history. This record decides what the conflict then means for the recovery.

Selected K, as an amendment:
- Before the relabel write, the migration stops as the changed-label A decision already says: "stop this bounded migration unfinished and preserve the discrepancy". No relabel intent or label write is issued, the acceptance and every existing association stay under 7, and the recovery adopts no 9 and must "invent no installation boundary".
- After the write (for example, a confirmed `b-7`), the machine keeps 7. The conflict is recorded durably beside the history, never as installation facts in it, and it is shown before each irreversible step on this machine. Showing it adds no refusal of its own: every existing check, hold and no-retry rule still applies.
- The next destructive reinstall opens installation 8 and writes `b-8`. Nothing renumbers the history automatically, and no repair step is added.
- The accepted 7 stays a proposal, and the conflict is never reported as resolved or as a passed comparison. Decision B's "acceptance cannot override a contradiction" holds: the conflict stays recorded and shown and is never cleared by the acceptance.

Because the sheet's groups stay apart, the live history keeps one sequence, and the credential format's refusal of a "duplicate or skipped installation ordinal" is unchanged.

Accepted cost: the refused sheet's fingerprints do not join the history, so a later reinstall cannot be checked against them. That earlier history is shown as unknown under the later-admission decision on this bead, and that comparison is never reported as passed.

Not selected:
- Stop: halt every step that depends on history, such as the label write and later reinstalls, keeping the conflict on record with no repair. Without a repair step, this could leave the machine with no reinstall route short of abandonment.
- Repair: a new operator step that renumbers the history with evidence, for example to `b-9` and then `b-10`.

Two independent readings recommended stopping; the third recommended K and called it simplest. One of the readings that recommended stopping called stopping the simplest. None recommended repair, and none wanted automatic renumbering. Two read the effect of a late contradiction on a completed recovery as a new policy; the third said that the treatment of a newly found contradiction needs an owner decision.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a refused late sheet that overlaps the admitted pin, 2026-11-03

Scope: the late-sheet case on this bead. A machine recovered under the recorded decision B has an installed-system pin that was admitted under the existing rules, for example pin P for installation 8. Later, the operator supplies an old recovery sheet that passes the existing import checks and records the same fingerprint P in an earlier installation, such as 4. The retained history places P in a different installation, so under the late-sheet enrichment decision this is a contradiction, and under that record's reading of its refusal the whole sheet is refused.

Selected: keep the admitted pin and warn, as an amendment.
- The admitted pin stays in use. Nothing retires or replaces it automatically, consistent with `CHN-R7`'s "Without a reinstall, no installed-system pin from any source replaces an active pin".
- The overlap is recorded durably beside the history, never as installation facts in it, and it is shown before each irreversible step on this machine, as the selected keep-and-record decision K for a contradicted installation number does. Showing it adds no refusal of its own: every existing check, hold and no-retry rule still applies.
- The overlap is never reported as resolved, and no comparison it touches is reported as passed. Decision B's "acceptance cannot override a contradiction" holds.
- A later destructive reinstall still opens a new installation with a new pin under the existing admission rules, which ends this pin's use in the ordinary way.

The credential format already says, within one installation, that later refused observations "MUST NOT invalidate an already admitted pin". This decision gives a refused late sheet the same effect on a pin it challenges across installations. It does not change that rule or the format's validation.

Accepted cost: contact continues on a pin whose freshness against earlier installations is now challenged. Because the refused sheet's facts do not join the history, later admission checks cannot use them either.

Not selected: suspend contact that relies on the pin until the conflict is reconciled. No step reconciles the overlap: none is defined, and decision K on this bead did not select repair. Suspension would therefore last until a destructive reinstall gave the machine a new pin or the machine was abandoned.

Two independent readings recommended keeping the pin, and the third recommended suspending contact. All three called keeping it the simplest.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.
