title: CNF-109's admission from the job-read and attest routes at stage 1, which has neither
description:
## The question

`CNF-109` is in the stage-1 required row ("109–110") with no carve-out. Two of its sentences need
a route stage 1 does not have: a new job-read pin needs the dedicated path's rescue job, and a new
attest pin needs the attest route:

- "a new valid published, job-read, or unused eligible attest introduction can pin under its own
  rules"
- "A consumed attest introduction stays consumed."

Stage 1 has no attest route: the row says items 18 and 61 "remain route-specific attest checks,
required before enabling that route, not stage-1 requirements". A stage-1 harness can hold an
attest pin as history (Restore round-trips "an initial empty group opened by a job read or attest"
and "the active or retired status of pins from each source", `CNF-84`), so the history cases of
`CNF-109` are owed at stage 1. Proving that a consumed introduction "stays consumed" needs a later
attest attempt, which only the attest route can make.

Decided 2026-10-15 (owner): item 109's admission of a new job-read pin is the dedicated row's;
its admission of an unused attest introduction, and a consumed introduction staying consumed, are
the attest row's, as item 23's attest-window case already is. Stage 1 keeps the cases against
earlier job-read and attest pins, on pins a Restore brings in.

The implementation's companion comparison of `pins-witnesses-v4.json` leaves the 16 witnesses
holding an `attest` step (and 2246 enumerated traces) unreplayed at stage 1 until this is
answered, and its stage-1 admission record lists them by name as pending.

## Done when

The stage-1 row, or `CNF-109`, says where these two sentences apply, on the spec's main.
close_reason: Applicability rows now assign each route-specific case to its route, retaining restored history at stage 1.

title: LNVPS operations have no confirmation predicate (restart, stop, renewal-off, reinstall, deletion)
description:
## The gap

`STA-24`: "Evidence is the observation the operation's own reconciliation contract admits — for
Robot, `STG-4`'s predicates". `STG-4` and the rules after it define those predicates for Robot only.
No requirement defines the observation that confirms any LNVPS operation: the typed restart, the stop
that stands in for a destroy, renewal-off, or the vendor's reinstall call.

So at LNVPS each of those calls stays unresolved until the operator disposes of it, and while one
that changes what the machine is running (`STA-24`) is unresolved, box-plane dispatch to the
machine stays stopped. Duties resting on the missing contract:
- `ARC-43`: the opted-in delivery restart, "with its own vendor confirmation under `STA-24`";
  "Until that confirmation, box-plane dispatch stays stopped." (the boot-identity read is never
  the restart's confirmation).
- `STA-24`: "At LNVPS renewal-off waits for the stop's confirmation".
- `STA-24`: the reinstall continuation at LNVPS is dispatched at "the vendor's reinstall call";
  its confirmation closes the restriction's successor barrier.
- The implementation's LNVPS tickets (stop and renewal-off; reinstall, "confirmed only by the
  predicate the spec pin carries").

## The question

For each of the four operations, what observation — from LNVPS's machine status read
(`GET /api/v1/vm/{id}`, `VmStatus`), its published host keys, or a box-plane read where `STA-24`
allows one — confirms it, what is merely "ended", and what leaves it unresolved? Ground it in the
2026-10-08 LNVPS research and the 2026-10-11 phase B observations.

Found by the 2026-10-16 contradiction pass over branch docs/grill-1015.

The vendor's deletion of a stopped machine needs a confirming observation beside those of the four harness operations. `SEC-5` rows 12 and 23 count it as the machine's destruction at LNVPS: "the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop that stands in for a destroy"; that deletion observation is owed here too. The starting fact in `docs/findings/2026-10-11-lnvps-phase-b.md` is "A stop (`PATCH …/stop`) left the machine `stopped` and still listed, with `deleting_on` one day after the expiry (the grace may lengthen with the subscription's age; it was read at day 0)." No deletion has been observed. The observation has to work for a machine whose vendor key went with a retired or missing seed (`STA-17`); without one, that machine's placed secrets stay listed for good.
close_reason: T50 specified in STA-5, STA-24, STG-21/STG-21a and CNF-112: narrow exact-call receipts, unique-match order reconciliation, renewal/reinstall/deletion reads and account verification/reissue. ADR-0042 and TRU-E1 record accepted administrative-transfer risk and the deferred reappearance billing-display gap. Lost-key duties remain; no operator-carried evidence path. Specification closure only; no live deletion or implementation claim.

title: Does a destructive disposition stop a box-plane job the harness starts on its own?
description:
## The question

While a disposition naming a destructive reinstall or abandonment stands on a machine, is a
box-plane job the harness starts on its own (`delivery_reboot`, `digest_secret`, the delivery
check's harness-composed reads, `replace_root_label`) refused, or dispatched?

## What the text says

- `STA-24`: "the harness worker MUST refuse the model's box-plane commands to that machine,
  whatever the disposed call was. A harness-owned job the model requests (`ARC-43`) is one of
  them". Harness-initiated jobs are not named.
- `STA-24`: "a disposed box-plane command restricts only what an unresolved box-plane command
  bars", and "Box-plane dispatch to the machine is governed by `STA-20` and `STA-20b`, not by
  this rule". `STA-20`'s hold (2026-10-18, ADR-0048) is released by any disposition, so it is
  not part of a disposition's reach.
- `STA-24`: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane".
- ADR-0044 rejected "A destructive continuation adds nothing beyond what the disposed call
  barred" because "A stray command would pre-empt the reinstall the operator chose".

`TauWeb.Dispatch` follows the text: under a standing destructive reinstall disposition of a
command, a `deliveryReboot` request is dispatched, stays unresolved, and its barrier refuses
the reinstall's rescue activation until its boot change is collected.

## Readings

- A: the destructive stop covers every box-plane job, harness-initiated ones included; only
  reads and the collection of job records pass.
- B: as written today; a harness-initiated job runs under a destructive continuation and can
  pre-empt the reinstall.

## Closes when

`STA-24` says which reading holds for harness-initiated jobs, and `TauWeb.Dispatch` agrees.
close_reason: STA-24 stops every box-plane job; ARC-43 paste at once; STA-17; CNF-95/CNF-110; TauWeb.Dispatch.stops; ADR-0050

title: Decide what ends a failed rotation attempt's new placement, and what a failed first placement does
description:
tw-38p (ADR-0063) records a rotation only when the act admits the rotation job's completed
root-only job record with a zero exit. Until then the new placement is listed, and its reference
required, from the record made before its bytes leave. This bead asks what ends that new placement
when the rotation is never recorded, and what a failed first placement does.

**What the text says.**
- `SEC-5`: "The record made before the bytes leave (`ARC-8`), a nonzero exit, a job that stays
  unresolved (`STA-8`) and a disposition (`STA-24`) record no rotation".
- `ARC-43`: "A rotation's new placement is listed from the record made before its bytes leave,
  whatever its job then does".
- The credential format writes a rotation's new placement only once `SEC-5` records the rotation,
  so a Restore ends a failed attempt's new placement.

**The gap.**
- After a nonzero exit, an unresolved job or a disposition, while the local store stays intact,
  the new placement stays listed and its reference required with no act that ends it. A later
  rotation attempt of P adds another.
- A first placement (no old placement) whose job exits nonzero, stays unresolved or is disposed:
  the text does not say whether it is listed, whether its reference is required, or whether the
  export writes it.

**Questions.**
1. What ends a failed rotation attempt's new placement, its listing and its required reference: a
   later recorded rotation, destruction, an operator act, or nothing?
2. What does a failed first placement do to its listing, its reference and the export?

Constraints that hold either way:
- `STA-4`: a call with an intent and no terminal record "may have been sent, never that it was not".
- `STA-24`: a disposition keeps the outcome unknown.
- The credential format's duplicate rule for records without a report at one machine, application
  name, secret name and path.
- No raw value, bare digest or scan key enters history or export.

Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.

title: Decide which machines a reported placement's pre-loss withholding reaches after a Restore
description:
tw-5qs and tw-e42 (ADR-0062) made a recorded operator report final and carried by the sheet. The
`reference_ended` mark (ADR-0060, tw-huu) covers a placement that ended without a report. The two
rules give the machines they reach differently.

**What the text says.**
- For a reported placement P, `SEC-5` says: "After local-store loss nothing restores P's ended
  reference: every job record from before the loss stays withheld for P".
- For the mark, `SEC-5` names its machines: it is set "of Q's machine while that machine stays live
  and of every live machine the exposure ledger records in a bound set with it (`STA-10`)".
- The reported rule names no machine. It does not say whether "withheld for P" reaches a job record
  on a peer in P's bound set, or on a peer of a machine that has since been destroyed.

**The risk.** One reader takes the reported rule to cover only P's own machine, and releases a
peer's pre-loss record that printed P's value. Another takes it to cover every machine. Neither can
point to a sentence.

**Question.** Which machines does a reported placement's pre-loss withholding reach after a Restore:
- the machines the mark would reach (P's machine and every live machine the exposure ledger records
  in a bound set with it);
- or every machine?

Whichever is chosen, add a `CNF-95` branch that checks it, including a peer of a destroyed machine.

Constraints that hold either way:
- "Unscanned bytes MUST be withheld" (`SEC-5`).
- A report never counts as a scan, and is final (ADR-0062).
- The mark's machine scope is not changed (ADR-0060).

Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.

Found by the 2026-10-15 grill (decision 5, tw-6ku).

comments.text:
## Owner decision — sheetless destructive recovery, 2026-11-02

Selected C: the operator acts at the vendor. Sheetless recovery adds no new destructive authority. For a machine that existing authorization cannot admit, the harness does not gain permission to stop, reinstall or destroy it from a listing, recovery-sheet mapping, newly introduced adoption card or a newly introduced recovery-evidence rule. A listing remains displayed and never relied on for destructive authorization.

The operator handles the old machine at the vendor where an actual route is available. The harness recreates only where its existing credentials, authority, allocation and approval rules permit. Report unavailable remedies honestly; do not promise that every vendor offers a manual destroy or that missing credentials can be recovered. At LNVPS, missing the old seed or allocation index can lose the vendor key, leaving the harness unable to stop, reinstall or confirm deletion. A manual referral alone establishes no deletion, billing cessation or cleared obligation.

Amend the unconditional Cloud destroys and recreates wording in STA-15/STA-22b to express these limits. Correct CNF-84's demand for a LNVPS stop without the vendor key so it agrees with STA-17's refusal and honest incomplete-recovery state. Update affected conformance applicability and checked references after the owner rules change; do not add a competing authorization home.

Existing authority stands unchanged, including SEC-4's abandonment exception for this setup's own create response or admissible key-tied evidence. The decision creates neither general listed-object adoption nor a new sheetless destructive-recovery flow. It does not enable pending bare-seed import, per-machine discovery or T44's coordinated format/recovery amendment. Required retained barriers, identity exclusions, host-pin rules, uncertain outcomes and exposure/billing displays remain in force.

Coordinate stage-1 acquisition with tw-ae7 C: abandonment and a separately started setup do not become an in-setup third rung or an extra order under this recovery decision. The separate dedicated rescue-rekey question remains tw-lq8; no new installation acceptance or reset gate is created under tw-l1l.

Required distinguishing cases: a listed machine without current destructive authority receives no harness destructive dispatch; another account machine is not adopted by selection; a missing LNVPS key yields an explicit unavailable stop/reinstall/deletion-confirmation path; an already authorized abandonment still works under its own proof and approval rules. External/manual action is not reported as confirmed destruction without the existing admitted evidence, and a fresh acquisition uses its own existing approvals.

This owner choice is settled. This record claims neither rule implementation nor completed recovery, and does not claim an unavailable vendor remedy exists.

## Source quotations — current text to preserve or amend

These are quotations of the current source, not claims that the selected amendments have already landed. The selected changes and the queued limits remain as recorded above.

`STA-15` (03-state-and-recovery.md:1012):

> Where a maintained cloud machine's pin is lost with no sheet anyway, the machine is destroyed
> and recreated, which re-runs its first contact and loses its state.

`STA-22b` (03-state-and-recovery.md:842):

> Cloud destroys and recreates (`STA-15`).

`CNF-84` (07-conformance.md:1516):

> Cloud with no
>       sheet exposes destroy/recreate, never an unpinned keyed-rescue login; at LNVPS `ARC-22`'s
>       forms apply instead — a stop with renewal off for the destroy, and for the recreate a
>       reinstall that is a new first contact.

`STA-17` (03-state-and-recovery.md:1135):

> At LNVPS a missing old seed or index
> also loses that machine's vendor key, so the harness can neither reinstall nor stop it; the
> machine remains shown as existing and billed.

`SEC-4` (04-security-model.md:197):

> What an adapter can list of
> the account is displayed and never relied on: a listing is the vendor's word at one moment, and
> the authorization at each dispatch is the enforcement.

`SEC-4` (04-security-model.md:206):

> **The abandonment flow is authorized outside any session.** It MUST act only on machines of
> the unfinished setup whose vendor machine id reached the approved entry through **this setup's
> own** create response, or through evidence tied to the seed-derived key. This authorization is
> checked at dispatch. A mapping imported from a recovery sheet is never enough by itself.

comments.text:
## Agent Brief — bounded specification amendment, sheetless cloud recovery adds no destructive authority

**Category:** bug. **Outcome:** land, in its normative homes, the owner decision already recorded on this bead. No further owner choice is needed for the scope below. Points the owner left unchosen stay unchosen: where the text work would have to choose one, stop and report it instead of choosing. The bead moves to ready-for-agent with this brief; the drain lane takes it after its current queue.

**Records this brief implements (sections on this bead, by title).** Each section's own text and limits govern. This brief summarizes them and widens none.

- "Owner decision — sheetless destructive recovery, 2026-11-02" (C), comment 34000001.

That record's "stage-1 acquisition" means the LNVPS setup flows under tw-ae7 C. Stages are removed (tw-o6r); read it without a stage.

**Current gap.** `STA-15` says "Where a maintained cloud machine's pin is lost with no sheet anyway, the machine is destroyed and recreated", and `STA-22b` says "Cloud destroys and recreates (`STA-15`)." That destroy names a machine the journal maps to no entry, and nothing authorizes it. `CNF-84` asks for an LNVPS stop with renewal off in that case ("at LNVPS `ARC-22`'s forms apply instead"), which contradicts `STA-17`: "At LNVPS a missing old seed or index also loses that machine's vendor key, so the harness can neither reinstall nor stop it; the machine remains shown as existing and billed."

**Desired behavior and owners:**

- **No new destructive authority**, at `STA-15` and `STA-22b`. For a machine that existing authorization cannot admit, the harness gains no permission to stop, reinstall or destroy it from a listing, a recovery-sheet mapping, a new adoption card or a new recovery-evidence rule. Replace the unconditional "destroyed and recreated" wording with these limits.
- **The operator acts at the vendor** where an actual route exists. The harness recreates only where its existing credentials, authority, allocation and approval rules permit. A fresh acquisition uses its own existing approvals.
- **Honest unavailable remedies.** Report what is unavailable. Do not promise that every vendor offers a manual destroy, or that a missing credential can be recovered. At LNVPS a missing old seed or allocation index can lose the vendor key. Then stop and reinstall are unavailable (`STA-17`), and so is deletion confirmation (comment 34000001). A manual referral alone proves no deletion, no billing stop and no cleared obligation.
- **`CNF-84`**: correct its LNVPS clause to agree with `STA-17`'s refusal and the honest incomplete-recovery state. Update the affected conformance applicability and checked references after the rule changes.
- **One authorization home.** Add no competing one. `SEC-4` stands as written, including "What an adapter can list of the account is displayed and never relied on" and the abandonment flow's authorization, with "A mapping imported from a recovery sheet is never enough by itself."
- **What stays in force:** retained barriers, identity exclusions, host-pin rules, uncertain outcomes, and the exposure and billing displays.

**Coordination.**

- tw-ae7 C governs every LNVPS setup until the in-setup replacement order is admitted (tw-ae7 comment 71000001). Abandonment and a separately started setup do not become an in-setup third rung or an extra order under this decision.
- tw-ae7's deletion check (comment 82000001) reads only under the machine's own recorded key. A machine whose key is lost gets no check, and the check is no adoption route.
- tw-lq8 owns the dedicated rescue rekey. This decision creates no installation acceptance or reset gate under tw-l1l.

**Stop and report — choose none of these:**

- Any wording that would grant destructive authority from a listing, a sheet mapping or selection, or create general listed-object adoption or a sheetless destructive-recovery flow.
- Any change to `SEC-4`'s abandonment exception or to `STA-17`'s refusal.
- Any edit that would weaken a theorem, gate, assumption boundary or requirement beyond what the decision qualifies. Stop and report the conflict.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each duty has one normative home, and the other places point to it. Every sentence asserting what another requirement says carries its quote, and the citation gate passes. Where a touched clause is formalized, change its Lean declaration and its prose together.
- The amendment lands with its ADR context, recording the readings not selected.
- Conformance cases, from comment 34000001's required list:
  - a listed machine without current destructive authority receives no harness destructive dispatch;
  - a machine of another account is not adopted by selecting it;
  - a missing LNVPS key yields an explicit unavailable stop, reinstall and deletion-confirmation path, with the machine shown as existing and billed;
  - an already authorized abandonment still works under its own proof and approval rules;
  - manual or external action is not reported as confirmed destruction without the existing admitted evidence;
  - a fresh acquisition uses its own existing approvals.
- Update the atlas pointers that cite tw-yhd (`docs/state-machine-atlas.md`, the restored-command and installation/recovery notes) to name the landed rule.
- Any new formal guard gets a positive trace and a discriminating refused/admitted guard-removal pair, and its mutation control fails exactly at the intended finding.
- Run the unpiped Nix check-all gate before and after, CI's offline unit suite and the full mutation controls, and record the actual exits. A document or witness pass enables nothing.

**Sequencing.** The drain lane's tw-l1l package and tw-ae7's brief both touch `SEC-4`, `ARC-22` and `STA-17`'s neighbourhood. Land after them, or rebase onto them.

**Out of scope:** pending bare-seed import; per-machine discovery; T44's coordinated format and recovery amendment; tw-lq8's rescue rekey; runtime code; admitting any capability.

This brief makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Implementation — sheetless cloud recovery adds no destructive authority

Landed the owner decision (comment 34000001) under the Agent Brief (comment 89000001).

- `STA-15` now holds the rule. Recovery adds no destructive authority: a listing, a sheet mapping, a selection, a new adoption card or a new recovery-evidence rule grants no stop, reinstall or destroy. The LNVPS paragraph says stop, reinstall and deletion confirmation are unavailable once the vendor key is lost, quoting `STA-17` and `STG-21a`.

- No formal declaration covers `STA-15`, so no Lean change and no new guard.

title: No check reads where the abandonment continuation is dispatched (TauWeb.Dispatch)
description:
## What is wrong

`STA-24` says of abandonment that the restriction ends at "that flow's operation naming the machine: the destroy, or the stop that stands in for it (`ARC-22`), whose own barrier then holds the box plane". `TauWeb.Dispatch.dispatchesContinuation` carries it as `.abandon, k => k == .destroy`, and no theorem reads that case: changed to `.abandon, _ => false`, `lake build` in `tools/formal` still succeeds (rehearsed on a scratch copy at `f801f0a`). Every other clause of the disposition rule has a decided theorem that fails when the clause is removed.

## Why it was left

`ARC-21` runs abandonment "never through a session", the module's `Request` is what a model sends, and the emitter labels every request a model request. A decided, tagged trace in which a destroy is dispatched under an abandonment disposition would put into `docs/design/dispatch-witnesses-v2.json` a model's destroy dispatched as the abandonment, which the Markdown does not say; `docs/design/witness-file-v1.md` states that the file holds no such trace.

## What done looks like

A check fails when the abandonment case of `dispatchesContinuation` is removed or widened, and the witness file still tells a comparing implementation nothing about a model's request for a destroy. Two routes were seen: carry who sends a request and label the abandonment flow's an operator act (ADR-0032's vocabulary has one), which changes the witness file's shape and so its schema version; or decide it by a theorem that is not a witness. The choice needs the maintainer.
close_reason: Implemented TauWeb.Dispatch.abandonment_ends_at_its_destroy_alone, with the controls formal: abandonment never ends at destroy and formal: abandonment also ends at reset. Each mutation fails exactly that theorem, while kinds_total stays green; no abandonment request trace was added.

title: Specify the harness route from LNVPS arch login to root
description:
The fresh LNVPS catalogue-image observation records a pinned SSH login as `arch`
(`docs/findings/2026-10-11-lnvps-phase-b.md`, observation 3). `OPN-24` tests that the
image accepts the operator's key on its default user. No requirement owns the route
from that login to root.

This blocks the root-only job-record setup in `STA-20` and T42's fixed reads:
`sshd -T` needs the root-only host keys, and the local-account check reads
`/etc/shadow`. The harness-composed delivery reads and the fresh-image checklist run
need a defined execution route too. The owner chose `arch` login and password-free sudo for each job on 2026-11-01.
The specification has not yet incorporated that decision; the executable amendment
brief and remaining verification obligations are recorded in this issue.

Resolve in the specification before the fresh-image checklist is treated as evidence:
name how root is obtained from the default user, what authorizes it, how credentials
are handled if needed, and what refusal means. Keep that route usable when the
checklist requires every password field to be locked or disabled; the selected sudo route
must remain usable after lockdown and reboot. Add conformance coverage for the chosen route and its
failure. Until then no assertion is made about the actual image's sudo policy or
whether it passes the checklist.
notes:
## Triage outcome — 2026-11-01

The owner chose A: subsequent LNVPS jobs log in as `arch` with the existing per-machine SSH key and obtain root through password-free sudo for each job. The route must keep working after lockdown and reboot. Direct root login and alternate-login fallback are excluded by that decision.

No further owner decision is needed for the bounded specification amendment. Startup accounting, the access mechanism and presentation need to be specified; the existing missing-record outcome, command hold and permission to collect are already settled. `STA-20` says "A missing record is unresolved, never proof of death." Sudo failure after dispatch and before a protected record exists stays unresolved, never a clean terminal refusal. No startup exception, new terminal evidence or formal command-hold change is necessary for the chosen route.

The startup contract must place non-interactive root acquisition and initial protected-directory/record creation within the journaled tracked launch. Collection uses the same route as the already-permitted read, not an ordinary exec or an untracked repair command. Preserve command identity and equality, file-redirected output, boot identity and command/runner liveness. A failure to read a reachable machine's protected record establishes neither liveness nor completion; show it promptly without releasing the hold or automatically repeating the payload.

The specification amendment brief in this issue's comments is the executable triage outcome. It includes command equality, placed-secret input through sudo, detached liveness, permitted privileged collection, reachable-but-unreadable records, later re-entry and model-free Replace. T42's fresh-image run and integrated conformance remain outstanding. This decision and review do not establish the actual image's sudo policy or checklist success.

comments.author: triage
comments.text:
## Specification amendment brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Specify the chosen LNVPS route from `arch` to root for every job and protected-record collection, preserving existing tracking and uncertainty rules.

**Current behavior:**
ADR-0051 records that "The route from LNVPS's default login user to root remains a separate open requirement; locking a password used by that route could break it." The recorded fresh-image observation establishes pinned login as `arch`, not password-free sudo or successful lockdown. The specification requires protected job records and root-dependent reads but does not state their access route.

**Desired behavior and settled decision:**
The owner chose A on 2026-11-01: subsequent LNVPS jobs log in as `arch` with the existing per-machine SSH key and switch to root through password-free, non-interactive sudo for each job. Protected-record collection uses the same access route. The route remains usable after password locking, lockdown and reboot, on fresh connections, during later re-entry and for model-free Replace. Decision A excludes direct root login and alternate-login fallback; this exclusion does not come from the credential inventory. No elevation password or interactive prompt is authorized.

A single journaled tracked launcher may acquire root, create the protected job directory and its own record, then start payload work. State its contract without introducing separately dispatched untracked setup. Initial setup, launch and collection must preserve command identity, byte comparison, boot identity, command/runner liveness and file-redirected output. Collection remains the existing permitted read, never arbitrary repair or ordinary `exec` under another label.

Startup and collection failure outcomes are already decided, not a fresh policy frontier. `STA-20` says "A missing record is unresolved, never proof of death." A dispatched sudo or setup attempt lacking its protected record stays unresolved and holds its machine; diagnostics alone do not settle it or authorize retry. Distinguish refusal before transmission, a finished protected record including nonzero exit, and unavailable collection. A reachable machine whose record cannot be read supplies no liveness or completion evidence; show the unavailable collection promptly and preserve uncertainty. Do not wait as though an unreadable record established a live command.

**Requirement owners:**
- The LNVPS-specific login and sudo route belongs to `STG-21`, with references wherever it is used; the generic checklist stays vendor-neutral.
- Generic launcher, directory/record creation and permitted collection belong to `STA-20`. Preserve `STA-20a`'s "Output MUST be captured by redirection to a file, never by reading a pipe the job holds open" and its generic POSIX requirements.
- `ARC-8` owns "Recording commits **per command**, before transmission." `STA-21` owns the sent/received comparison, demonstrated by `CNF-56`: "The command recorded by the machine matches the command the browser journal recorded before sending." Make the launcher/payload representation explicit without weakening that equality.
- `ARC-43` owns read evidence and verdicts: "a read refused or held before dispatch, or with no record, settles nothing". Root-route failure supplies no successful lockdown or delivery evidence.
- `STG-9` requires "at least one later session re-enters over the same pinned channel and re-runs the check". `STA-17` owns Replace's key installation, new-key confirmation, old-key removal and held-machine handling. Apply A to the `arch` account in that flow without changing its ordering or claiming an incomplete migration finished.
- `SEC-11` requires "An SSH session MUST check the host key against the stored fingerprint, and a key that does not match MUST halt the session." Root launch and collection provide no exception.
- `STA-20`'s input rule says "the job wrapper MUST NOT write that input to any file but the job's destination". Preserve placed-secret input through sudo, including relevant capture/logging behavior, and test it against existing secret-handling rules.
- `STG-21` says "Stage 1 still waits for the integrated conformance in `07-conformance.md`; a failure there blocks stage completion." Missing elevation leaves relevant checks/flows incomplete. Do not change `OPN-24`'s vendor target criteria by implication.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The normative route states A, its authorization and persistence, no password/prompt/alternate-login fallback, and protected collection through the same route. References do not duplicate the rule.
- [ ] Startup creates and uses the protected directory/record within the same tracked launch before ordinary payload work. Launch and collection preserve command comparison, recorded boot identity, detached liveness and file output; no untracked successful setup is introduced.
- [ ] Conformance distinguishes pre-transmission refusal, recorded nonzero exit, sudo/authorization/password/terminal/setup failure after dispatch with no record, disconnect around record creation, and unavailable collection. Missing or unreadable records never release the hold, create successful evidence or cause an automatic retry.
- [ ] Conformance exercises fresh privileged collection while dispatch is held, with no collection deadlock, no arbitrary command admitted as collection, and an immediate visible unavailable-collection result that settles nothing.
- [ ] Conformance exercises the selected route after locked/disabled password fields, lockdown, disconnect, reboot, later fresh-session re-entry and Replace key migration. Changed host keys halt before root work; other machines retain their existing independence.
- [ ] Conformance covers byte equality through the launcher, command/runner liveness through sudo, and placed-secret input without extra capture or consumption by a prompt. Retain relevant existing cases, including `CNF-16`, `CNF-20`, `CNF-40`, `CNF-55`, `CNF-56` and `CNF-108`; any new item acquires its applicable stage row and required tier metadata.
- [ ] Land the normative rule before recording its rationale. Update ADR-0051's now-open-route statement and record the choice and rejected alternatives without writing a second normative copy.
- [ ] Run the repository's required gates before and after the amendment. Leave T42's fresh-image run and integrated evidence explicitly outstanding until demonstrated; a green specification gate is not a live-image result.

**Boundaries and readiness:**
This issue is ready for the bounded specification amendment, not closed and not evidence that the image or integrated harness passes. No new startup exception, terminal evidence, dispatch kind or Lean command-hold change is needed for A. Do not weaken the missing-record rule, hold, theorem, gate or assumption boundary; any later proposal changing those semantics requires separate review. Harness implementation, live vendor/machine operations, vendor selection changes and tw-ub7's restored unjournaled-command policy are outside this amendment.

title: Does a reinstall end a placement's required reference?
description:
Does a reinstall end a placement's required reference?

`SEC-5` row 23 gives the reference's lifetime as "Until rotation, machine destruction or
local-store loss; re-arm replaces it with a fresh key/reference". `ARC-43` lists the placed
secret in the trust display "until it is rotated or the machine is destroyed".

A wipe and reinstall is neither rotation nor machine destruction. Under the present text,
after a reinstall the machine's references stay required, and the bound set's output waits
on a paste or a rotation. Decide whether a reinstall should end the required reference,
and amend its owning lifetime and display rules together if so. This question is not fixed
by the destructive-stop and immediate-paste amendment.
close_reason: No. A reinstall alone ends neither a placement's required reference nor its listing; rotation is the way on only once `ARC-17`'s placement gates admit it, and the operator's revoked-at-service act is tw-i55.

title: Does an outstanding rescue activation hold the delivery reboot?
description:
`STA-24` says "An unresolved activation or key registration touches no running system and blocks nothing on the box." ADR-0048 follows it for the delivery reboot: "The delivery reboot is box-plane work, held by `STA-20`; it can be issued beside an unresolved activation."

On a vendor with rescue activation, an activation that has not yet been consumed by a reset makes the next boot a rescue boot. A `delivery_reboot` issued then boots the machine into rescue; `ARC-43` settles the call by its boot change, and the delivery check runs against the rescue system, without `STA-20b`'s planned-reset prerequisites or a reset intent. A model `exec` of a reboot has the same exposure.

Decide whether an outstanding rescue activation holds a reboot on the box, or whether the delivery reboot's settlement or the delivery check must refuse a rescue boot. The dedicated path is not offered before stage 3.
close_reason: Coverage, not new behavior. The premise was wrong: a delivery check does not run against an ordinary rescue boot. Rescue's different host key fails the installed pin at the handshake (SEC-11, CHN-R1), the halt ends the attempt with no reconnect (ARC-41), and no collection, settlement or verdict follows (STA-20). CNF-53's dedicated path now exercises that rescue-return halt beside a paired installed return, including the exec case; ARC-43 points at ARC-41's halt; the atlas moves tw-z99 to coverage. Reboot admission, settlement and recovery are unchanged, the different-key construction does not attest the remote root, and live Robot and integrated browser evidence are still owed.

comments.text:
## Agent Brief — rescue reboot composition coverage

Category: bug (incorrect premise and missing conformance coverage). Triage outcome: ready for an agent; no owner policy choice remains after unanimous technical review.

Summary: correct the rescue-delivery premise and exercise the existing installed-pin halt before reboot collection or delivery verification. Preserve current reboot admission, result and recovery behavior.

Current contract: a retained rescue activation can coexist with otherwise eligible box-plane work. If an ordinary vendor-configured rescue boot presents its distinct server key, reconnect under the active installed pin halts before authenticated collection. No collection bypasses that pin check. No new delivery verdict may be fabricated. The ordinary different-key construction does not attest the remote root or defeat a malicious vendor; integrated evidence remains outstanding.

Desired change: re-scope tw-z99 as conformance coverage, and extend the dedicated-path CNF-53 case to compose CHN-R1/SEC-11/ARC-41 pin admission with STA-20 collection/hold and ARC-43 reboot-result/pending-check duties. Reference the owners through checked quotations rather than duplicate a rule. Add only an informational owner pointer where one is needed for the halt ending a reconnect attempt.

Acceptance criteria:
- Correct the claim that a delivery check necessarily runs against ordinary rescue. Distinguish an admitted reboot that enters rescue from an admitted installed-pin connection or a settled reboot.
- In the dedicated rescue-return trace, the installed-pin handshake refuses the different rescue key before record collection; there is no fallback pin, automatic reconnect after halt, new result or delivery verdict. Retained command/resource/pending-check restrictions keep their existing effects. Stopping the pending check is shown as stopped and settles neither the reboot nor activation.
- Pair that refusal with an installed-return positive case: eligible installed pin, genuine matching own-command record collected on a different boot, durable settlement, and required service/lockdown reads before a verdict. A possibly ineffective unresolved activation may remain independently unresolved; it is not settled by the reboot.
- Preserve the distinction between existing-record collection and a newly dispatched read job. Preserve ordinary exec settlement by a genuine terminal record; if none was established before the rescue pin halt, a boot change alone cannot settle it.
- Preserve existing wrong-call/machine, same-boot, missing-record/boot and failed-append refusals, and the dedicated reinstall/activation/withdrawal boundaries. A surviving record on installed disk does not override a refused channel; do not rely on universal record absence in rescue.
- Keep journal-only recovery and all independently retained restrictions. Do not add a recovery enumeration or wait for omitted activations.
- Keep stage applicability: dedicated delivery_reboot composition belongs to the dedicated path, not stage-1 LNVPS typed restart. State the live Robot OS-reboot activation/key-publication behavior and integrated browser pin/collection/verdict evidence still owed; synthetic source traces supply none of it.
- Run the repository's unpiped specification gates and exact CI checks. Demonstrate the conformance refusal/positive expectations in downstream evidence before dedicated admission. Add no new semantic engine merely to check prose.

Out of scope: activation-based all-job or selective reboot holds; a new installed-system evidence predicate; a new operator warning duty; altered boot-change settlement; accepting a rescue pin as installed; optional extra fingerprint exclusions; changing any capability, formal guard, theorem, witness schema, or previously selected owner decision. Optional hardening requires its own request and must not be folded into this task.

The coverage amendment belongs to its conformance owner; current normative behavior remains at CHN-R1, SEC-11, ARC-41, STA-20/STA-24 and ARC-43. No implementation completion or runtime proof is claimed.
